runners.comment: Only 11th in 6f Pontefract handicap 18 days ago; she needs to bounce back

runners.owner: Hot To Trot Racing 2 & J Fill
runners.comment: Sister to Group 1 winner Dreamloper; Lope De Vega filly rates an interesting debutante
runners.spotlight: Sister to 7f-1m1f winner Dreamloper (Group 1; RPR 121) and a half-sister to four other winners, notably Santorini Star (1m-2m Group 2; RPR 113); dam 1m2f-1m4f winner (Listed; RPR 99); this daughter of Lope De Vega makes a lot of appeal on paper and rates an interesting debutante.

runners.comment: Never dangerous in Newcastle maiden and Pontefract novice; can do better in due course
runners.spotlight: Never dangerous in 7f Newcastle maiden and 6f Pontefract novice this spring; this Territories filly can do better in the longer term.

runners.comment: Always behind when eighth in Kempton novice on her debut in February; lots more is needed
runners.spotlight: 80-1, always behind when eighth of 12 in 7f Kempton novice on her debut in February; needs to take a big step forward.

runners.comment: Very promising debut fifth at Carlisle in September; capable of a lot better and a player
runners.spotlight: 7-2 and green, shaped with plenty of promise when a debut fifth of ten in novice at Carlisle (6f, good) in September, finishing well after a very slow start; this daughter of Havana Grey was a 500,000euros buy at the breeze-ups as a juvenile and is a big player here with a lot better to come.

runners.comment: Too Darn Hot filly; bred to be well above average and needs considering on her first run
runners.spotlight: Too Darn Hot filly; dam a Group-placed 1m2f winner (RPR 105), is closely related to 1m2f Listed winner John Leeper, out of Oaks, Irish Oaks and Irish Champion winner Snow Fairy; bred to be well above average and she needs considering on her first run.

runners.comment: Zoustar filly; the betting can prove an accurate guide for this newcomer
runners.spotlight: £22,000 yearling; Zoustar filly; dam placed at 5f/6f (RPR 72), is a half-sister to winners Gilt Edge Girl (5f Group 1 Abbaye) and Godfrey Street (5f 2yo Group 2); the betting can prove an accurate guide for this newcomer.

runners.comment: Frankel filly ended 2025 with a good Newcastle second; must enter calculations on return
runners.spotlight: Progressive Frankel filly who came in second of nine in 7f Newcastle novice in October; she has more to offer so must enter calculations on her seasonal return.

runners.comment: Promising Haydock second but twice failed to build on it; could still do better in 2026
runners.spotlight: Daughter of Blue Point who made a promising start when second in a 6f Haydock maiden last May but she failed to build on it in two subsequent outings, although not totally disgraced when third in 7f Salisbury maiden in October; she fetched 500,000euros as a yearling and could still do better.

stable_tour.quote: I said last season I thought she was a good filly, but she underachieved. I'm not sure of her trip, but she's very talented, with a proper filly's attitude - not the most straightforward, but with a lot of ability. 21-04-26

runners.comment: This daughter of St Mark's Basilica is in good hands and can't be ruled out on her debut
runners.spotlight: 62,000gns 2yo; dam 5f-6f winner (Listed; RPR 111), half-sister to Listed-placed 5f 2yo winner Looks A Million; this daughter of St Mark's Basilica is in good hands and can't be ruled out on her debut.

runners.comment: Failed to build on debut when last of five at Kempton last month; worth another chance
runners.spotlight: Night Of Thunder filly who failed to build on a debut 7f Wolverhampton fourth in August when last of five in 6f Kempton novice last month; she's worth another chance.

runners.comment: Yet to offer much and beat one at Newcastle in February; blinkers are tried now
runners.spotlight: Yet to offer much for three different trainers, undergoing wind surgery before beating one in 6f Newcastle classified event in February; blinkers are tried now.

runners.comment: Debut Nottingham winner; shaped well when Wolverhampton second on return; the one to beat
runners.spotlight: Starman filly who impressed when making a winning start in 5f Nottingham maiden in October; again shaped well when an odds-on second of three in 5f Wolverhampton novice on her return last month, not enjoying a clear passage, so she's very much the one to beat.

quotes.race: PricedUp EBF Slip Anchor Maiden Stakes (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Time To Take Off feels nice and James [Tate, trainer] was pretty bullish about her. She's going to be lovely, she did it very professionally and travelled into the race lovely. She got a bit tired towards the end but you'd expect that first time out. I said to Phillip Robinson that she feels like she's got a bit of class around her, so it was a good performance - Daniel Tudhope, jockey.Time To Take Off has been working with 80-rated horses and going as well if not better than them, so we thought it would take a decent one to beat her today. We were pretty confident, I'd have been surprised if she'd have got beat today. I was a little bit worried about the ground, she wouldn't have wanted it to have gotten any softer. I think she'll be one for next year. She's got a nice pedigree and will get further in time, she's still got a bit of growing to do so she'll be more of a project - Phillip Robinson, owner's racing manager.

runners.comment: Hinted at promise in pair of 6f novices at Chelmsford and Wolverhampton; place prospects
runners.spotlight: Havana Grey colt who has hinted at promise in a pair of 6f novices at Chelmsford and Wolverhampton this spring, fifth on latter occasion eight days ago; holds place prospects.

runners.breeder: G H S Bloodstock & J C Bloodstock
runners.comment: Son of Mehmas can't be discounted on his debut, especially if market vibes are positive
runners.spotlight: 105,000gns yearling; brother to 5f winner Tiva (RPR 86); dam placed at 6f (RPR 71), is closely related to 6f Group 2 winner Tasleet; this son of Mehmas is in good hands and can't be discounted on his debut, especially if the market vibes are positive.

runners.comment: Last at Wolverhampton on sole run for James Tate ten months ago; hooded for new yard
runners.spotlight: Sent of 11-4 but he came in a tailed-off last of four in 6f Wolverhampton novice on his sole run for James Tate ten months ago; since gelded and hood goes on for his new yard.

runners.comment: Last at Ripon on debut nine days ago; significantly more is required
runners.spotlight: 40-1, last of seven in novice at Ripon (6f, good to soft) on his debut nine days ago; significantly more is required from this son of Tasleet.

runners.spotlight: 16,000euros yearling, 55,000gns 2yo; dam, 5f winner (RPR 70), is closely related to 6f winner So Many Questions; this A'Ali filly is no forlorn hope on her first run.

runners.spotlight: Still to register a victory but she's proving a reliable filly and returned from eight months off with a clear second of five in 1m Southwell handicap last month; can race off the same mark here and this step up in trip promises to suit so she's a player.

runners.owner: Hot To Trot Racing 2 & J Fill
runners.comment: Lingfield maiden winner; good fourth at Yarmouth and has more to offer now handicapping
runners.spotlight: Lightly-raced daughter of Masar who got off the mark at the second attempt in 1m Lingfield maiden in September and backed it up with a good fourth under a penalty in 1m Yarmouth novice following month; has more to offer now going handicapping over this longer distance.

stable_tour.quote: She's a lightly raced filly from a family we know well, as a half-sister to Dreamloper, and has progressed encouragingly. I hope she can climb the ladder in handicaps before hunting black type. I think she'll stay 1m2f. 22-04-26

runners.comment: Ended 2025 with 1m h'cap wins at Chelmsford and Newmarket; big shout going up in trip
runners.spotlight: Low mileage and ended 2025 firmly on the up with a pair of 1m handicap victories at Chelmsford and Newmarket in October; up another 5lb but this well-related Dubawi filly remains on a workable mark; big shout on her first go at 1m2f.

quotes.race: CopyBet Fillies' Handicap
quotes.quote: Naga has not been the most straightforward but has been on an upward curve in recent weeks and she could stay in training but that is up for discussion - Thady Gosden, joint-trainer.

runners.comment: Dual 1m2f winner but off since coming in last at Sandown last July; others are preferred
runners.spotlight: A dual 1m2f winner at 2yrs but she's been off the track since coming in last of ten in 1m2f Sandown handicap last July; others are preferred.

runners.comment: Course winner; failed to beat rival in Fillies Mile at Newmarket; remains with potential
runners.spotlight: Made a winning start over 7f here and followed up in 1m Chelmsford novice last summer; failed to beat a rival in the Fillies' Mile at Newmarket after but she remains with potential on her return in this less exacting company.

quotes.race: bet365 EBF Restricted Novice Stakes (For horses In Bands B, C And D) (EBF Qualifier) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: We all came here hoping to see Amora Queen win a bit more impressively, but the fact we thought she might still be raw was why we're here and not in better company. We actually thought about taking this filly to the Star Stakes at Sandown, but Jaber actually won that with another filly [Hope Queen], who beat my runner [Jennifer Jane] on the line, very frustratingly - Charlie Johnston, trainer.Amora Queen has done what's needed. She's a big girl, but she's got a good engine - Jaber Abdullah, owner.

quotes.race: Yorkshire Air Ambulance EBF Maiden Fillies' Stakes (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Has Waldgeist ever had a June two-year-old winner? Have a look at the size and shape of Amora Queen, what's she going to be next year? - Mark Johnston, trainer's father.

stable_tour.quote: She's a huge, scopey filly and was probably achieving ahead of her time last year. We bit off more than we could chew in the Fillies' Mile and an Oaks entry is probably ambitious at this stage, but she should stay very well and it wouldn't be a huge surprise if she improved enough over middle distances to be up to having a shot at something like that. The tentative route would be to reappear in a fillies' handicap at Doncaster on Saturday, or the slightly more ambitious route would be the Cheshire Oaks. She showed a good level of ability at two and has always looked like she'll be much better at three, which is quite exciting. She's wintered very well and had a racecourse gallop at the Craven meeting. 21-04-26

runners.comment: Bagged novices at Wolverhampton and Southwell; capable of better on h'cap/turf debut
runners.spotlight: Progressive Golden Horn filly who bids for a hat-trick after bagging novices at Wolverhampton (9.5f) and Southwell (1m4f) last month; capable of better still now venturing into handicap company on her turf debut.

runners.comment: Breakthrough win at Newcastle in February; not ruled out on h'cap debut up in distance
runners.spotlight: Built on earlier promise when gaining her breakthrough victory in 1m novice at Newcastle in February; this Massaat filly is another who can't be ruled out on her handicap debut stepping up in distance.

racecards.verdict: John and Thady Gosden's NAGA is taken to continue her progress and complete a hat-trick at the chief expense of Rockin' The Boat

runners.comment: Looks quirky but beat Sailor Song in Southwell maiden (AW) when suited by move up to 1m3f
runners.spotlight: Looks quirky but he followed three seconds at 1m/1m2f by asserting late on from Sailor Song in a 1m3f maiden at Southwell (AW) two weeks ago, looking suited by the extra distance; blinkered on last two starts; 2025 turf form to start career was modest but another extra furlong should help; player.

runners.comment: Cheekpieces now after Al Azd proved too strong late on Southwell (1m3f, AW); player
runners.spotlight: Made debut in February; improved when second in maidens at Doncaster (1m2f, good to soft) and Southwell (1m3f, AW; under Toby Moore) and now has cheekpieces after Al Azd proved too strong for him late on in the latest race; should be competitive on handicap debut.

runners.comment: 1m win on heavy at Goodwood (three ran) last September, far better than starts either side
runners.spotlight: Showed staying potential with a 1m win on heavy ground in three-runner race at Goodwood last September, which was far better than his starts either side; gelded since; should be capable of better this season switched to handicapping but it is needed.

quotes.race: British EBF Peter Willett Future Stayers' Maiden Stakes (Sire/Dam Restricted) (GBB/GBBPlus Race)
quotes.quote: Lopeo is definitely a future stayer in the making. I liked him in Chester [debut] and you knew one of David's [Menuisier, trainer] would come on for the run. He loved the ground and, although the penny has nowhere near dropped, he's going about it the right way - Rossa Ryan, jockey, speaking to Racing TV.

runners.comment: Fair 5th at Nottingham (1m2f, good) on return did not press his claims for handicap debut
runners.spotlight: Two runs in November were on AW, rallying to win a novice at Newcastle (1m) on second occasion; fair fifth of nine in a novice at Nottingham (1m2f, good) from the front on reappearance did not press his claims for today's handicap debut, but these are early days.

quotes.race: Best Odds Guaranteed At BetMGM EBF Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Director's Cut was massively in need of it at Wolverhampton first time out, very green and raw, but he's stepped up and done the job nicely. I think he'll make a better three-year-old so it's nice he's got a win under his belt. He showed a willing attitude and is a horse who will probably get ten furlongs - Luke Catton, jockey, speaking to Sky Sports Racing.

runners.comment: Makes a striking move from 1m to 1m4f for this handicap/turf debut and needs a close look
runners.spotlight: Made debut in December; runner-up on first two starts before making all at 4-9 in a five-runner novice at Newcastle in January; all those races were 1m on AW and he kept hanging left last time, but he makes a striking move up to 1m4f for this handicap/turf debut and needs a close look.

stable_tour.quote: He won his novice over a mile but is shaping as though he'll be better when stepped up to a mile and a quarter, and he may well get a mile and a half come the summer. He's a colt we've always liked and strikes me as one of those three-year-old middle-distance handicappers that we tend to do well with. 21-04-26

runners.comment: Good third of seven off this mark at Nottingham (1m2f) in October; gelded since
runners.spotlight: 33-1 winner in an eight-runner novice at Thirsk (7f, soft) last September, coming from towards rear to lead in final strides; good third of seven in nursery at Nottingham (1m2f, good to soft; gelded since) in October made 1m4f looks plausible but he needs further improvement off the same mark.

runners.comment: 1m3f AW maiden latest suggests she will stay 1m4f; needs to find extra on handicap debut
runners.spotlight: Fair form on all three starts, best form on soft ground on second occasion; latest was her closest finish, though, when making most in a 1m3f maiden at Kempton (AW) and that performance suggests she will stay 1m4f; needs to find extra to get off the mark on this handicap debut.

racecards.verdict: Al Azd found more than Sailor Song at the end of their 1m3f maiden at Southwell but ALBA GU BRATH (nap) could be a big improver.

runners.comment: Got off mark over C&D last July; since gelded and looks to have more to offer; big shout
runners.spotlight: Highly tried before getting off the mark in novice over C&D last July; not seen again but this son of Frankel has since been gelded and remains with plenty of potential for this season; big shout.

quotes.race: Darley EBF Novice Stakes (Winning 3yo To Receive Free Entry To 2025 Betfred St Leger) (GBB/GBBPlus)
quotes.quote: The Cursor has done nothing wrong really, he's just struggled at the grade on his last couple of starts. I think he'll get there in time. He stays well, has a lovely big action, and kept finding when challenged. Connections will have their ideas. Today was an easier assignment and we were hoping he'd pick it up as well as he did - Jason Watson, jockey, speaking to Sky Sports Racing.

runners.comment: Off six months off before solid second at Wolverhampton recently; can make presence felt
runners.spotlight: A two-time AW scorer (around 1m4f) last spring and she resumed from six months off with a solid second of seven in 1m4f Wolverhampton handicap three weeks ago; she can make her presence felt back on turf.

runners.comment: Won over fences at Southwell before pulled up at Market Rasen in December; more is needed
runners.spotlight: Ended his time with Adrian Keatley below par last autumn but a winner over fences at Southwell for his new yard before being pulled up at Market Rasen in December; needs to bounce back after a layoff.

quotes.race: William Hill More Top Prices Novices' Hurdle (GBB Race) (Div I)
quotes.quote: I'd say Maghlaak is going to be a decent horse, jumping will toughen him up. His bit of class showed there late on and he did that well.  We bought him as a dual-purpose horse and he has a great pedigree - his dam won the Guineas - Adrian Keatley, trainer

quotes.race: Golf At Goodwood Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Maghlaak had a lot of weight, so did it well. I've no idea about plans - Jim Crowley, rider.

stable_tour.quote: He finished well to win at Goodwood on his comeback, but he was drawn ten of ten at Redcar last time and could never get any cover. It was a non-event and I'm putting a line through it. He's a pretty talented horse, who likes to get his toe in, and I think the mile and a half would suit him well if he makes the cut. 13-06-24

He's been a good servant for us. He ran a good race in the Group 3 Silver Cup at York and then went so close at Market Rasen. I think if we keep stepping him up in trip, we'll get similar or better results with him. We'll look at the staying race at the Shergar Cup meeting and continue to mix it between hurdles and the Flat. He might jump fences in time. 07-08-25

runners.comment: A three-time 1m4f winner but ended 2025 under a cloud; has gone well fresh though

runners.comment: In good form until only sixth in Newcastle h'cap last month; needs to bounce back
runners.spotlight: French recruit; gained a first success for his current yard in 1m2f Newcastle handicap in December and in good form since until only sixth of seven in 1m4f handicap there last month; needs to bounce back.

runners.comment: Started well for new yard until beating two at Lingfield in January; returns from a break
runners.spotlight: Bagged three 1m2f handicaps last season (final one for Brian Toomey) and started well for her new handler until beating just two in 1m2f Lingfield handicap in January; returns from a break here.

runners.comment: Good second at Kempton but well held at Yarmouth since; the sort to bounce back
runners.spotlight: A fair 1m4f scorer for Jedd O'Keeffe; resurgent for his new yard when runner-up at Kempton (1m3f) in February but well held at Yarmouth two weeks ago; the sort to bounce back though.

racecards.verdict: The Harry Eustace-trained 4yo SEA OF KINGS has better days ahead of him and can make a winning return, with Charmaine next best.

runners.spotlight: Back to winning ways at Lingfield (1m) in February but he beat one in 1m Southwell handicap 20 days ago; needs to bounce back on turf.

runners.comment: Took this 12 months ago; hinted at revival with Thirsk seventh latest; interesting
runners.spotlight: Took this 12 months ago; not seen after June in 2025 but hinted at a revival on his second run back when seventh of 13 in 1m Thirsk handicap 15 days ago; he's one to be interested in off a 2lb lower mark here.

stable_tour.quote: He had his first run for us over hurdles at Musselburgh last week and did okay, finishing fourth. He'll go back on the Flat now and is probably very well handicapped. He's the type who'll be winning at the back end of January in a 0-65 over a mile at Wolverhampton. 05-12-24

runners.comment: Beat one at Southwell in October; this C&D winner needs a wind op to spark a resurgence
runners.spotlight: It's now 14 starts since his last success and he beat just one in 1m Southwell handicap when last seen in October; this C&D winner needs a subsequent wind operation to spark a resurgence.

quotes.race: MansionBet #Betstival Handicap
quotes.quote: I wouldn't say Siam Fox liked the track on this ground as he hit every undulation, but he got away with it. I didn't want to take any chances as I think a mile is as short as he wants to go. I think a different track and further will bring out more improvement - Silvestre de Sousa, rider.

prev_owners.owner: Anthony Ramsden, Nigel Skinner & Ron Hull

runners.comment: Not one to rely on and he failed to beat a rival on his return in Thirsk h'cap 15 days ago
runners.spotlight: Not one to rely on and he failed to beat a rival on his return in 1m Thirsk handicap 15 days ago; others are much preferred.

quotes.race: Play Coral "Racing-Super-Series" For Free Nursery Handicap
quotes.quote: It was testing and we were scratching our heads in the final stages as we hadn't got the job done yet, fortunately he got his head in front. I thought I was going to win easily two furlongs out, but Whiskey Pete was waiting the whole last furlong and went away when one came to him - Hector Crouch, jockey.

stable_tour.quote: We bought him to go to Bahrain at the start of the year, where he ran twice. He ran very well when he was second at Doncaster in August and then lost his way a bit. He wants a mile because 1m2f probably stretches him. He wants good ground and I don't think he'll go on the all-weather. He'll win races. 01-10-25

prev_owners.owner: J C G Chua And Partner

runners.comment: Winless since March 2024; yet to hit top form in trio of handicaps at Newcastle this year
runners.spotlight: Without a victory since March 2024 and he's yet to hit top form in a trio of handicaps at Newcastle this year, only seventh of nine over 1m there last month.

quotes.race: British Stallion Studs EBF Novice Stakes (GBB Race) (IRE Incentive Race)
quotes.quote: I think the world of Chuzzlewit. He relaxed lovely today but he was still green and backward and there is more to come. He shows speed at home but he'll have no problem staying a mile next year. He won't run again until next year, he'll keep progressing and I don't know how good he could be - Kevin Ryan, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: He travelled very strongly through the Lincoln but just got a bit lost when he was let down on the testing ground. It was a better run than his finishing position suggests and we know now not to run in such testing conditions again. He's another who could be competitive in some of those decent 7f-mile handicaps in the summer. 04-04-24

I really like what I have seen from this colt who is a half-brother to triple Group 1 winner Advertise out of a particularly good Cheveley Park mare. He is doing everything nicely at home although I am not pressing too many buttons too soon, so he will be ready hopefully by the middle of next month, but definitely one to look out for. 15-06-22

runners.comment: Underwent breathing surgery before breakthrough Yarmouth win; up 4lb but not taken lightly
runners.spotlight: Underwent breathing surgery before gaining a breakthrough win on her seasonal return in 1m Yarmouth handicap two weeks ago; back up 4lb but she's not taken lightly in her current mood.

runners.comment: Winning return at Kempton; solid Lingfield third since so not out of things back on turf
runners.spotlight: Made a winning return after a spell in Hong Kong in 7f Kempton handicap and backed it up with a solid third of seven at Lingfield (7f) later in February; not out of things back on turf with this step up to 1m a likely plus.

quotes.race: Ascot Iron Stand Membership British EBF Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: We might look to throw  U S S CONSTITUTION in at the deep end next time. He's a lovely horse and I think he's the sort to be better when he's in a better class of race too - Ed Walker, trainer.

runners.comment: Failed to beat a rival in 7f Wolverhampton handicap last time; hard to warm to
runners.spotlight: Scored on his debut here in June 2024 but without a victory since and fitted with eyeshields when failing to beat a rival in 7f Wolverhampton handicap last time; hard to warm to.

quotes.race: HKJC World Pool Vintage Stakes (Group 2)
quotes.quote: Wolf Of Badenoch ran very well but he was quite inexperienced over the first half mile. I had to engage him down to the two pole but he put up a big performance around the field - Jamie Spencer, rider.

quotes.race: Ice Cream Direct EBF Maiden Stakes (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Jamie was very impressed with Wolf Of Badenoch. He said he sustained a really good, long run while still being quite babyish. He said he galloped out very well and the feeling is there's plenty more to come from him - Hugo Palmer, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: He's filled into his frame over the winter and I was struck by how much he'd grown when I saddled him for the Autumn Stakes. He ran well at Chelmsford but he probably looks more like a handicapper than a Group horse at this stage. He's been gelded and we'll aim for the Britannia. I expect he'll get a mile and a quarter as the season progresses. 09-04-25

runners.comment: Dual 1m AW winner in 2026; tenth in h'cap here four weeks ago so needs to bounce back
runners.spotlight: Already a dual 1m AW winner in 2026 but he saw his run of good form come to an end when tenth in 1m2f handicap here four weeks ago; needs to get back on track.

quotes.race: Clieveragh Handicap
quotes.quote: Relevant Range was flat out the whole way but Darragh got him travelling and enthusiastic. It was a fantastic ride because the hors isn't the most genuine - Gillian Scott, trainer.

prev_owners.owner: Haras D'Etreham, Riviera Equine Sarl & Ecurie De Montlahuc

runners.comment: Veteran is on a losing run but has gone well off a break though so is no forlorn hope
runners.spotlight: A useful 1m winner at his best but this veteran seems not so good nowadays; he has gone well off a break though so is no forlorn hope on his seasonal return.

stable_tour.quote: He won at Beverley on his comeback and then ran a nice race in the Thirsk Hunt Cup. A nice, big horse with some reasonable form in France, he could have a good enough summer and might run at York this week. 09-05-22

runners.comment: In decent nick, suffering a poor run when seventh at Beverley latest; considered
runners.spotlight: A dual 7f/1m scorer at Redcar last autumn and she comes here in decent nick, suffering a poor run when seventh of ten in 8.5f Beverley handicap ten days ago; needs considering off a slipping mark.

runners.comment: Without a win since October 2024; just seventh at Newcastle 12 days ago; more needed
runners.spotlight: Without a win since October 2024 and he failed to build on a reappearance Newcastle third when just seventh in 1m handicap there 12 days ago; needs to take a step forward.

stable_tour.quote: Last year was a good one for him with four wins, all at Newcastle over a mile. He had a busy time of it and has had aeak since December. He'll need to improve a bit this year because he's risen to a mark of 66. He needs to be held up. 09-04-25

runners.owner: Dr M Voikhansky & Mrs S Voikhanskaya
runners.comment: In good form when last seen in the autumn; has gone well fresh too so can't be discounted
runners.spotlight: Scored twice (around 1m) at Leicester and Lingfield last summer but not seen out after a solid third in 8.5f Wolverhampton handicap in September; she has gone well fresh though so can't be discounted.

racecards.verdict: It could be worth siding with Jennie Candlish's MARINER to build on a recent Thirsk seventh and follow up his victory in this a year ago
racecards.betting_forecast: 3/1 U S S Constitution, 5/1 Queen Of Good News, 7/1 Pisanello, 8/1 Pretty Spirited, 9/1 Mariner, 10/1 Chuzzlewit,  Barleybrown, 11/1 Fire Eyes, 12/1 Union Island,  Siam Fox, 16/1 Relevant Range, 20/1 Wolf Of Badenoch, 33/1 Whiskey Pete

runners.owner: Exors Of The Late Sheikh Mohammed Obaid
runners.comment: Impressed at Southwell (1m4f) last month; up against a useful opponent but can do better
runners.spotlight: Created a positive impression when easily winning a 1m4f novice at Southwell last month, coming home 3l clear of a stablemate of Pursuit Of Love; likely he will need more to follow up but he is still of serious interest.

runners.comment: Upped in trip and fitted with headgear for his return; needs to leave 2yo form behind him
runners.spotlight: Ran to a modest level in novices on good to soft ground last autumn (7f and 1m1f); upped in trip and tried in headgear for his reappearance and this 4,300,000gns yearling remains capable of better.

runners.comment: 13,000euros yearling from a good German middle-distance family; tough task on debut
runners.spotlight: 13,000euros yearling; ninth foal; half-brother to seven winners including Quian (1m-2m Flat including 2yo/German Group 3, RPR 104; 2m-2m3f hurdle) and Laggata (9.4f; 76); dam German 1m4f winner, half-sister to triple 1m4f Group 1 winner Quijano; should have a bright future but he makes his debut in a good novice.

racecards.verdict: Ravenspire should be winning more races but PURSUIT OF LOVE was strong at the finish when scoring at Southwell and can follow up.
racecards.betting_forecast: 8/13 Pursuit Of Love, 9/4 Ravenspire, 9/1 Poker, 10/1 Quiet Summer

racecards.race_name: William Hill Price Boosts Every Day EBF Fillies' Novice Stakes (GBB Race)

runners.comment: Improved for a hood when springing 50-1 surprise at Southwell (1m) this month; more needed
runners.spotlight: Never in contention on her Wolverhampton debut in February (8.6f); fitted with a hood for her second start and she recorded a shock 50-1 success in a five-runner event over 1m at Southwell 23 days ago; this looks tougher under a penalty.

runners.comment: Did really well to win on debut (1m, AW) given she did a lot wrong; looks a good prospect
runners.spotlight: Smart pedigree; did really well to win a 1m fillies' novice at Chelmsford in December, blowing the start and having plenty to do turning for home but producing a fast finish to win under a hand ride; strong claims despite her penalty.

runners.comment: Half-sister to six winners and should have a future; trainer also runs Chimes Of Thunder
runners.spotlight: Eighth foal; half-sister to six winners including Alkandora (10.5f Listed; RPR 107), Persian Royal (1m; 97) and Cambric (1m4f-1m6f; 84); dam Listed-placed 1m 2yo winner (103); one of two for William Haggas but Tom Marquand rides Chimes Of Thunder.

runners.comment: Promise on sole 2yo start for D Menuisier (7f, good); open to improvement over 1m+
runners.spotlight: Dropped away in the final furlong on her Salisbury debut last October (7f, good; trained by David Menuisier), a race that developed into a three-furlong sprint; should appreciate today's longer trip and she's an interesting contender starting out for William Haggas (same owners).

runners.comment: 300-1 and finished well beaten on last month's Wolverhampton debut (8.6f)
runners.spotlight: 300-1 and finished well beaten on last month's Wolverhampton debut (8.6f).

runners.comment: 425,000gns half-sister to two winners out of a useful 6f winner; market check advised
runners.spotlight: 425,000gns yearling; third foal; half-sister to winners Manara (1m-1m4f; RPR 89) and Dance Desire (Saudi Arabia 7f-1m1f); dam 6f winner (96), out of close relative of 1m2f Group 1 winner Wavering and half-sister to 1m2f 2yo Group 1 winner Mandaean; market strength would look significant.

runners.comment: Dam a Group-placed 1m/1m2f winner (RPR 115); makes her debut with her trainer in fine form
runners.spotlight: Second foal of a Group-placed 1m/1m2f winner (RPR 115), herself from a good family; makes her debut for a stable in good form and she needs a look in the betting.

racecards.verdict: Some interesting fillies on show but none more so than SYMBOL OF MAJESTY, who overcame adversity to make a winning debut in December.
racecards.betting_forecast: 10/11 Symbol Of Majesty, 5/1 Forbidden Colours, 7/1 Chimes Of Thunder,  Mountain Of Light, 9/1 Silken Bay, 10/1 Sedeirah, 16/1 Brighton Beach, 200/1 Golden Mabel

runners.owner: Exors Of The Late Sheikh Mohammed Obaid
runners.comment: Ex-Australian; Group 1 placed; absent 420 days; looks to face stiff task on British debut
runners.spotlight: Finished second in a Group 1 in Australia in October 2024 (1m2f, good; visored first time); well short of his best in two runs in early 2025 and has since been gelded and transferred to Britain; had a wind op prior to this first start for Kevin Ryan; no easy task under top weight.

runners.owner: Nick Bradley Racing 2 & Mrs E Burke
runners.comment: Unexposed at 7f; better than he showed at Newcastle three weeks ago; not ruled out
runners.spotlight: Close third in Listed company at Wolverhampton last month on his first attempt at 7f and he wasn't beaten for a lack of stamina; not at his best in a hot sprint handicap at Newcastle on Good Friday; no surprise to see him bounce back with a big run.

quotes.race: William Hill Best Odds Guaranteed Cammidge Trophy Stakes (Listed Race)
quotes.quote: Marshman was on and off the bridle all along, he was never travelling like he usually does. I'm sure there is more in the tank from him - Karl Burke, trainer.

quotes.race: BetUK Kachy Stakes (Listed Race)
quotes.quote: Marshman has been gelded and the wind op has improved him a bit more. It feels like he can breathe a bit better in his races. We've got a long season ahead - it's not really started yet so there'll be plenty of races - and he'll probably go into a Group 3 at some point. He's beaten some really good horses and I'll be looking forward to him next time. There were a few question marks as it was a sharper six furlongs, but a quicker gallop was going to suit him. He's very fiery. Even though he's won over six furlongs at Newcastle he's performed today - Clifford Lee, jockey.

quotes.race: Weekly £5 Free Bet With BetUK Handicap
quotes.quote: We don't really have a long-term target but Marshman took well to the all-weather, so the six-furlong handicap on finals' day would be an obvious place to look. That was his first time on the surface, so we'd need to find two more runs. We can aim high with him. I hope that's not the highlight of the year for him and it's just the start - Nick Bradley of Nick Bradley Racing.

quotes.race: Al Basti Equiworld Dubai Gimcrack Stakes (Group 2) (Colts & Geldings) (IRE Incentive Race)
quotes.quote: They're two lovely colts and we've got a lot to look forward to with them. Maybe running seven days after last week may not have helped Marshman, he had a real good blow. Though he won very easily, he had a race. There's a little bit more to come from him, maybe ridden a little bit differently. Clifford said he's still a bit green when he's in front on his own - Karl Burke, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: Being gelded and having wind surgery last summer definitely helped him. He's been in really good form on the all-weather this winter and goes for the All-Weather finals day at Newcastle on Friday week. He was a bit wound up in the stalls at Doncaster and never travelled after that, so I don't think that was his true running. If he can stay calm at the start, I think he'll be competitive off top weight at Newcastle. 11-04-25

An exciting time of the year for our stable as last year's smart juveniles form part of the strongest team of three-year-olds I have had to train. Marshman did his bit last year winning the first starts before finding only Noble Style too good for him in the Gimcrack. He is a very fast horse who will stick to sprints this year and he showed his well being when taking the Group 3 Prix Sigy at Chantilly (5½f) a couple of weeks ago. That was a smart performance as I thought he would need the run first time out. He has come out of that well and the plan is the Sandy Lane Stakes, which we won last year with El Caballo. He also has the Commonwealth Cup as his first big target for the year. 07-05-23

runners.breeder: D Ryan, D S Ryan & R A Williams
runners.comment: Ended 2025 in fine form at 1m; may come on for this first start since October
runners.spotlight: Had strong handicap form over 1m in the second half of 2025, finishing second at York's Ebor meeting (good to firm) before recording back-to-back wins at Goodwood (good to soft and good); ran well for third in a Nottingham Listed race when last seen 178 days ago; only seventh in this race 12 months ago and he's 4lb higher today.

quotes.race: Best Price Guaranteed Daily At Vickers.Bet Handicap
quotes.quote: All credit to Cerulean Bay, he had it all to do from that draw,. We were drawn the widest and he's off 96 now, he's high enough but he's got the right attitude. If something comes to him, he keeps going and he likes it here. There's no stopping him at the minute, he's having a great season - Danny Tudhope, jockey, speaking to Racing TV.

quotes.race: EBF Stallions Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Cerulean Bay was very good. This would be his minimum trip but he's a lovely horse for the future. It felt like a good race, so it's a nice performance to give away that weight - Danny Tudhope, jockey.

stable_tour.quote: He had a very good season last year. On his last run in Ireland he pulled up lame, so we feel there's still room in his mark and he can go on again. Dropping him back to seven furlongs seems to have been the making of him. He's very tough round a bend, so we'll look at the good handicaps on those tracks. 14-04-25

runners.comment: Improved effort when 3rd in 6f Listed event four weeks ago; up 3lb and stamina not assured
runners.spotlight: Won a valuable pot as a 2yo; slow to come to hand as a 3yo but he changed yards last summer and made an impressive winning return from a gelding operation last September (6f, good to soft; cheekpieces on for the first time); fine reappearance when third in the Listed Cammidge Trophy at Doncaster (6f, good to soft) four weeks ago; raised 3lb for his troubles and still has to prove his stamina for 7f.

quotes.race: Boodles Handicap
quotes.quote: We had changed a lot of things and of course you're nervous. It was Caburn's second run for me ? first time gelded, first time in cheekpieces, first time on easy ground. There were quite a lot of changed variables. My fear was whether he'd handle the ground, but I got more optimistic as he moved down to post. He had some really hard races as a two-year-old, and you wouldn't have blamed him if he wasn't up for putting his best foot forward. I did think I had my work cut out. We needed a complete change, and it was nice to see him back to form. He's a horse that doesn't have the straightest of legs and he was moved to me so he could swim every day, which he embraces now and it seems to have helped him a lot. We'll have to see what the handicapper does and whether we go for a big handicap or some smaller Listed races - James Tate, trainer.

quotes.race: Weatherbys Super Sprint Stakes (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: The question mark was dropping back to five furlongs after Caburn won over six on his debut. We were always coming here with the prize-money but, in the first two furlongs, I thought this ain't happening today. To do that on his second start is pretty unreal and the Gimcrack would be an obvious next step. This will be the last time he'll run over five furlongs; onwards and upwards - Jack Jones, trainer.

quotes.race: Juddmonte EBF Restricted Novice Stakes (Bands C/D) (EBF Restricted Race Qualifier) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: At home Caburn was showing the right things to be a nice horse but, worryingly, most of the 2yos I've ran so far have ran averagely but I thought he was above them so it was nice to see him put it in on the track. This was a half bit of a stepping stone to the Super Sprint and so far the first leg has gone remarkably well - Jack Jones, trainer, speaking to RTV.

runners.comment: Strong 7f handicap form in blinkers in 2025; headgear absent for return but back on today
runners.spotlight: Strong handicap form over 7f last summer, winning at Goodwood and Chepstow as well as finishing second in a 20-runner event at Ascot (all when wearing blinkers); still feasibly weighted on that form and he went without headgear when down the field in the Lincoln; the blinkers return today and he's a leading contender.

stable_tour.quote: He did really well last year, winning four times. He's been a little disappointing this season but I think possibly the handicapper's got hold of him. He went up from 68 - the mark he won his first race off last year - to starting this year on 92. With a bit of luck, he'll start winning again soon - and he runs at Newmarket on Thursday. 02-07-25

runners.comment: Conditions should suit and he has good record in a hood; new stable going well at present
runners.spotlight: Began 2025 with 7f novice wins at Kempton and Doncaster; ended his 3yo campaign with a close third at Doncaster (7f, soft) 183 days ago; sold out of Roger Varian's stable for 85,000gns in October; still has low mileage, is yet to run a poor race when wearing a hood and is starting out for a trainer in great form; lots to like.

runners.comment: Below par over 6f last time but on the up over 7f beforehand; now tries cheekpieces
runners.spotlight: His latest Newcastle defeat isn't the run to judge him on and he had been progressing well beforehand; no problem with the return to turf and stepping back up to 7f will be of benefit; interesting with cheekpieces now given a go.

runners.comment: Smart handicapper for the Crisfords but he has a 1038-day absence to defy on stable debut
runners.spotlight: Progressive handicapper for the Crisfords and he was last seen finishing second in the Buckingham Palace at Royal Ascot (7f, good to firm) in June 2023; sold for 20,000gns in May 2024; only dropped 3lb during his 1038-day absence; likely best watched.

quotes.race: Sky Bet Hambleton Handicap
quotes.quote: Croupier is a lovely horse. They went quite hard up front and William sat just off it a bit. He rode a very nice race and the horse travelled into it very well. I thought they were coming after him but he kept finding more. We can head to the the Hunt Cup now, that's the plan and it could be a good race for him, the strong pace and big field should suit him. It's nice to see him bounce back because we probably shouldn't have run him on terrible ground in the Lincoln. He's come back in good style - Ed Crisford, joint-trainer.

stable_tour.quote: He came through his nursery programme with credit, will stay at least a mile and is one to look forward to in handicaps this season. I think he has enough upside on his rating to make him interesting. 25-04-22

runners.comment: Unexposed 4yo; stable in better form now and he is one to consider after nine months off
runners.spotlight: Began his career with two 7f AW wins and he was a fine second at Chester on his handicap debut last June (7f, good); fourth of 17 in a 1m handicap at Ascot when last seen nine months ago, a run that can be marked up as he raced away from the first three home; still has potential and he returns with his stable back in better form.

runners.breeder: E A R L Ecurie Haras Du Cadran Et Al
runners.comment: Stiff task on his return and finished well held; the absent visor remains a concern
runners.spotlight: Came good at Goodwood last August (7f, good to firm), running on strongly to bag a Class 2 handicap; faced a stiff task in a Thirsk conditions event on his reappearance two weeks ago; opposable with his usual visor remaining absent.

quotes.race: Winners Wear Cavani Handicap
quotes.quote: Darkness enjoyed the change of tactics and he's got plenty of ability, it's just getting it out of him. It was a decent enough run today, he just got tired close home - Hollie Doyle, jockey.

stable_tour.quote: He's a law unto himself. Last year he won at Newmarket and then ran well in the Golden Mile at Goodwood, but he can throw a bad run and doesn't win as often as he should. He likes to be ridden forward, but when he gets behind he has his own ideas. 19-04-24

runners.owner: Fine Claret Racing,Mrs Burke & C Wood

prev_owners.owner: Fine Claret Racing & More Turf Racing

runners.comment: Doncaster return easy to excuse; on dangerous mark and 7f looks an avenue worth exploring
runners.spotlight: Well beaten at Doncaster on his return but he wasn't well drawn and has a modest record fresh; stepping up to 7f will give him more time to claw back the ground he's likely to forfeit at the start; on a dangerous mark and he's a lively outsider, for all his losing run stretches back to October 2023.

quotes.race: Virgin Bet Ayr Gold Cup Handicap (Heritage Handicap)
quotes.quote: Korker seemed to get away reasonably well, he was tracking the pace and he finished strongly - Karl Burke, trainer.

quotes.race: Sri Lanka, The Jewel Of Asia Handicap
quotes.quote: Korker was very good and he especially jumped the gates nicely. He was very relaxed at the start and he picked them off. He bumped into a horse rated 111 at Ascot [Emaraaty Ana] and wasn't far behind him. His last three runs have been very good and he's been frustrating at the gates before, but he's really come on. He's grown up now. He's got a bit of a confidence booster now and after speaking to the boss that might be it for the year, so he'd be ending it on a high - Clifford Lee, rider.

quotes.race: Eddie And Violet Smith Conditions Stakes (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Korker has been so unlucky as he keeps missing the break and deserves his win. I've ridden him loads and when he doesn't miss the break, he never actually races through, but when you miss it slightly he hits the frame. He didn't miss it today, but we couldn't get into stride in the first furlong. I thought we were going to get lapped but he really got me back into it - Clifford Lee, jockey.

quotes.race: Longines Irish Champions Weekend Handicap
quotes.quote: Korker was very relaxed for a sprinter. He'll go for the Holyroodhouse Handicap at Royal Ascot.

quotes.race: Lee Thomas Christy Memorial Nursery Handicap
quotes.quote: Korber is a little bit quirky in the stalls, hence he goes in last with the hood on, but he jumped reasonably quickly and had a nice smooth run. He's a high-class horse, who we've thrown in the deep end, and he's proved he's got a lot of ability. We'll see what Listed races are around for him and I'm sure he'll be a lovely horse next year - Karl Burke, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: He came back a little bit tight from his last run at Hamilton but we should be able to get him back for the Wokingham. He can be a bit slowly away but Jack Nicholls seems to get a good tune out of him and we'll stick with him. It's a good opportunity for Jack to ride in a race like that.   12-06-25

A horse I have a lot of time for. He was most unfortunate not to win on his debut at York last year when missing the break, giving up several lengths and only going down by a head. He has not done a lot wrong since, winning three times as a juvenile and ending up the season on a mark of 92. On his second run this season at York last time he defied top weight with an impressive win over 5f, but the handicapper has really hammered him hard with a 9lb rise. He was going for the Holyroodhouse after that but it will be tough now off 104. We will still head to the royal meeting and see how that pans out, but off his new mark we will have to start looking at Listed and Group 3 races for him. I think there is more to come - I certainly hope so after such a sharp hike in his mark. 01-06-22

runners.comment: Two 7f wins on slower ground in France; sold 36,000euros since latest run; others safer
runners.spotlight: The winner of two of his six starts in France, both over 7f on ground slower than good; sold for 36,000euros in February; makes his stable debut in a competitive race.

racecards.verdict: The return of blinkers should see GREAT ACCLAIM (nap) in a better light and his 7f handicap form last summer was rock solid.
racecards.betting_forecast: 7/2 Cosi Bello, 9/2 Sarab Star,  Khafiz, 7/1 Caburn,  Great Acclaim, 9/1 Cerulean Bay, 10/1 Marshman, 16/1 Darkness, 20/1 Henlein,  Korker, 33/1 Croupier,  The Angel King

racecards.race_name: William Hill Bet Builder Winnings Boost Handicap (GBBPlus Race)

runners.comment: Good 2nd on AW return last month; poorly positioned when 3rd over 1m2f latest; solid
runners.spotlight: Two wins over shorter as a 3yo; improved when second at Kempton on his seasonal return last month (1m) and when third at Nottingham 17 days ago he found himself poorly positioned; well worth another crack at this trip and he should make a bold bid.

runners.comment: Lightly raced filly; conditions should be fine and drop back in class will help; chance
runners.spotlight: Only four ran when she won her novice at Newcastle (1m2f) last September; better form in handicaps on her last two starts, second at Newcastle (1m4f) and a close sixth in a Class 2 at Lingfield when last seen in December; still has time to better now returned to turf.

runners.comment: 1m maiden win in Ireland came on soft ground; well beaten on stable debut; new trip today
runners.spotlight: His two peak efforts for Paddy Twomey came over 1m on soft ground; 50-1 when tailed off in the Spring Mile at Doncaster on his seasonal return; some encouragement for the longer trip on pedigree but he is not a solid option.

runners.comment: Three-time winner in France; market useful back from a break on new ground
runners.spotlight: Three-time winner in France, the latest a claiming success over 1m4f at Longchamp last September (very soft ground); now tackles a much faster surface than he is accustomed to but his brother Ring Of Beara handled good, and probably good to firm too; betting to guide.

runners.owner: Hale Racing, Lyle Farming Company & Ptnr
runners.comment: On a fair mark and dropping back in trip could help; others are more persuasive though
runners.spotlight: On a fair mark on her best Flat form for Harry Charlton; some promise over hurdles for new stable and 1m4f may have stretched her when back on the Flat at Thirsk two weeks ago.

quotes.race: Village Hotels Fillies' Handicap
quotes.quote: Roarin' Success had a little niggle at the beginning of the year so we've taken out time with her. I thought she'd need that on that ground, so I'm nicely surprised with that performance. We'll stick to a mile and find another handicap - Harry Charlton, joint-trainer.

runners.comment: Made all to win at Chester (10.3f, heavy) 218 days ago; this is tougher up 4lb after break
runners.spotlight: Back to winning ways with a front-running 10.3f success in the mud at Chester last September; this course winner will need to return at the top of his game if he is to defy this 4lb higher mark.

quotes.race: Black Type Accountancy EBF 'Confined' Restricted Novice Stakes (Run No More Than Once) (Qual') (GBB)
quotes.quote: Charlie said this morning that Empire Of Light was a better horse than the form of his first run suggested. He felt it was just too firm there for a big, heavy horse like him. He has gone well from the beginning to the end. That rain they had this morning has probably helped him as it was the extreme of conditions last time - Mark Johnston, joint-assistant trainer.

stable_tour.quote: He's a frustrating horse as he's so talented. He's 75 rated and should be 85. He wants a mile to 1m2f, but he's just keen. He's only had a couple of runs this year but we've got him right now. Hopefully he's going to string together a few runs, starting at Haydock on Thursday, and win a couple of races as he's well handicapped. 04-09-25

runners.comment: Not at her best last month; down in the weights and today's return to turf should suit
runners.spotlight: Shaped okay at Wolverhampton on her return from 11 months off in December but she failed to back it up at Southwell last month; dropping down the weights and this return to turf could be beneficial.

stable_tour.quote: She had some decent form on the Flat in Ireland and has more to offer in that sphere, but she's jumped well at home, so we've got options with her. She's probably one for the spring, and undoubtedly a nice dual-purpose prospect. 18-11-25

runners.breeder: D Hefin Jones & Whitsbury Manor Stud
runners.comment: Did well in 2024 but last season was difficult; returns with a point to prove
runners.spotlight: Three wins, two on soft ground, as a 3yo and he is now 9lb lower than for the latest; generally struggled last year though, before and after wind surgery, and he has too much to prove for comfort.

stable_tour.quote: He's another who needs soft ground - it's a never-ending list. It was soft when he won at Windsor and Newbury last year, so we're just waiting for some rain for him. 02-07-25

runners.comment: Four wins last year all came in cheekpieces which are absent for her seasonal return
runners.spotlight: Four wins in 2025, including at this track (extended 1m3f); all of those were in cheekpieces (absent today) and others may have her measure.

racecards.verdict: This may rest between the 4yo contingent with CAVOLO NERO preferred to Winter Flower and Ted Le Saux.
racecards.betting_forecast: 5/2 Cavolo Nero, 11/4 Ted Le Saux, 100/30 Winter Flower, 5/1 Empire Of Light, 14/1 Roarin' Success,  Jujubella, 16/1 Cancelled, 25/1 Due To Henry, 33/1 Naples

racecards.race_name: William Hill Best Odds Guaranteed Handicap

runners.owner: Hambleton Racing Ltd XXXV & E Burke

prev_owners.owner: Hambleton Racing Xlviii & Mrs E Burke

runners.comment: 2-2 in handicaps, readily over 7f (good to firm) and 1m (good to soft); up 4lb; unexposed
runners.spotlight: Has taken great strides since winning a seller last June, winning with authority on handicap debut at Newbury (7f, good to firm) on final 2yo start and he again had reserves when successful at Musselburgh (1m, good to soft) this month; up 4lb but he's anything but exposed; respected.

quotes.race: Virgin Bet A Good Bet Royal Mile Handicap
quotes.quote: The race went exactly as I hoped it would, with a strong pace. Strength Of Spirit doesn't do a lot when he hits the front and I thought Sam might have got there a little bit too soon. We gelded him after his last run last year. He's a little bit of a monkey, he saves a bit for himself and I don't think he was overdoing himself when he hit the front there. We'll see what the handicapper does and he'll step up again - Karl Burke, trainer.

runners.owner: Two Plus Three Two Plus Four
runners.comment: 6f winner on debut; well held in two sales races in September; tough return upped to 1m
runners.spotlight: Bright start, winning at Pontefract (6f, good to firm) then had work cut out trying to give weight to a promising newcomer on AW; big prices and well beaten in two sales races when last seen in September; gelded since and now goes in cheekpieces on handicap debut; faces a tough return upped to 1m.

runners.comment: Arrived late to justify support on AW debut; toppled by useful type since; turf debut
runners.spotlight: Hit the front in the nick of time when justifying support on his Kempton AW debut in September but he was easily outpointed by a promising type on Southwell reappearance (1m) last month, when much more use was made of him; interesting to see the tactics on turf debut but should do better.

runners.comment: Golden pedigree; hard to quantify recent 1m AW maiden win when making all; could progress
runners.spotlight: Golden pedigree, dam had four Group 1 winners (at 1m up to 2m4f) among her siblings, including Friendly Soul for this yard; this one hasn't been as dynamic as the latter so far and his defeat of some newcomers and handicap prospects on Kempton AW (1m; made all) 17 days ago was hard to assess in merit terms; needs more now handicapping but that's quite possible.

runners.comment: Bred to stay well but sharp enough to win over 6f on debut; excuses since; handicap debut
runners.spotlight: Bred to stay further than 1m but was sharp enough to win 6f Newbury novice (good to firm) on debut; found wanting in two later runs but in Listed company first and soft ground may not have suited back at Newbury (1m); gelded since; this first handicap looks competitive.

runners.breeder: Stiftung Gestut Fahrhof U Flaxman Stable
runners.comment: Off the mark on third start, a C&D novice in September; open to progress; handicap debut
runners.spotlight: Ran up against smart types on first two 7f starts, on this track and at York (both on good), keeping on pleasingly into third on debut, then ran to similar level next time; was in the right place at the right time, unlike the second, when winning a C&D novice in September; open to improvement as a 3yo; goes handicapping with cheekpieces fitted.

runners.comment: Winning 7f debut; looked sure to be suited by 1m on AW next time but she disappointed
runners.spotlight: Needed every yard of 7f on Ayr debut (good) in August but the further she went the better she looked; the step up to 1m should have suited on Kempton AW in October but she found disappointingly little; returns to action with something to prove.

runners.comment: Won 3 handicaps at about 1m as 2yo but still 12lb higher than for the latest of them
runners.spotlight: Ten 2yo runs, winning three handicaps at about 1m (good to firm, good and soft); took a hefty rise for the latest of them and is now 12lb higher; creditable comeback at Musselburgh recently but surprising if she's well enough treated to win today; yard also runs Strength Of Spirit.

quotes.race: Rowland Family Day Out Nursery Handicap
quotes.quote: She's very tough. I spoke to Karl Burke beforehand and he said Dunkeld Dreamer stays very well, keep the revs up. She was there to be shot at at the four-marker but she dug deep. She was loving the battle, every time one came to her she found more - Shane Gray, jockey.

runners.comment: Ran well in all three handicaps as 2yo, at 7f and 1m; tough to get off the mark today
runners.spotlight: Maiden who ran well in all three handicaps at 7f and 1m, making most when runner-up over this trip at Newmarket (good) in September; this looks a tough race in which to get off the mark; yard also runs Mr Seagull.

stable_tour.quote: He's been knocking on the door so it's been frustrating. He's definitely up to winning off his mark and we'll do everything we can to win with him this year. He's from a family that's a bit quirky - they all know the Withefords quite well for stalls work - but I think he'll improve from two to three. 08-10-25

racecards.verdict: Commanding Officer and Go Rimbaud are interesting but STRENGTH OF SPIRIT has won both his handicaps and can add another.
racecards.betting_forecast: 5/2 Go Rimbaud, 3/1 Strength Of Spirit,  Commanding Officer, 13/2 See Blue, 12/1 Mr Seagull, 14/1 Gold Dawn, 16/1 Dunkeld Dreamer, 20/1 Electrical,  Spiritoftheblues

racecards.race_name: William Hill Each Way Extra Handicap

runners.owner: G H Thompson &  S P C Woods
runners.comment: Good 2nd in an AW handicap 18 days ago; big player if transferring that back to the grass
runners.spotlight: 6f maiden win at Wolverhampton in November; better form when second of 12 in a 6f handicap at Southwell 18 days ago; 1lb higher today but still a key player if able to transfer AW form back to turf.

runners.comment: Makes stable/seasonal/handicap debut off a tough-looking mark; hooded for the first time
runners.spotlight: Two promising 5f runs to begin his career (trained by Adrian Keatley as a 2yo) but he didn't get home over 6f when last seen; gelded and sporting a hood on this seasonal/stable/handicap debut; opening mark not an obvious gift though.

stable_tour.quote: It was probably trainer error running him over 5f and he ran over 6f at Thirsk a couple of weeks ago and he has his mark now. He might go for one of the nurseries at York. He's going to have a big future and I firmly believe he'll end up highly rated. He's such a big, heavy horse and he looked like a sprinter but he's more of a 7f to a mile horse. 07-08-25

runners.comment: 6f AW win in November and several good runs have followed; he has more to prove on turf
runners.spotlight: 6f AW winner in November (form solid) and several good placed runs followed; he has more to prove on turf but he won't be far away if able to transfer his form back to the grass.

runners.comment: Low-key nursery debut here (7f) seven months ago; still has time to do better
runners.spotlight: No immediate improvement for the switch to handicaps when eighth of nine over 7f here seven months ago; his novice and maiden runs had threatened better though and he still has time to fulfil that promise; betting useful.

stable_tour.quote: I really like him. He's shown up really well and will be a cracking horse next year. His runs have been very good apart from his last run at Hamilton, where he raced a bit free and didn't handle the track. He started favourite that night but did it all the wrong way and since then he's been gelded. We've identified a nice nursery for him at Haydock at the end of the month. 10-09-25

runners.comment: Low-key handicap debut (6f, AW) 31 days ago; headgear now tried; others are safer
runners.spotlight: No threat when sixth of seven on her handicap debut at Lingfield (6f, AW) 31 days ago; dropped 3lb and now tried in cheekpieces  but others bring stronger claims.

runners.owner: J Raybould N Skinner D Jenkins
runners.comment: Promise as a 2yo but this is a better race than he was contesting when last seen
runners.spotlight: Failed to win in five 2yo runs but has shown ability on both AW and turf; this is a deeper race than he was contesting when last seen though.

stable_tour.quote: A very nice horse who hasn't run since finishing third on his debut at Redcar in May. He chipped his tibia and had to have the summer off. He's back cantering now and will go on the all-weather in November. 01-10-25

runners.comment: Needs to come on for this month's reappearance but not out of it on his 2yo best
runners.spotlight: Followed August's 6f win at Nottingham with two solid efforts over 7f; down the field on this month's return to action at Kempton but that should have sharpened him up and he is feasibly weighted.

runners.comment: Ended 2025 with two low-key runs; blinkers added for his return; drops back to 6f
runners.spotlight: Second of seven on his nursery debut last July (7f, good to firm) but that was followed by two lacklustre efforts (gelded before latest); back down in trip for his reappearance and goes in blinkers for the first time.

runners.comment: Returns to handicap company off a reduced mark; has C&D form; no accessories today
runners.spotlight: Eight of her nine runs have come in novice/maiden company but her one handicap run saw her finish second over C&D last July off an 8lb higher mark; returns from an 86-day break without any accessories; betting useful.

runners.breeder: Mr & Mrs C Booth & Mrs S Cammidge
runners.owner: Pcf Racing Ltd Ceramic Tile Merchants
runners.comment: 0-6 but ran a good race when second at Bath (5f, good) three weeks ago; major contender
runners.spotlight: Six-race maiden but she went close at Bath (5f, good) three weeks ago on her return from a six-month absence; returning to 6f should be fine and she is not fully exposed just yet; major contender.

runners.comment: More encouragement to be gleaned from recent AW 4th; headgear added today; one to consider
runners.spotlight: More encouraging signs with his staying-on fourth of 13 at Newcastle (6f) 12 days ago; dropped 2lb for his troubles and now has headgear added for the first time; could have a bigger effort lurking.

runners.comment: 2yo campaign fizzled out but he starts out for his new stable off a reduced mark
runners.spotlight: Early promise for James Horton last season but his campaign rather fizzled out; starts out for a new trainer (sold for 5,000gns in October) off a reduced mark; worth a market check.

runners.comment: Needs the new headgear/return to 6f to give him a lift judged on his 2yo exploits
runners.spotlight: Ended his 2yo campaign with a couple of creditable runs in 7f AW nurseries; drops back to 6f for his seasonal return and with blinkers enlisted (wore cheekpieces final 2yo run); others look stronger.

racecards.verdict: Full Gas could benefit from headgear but this could be the day for JENNY JEROME to shed her maiden tag.
racecards.betting_forecast: 3/1 Paranjape, 9/2 Flash Rascal, 6/1 Whiskey Kisses,  Jenny Jerome, 9/1 Black Endeavour, 10/1 Adalida, 11/1 Full Gas, 12/1 Stoic Poet,  Houndhill,  John Barleycorn, 16/1 G'Emmethegreenlite, 40/1 Call Me By My Name,  Ellie's de Vega

runners.comment: Not gone on from Chelmsford 3rd in October but several factors that point to better today
runners.spotlight: Promising return to action at Chelmsford in October (6f) and that was off a 6lb higher mark; no progress since but 7f has stretched him on his last two starts and he returns to 6f in a lower grade; big player with cheekpieces added for the first time.

runners.owner: The Good Racing Company Ltd & Partner

prev_owners.owner: The Childe Of Hale The Good Racing Co

runners.comment: 7f win last summer; failed to build on it after and drops back in trip after 172 days off
runners.spotlight: Strong at the finish when winning a 7f handicap at Doncaster last summer (good to soft); three lesser efforts followed and he returns from his 172 break over a trip that may be too sharp; he is drawn near some good pace though and looks worth a market check.

runners.comment: Struggled in handicaps following a 6f AW novice win; drops into a 0-70 on his return
runners.spotlight: Won a 6f novice at Newcastle on his second start last summer; handicaps have proved more troublesome but he is edging down the weights and now drops into 0-70 company for the first time.

runners.owner: S Thompson, Mrs R Carr & G Shields

prev_owners.owner: S Thompson And Mrs R Carr

runners.comment: Good 3rd at Thirsk two weeks ago; solid contender off the same mark
runners.spotlight: No win on turf since September 2024 but he ran well for third at Thirsk (6f, good) two weeks ago, form that has been boosted by the winner and second running well in big fields since; one to be interested in off the same mark.

stable_tour.quote: He's another to have had a winter's break and he's not quite ready to come back yet - he's about a month away. He won't find things so easy when he returns because he's only 1lb below his highest ever mark, but that's the price of success because he won two races in the autumn. He's a straightforward sprinter, though, and always gives his best. 09-04-25

prev_owners.owner: Mrs J A Wakefield And Partner

runners.comment: Two Class 6 wins over 6f at Southwell this year; only fourth off this mark 20 days ago
runners.spotlight: The winner of two of his six starts this year, both over 6f at Southwell; he could only manage fourth of the nine runners back at Southwell 20 days ago and he will need to raise his game to defy this mark.

quotes.race: Sky Bet Sunday Series Sprint Handicap
quotes.quote: Good Earth ran at Goodwood on unraceable ground in the Stewards' Cup and they called the meeting off after that and Yarmouth was on the dead side and today was more on the ground that he likes. We know he jumps the stalls well, but we weren't expecting him to jump that well. We half expected to take a lead of Tom Marquand's horse (Get It) and sit maybe fifth or sixth and come with a run and see how far we have got. I've put him in the Ayr Gold Cup, but it depends on the ground and if it soft that would be a bit stiff. There is a race at York on Saturday but that might come too soon. The Portland would be a race for him and he only just missed getting in last year, but that would be a race for him - Michael Herrington, trainer.

quotes.race: cavani.co.uk The Sartorial Sprint Handicap
quotes.quote: Good Earth loves a stiff five furlongs as he has won at Beverley and run well at Sandown. I think a stiff five probably suits him better than an easy six as he can sometimes over race a bit early. The top horses probably came out of the race which made it a little bit easier for us, but he has done it well. We've got some good races to go to war at.  There is the Sunday Series, and he has won one of them already so we might get greedy and go for another one of them. I've put him in the Stewards' Cup, but that is an easy six with a stiff finish. I'm in the Racing League as well in the Yorkshire team with Leonna Mayor and hopefully she might put me in one of them races as they are worth a good bit - Michael Herrington, trainer.

prev_owners.owner: Mps Racing, The Olliers, S Perkins

runners.comment: Not beaten far at Bath three weeks ago (5f, good); Tom Marquand booked; each-way shout
runners.spotlight: Conditions shouldn't be an excuse and he didn't run badly at Bath (5f, good) three weeks ago after a short break; Tom Marquand a notable booking; each-way shout.

stable_tour.quote: He's been a bit unlucky not to win more than once this year and the handicapper has probably got hold of him. He'll run on the all-weather as he likes Newcastle, provided it's not riding too deep. The jockey says he wants 6f, whereas the trainer says 5f. 01-10-25

runners.comment: Chance on his best efforts this year and the return to a straight track may help
runners.spotlight: Prominent racer; close second at Newcastle (6f) last month but he failed to back it up at Southwell three weeks ago; all his best efforts have come on a straight course so perhaps can be given the benefit of the doubt for last time; one of two runners for the stable; not discounted.

quotes.race: Carol Simpson Legacy Handicap (Div I)
quotes.quote: It was absolutely brilliant with Andalprofit. He was on the far side, which was a big advantage, and he was given a great ride by Alex. He did win very easily last year at Newcastle and he's bounced back today - Nigel Tinkler, trainer.

quotes.race: Gamble Responsibly At BetMGM Handicap
quotes.quote: Andalprofit did run okay last year but he was quite weak and just needed a lot of time. I'm surprised he won as well as he did but he is a nice horse and hopefully he can go on - Nigel Tinkler, trainer, speaking to Sky Sports Racing.

stable_tour.quote: We thought he was going to be a nice horse but he's been a bit disappointing. He ran very well at Haydock in May and we thought he was ready to win again but he hasn't since. He's a bit of a worrier who's lost confidence in himself. We'll have to work to build it up, but he can bounce back - he goes on Thursday . 01-10-25

runners.comment: Knocking at the door on AW (6f/7f) this year; another bold bid likely back on turf
runners.spotlight: Knocking at the door over 6f and 7f on AW this year; won't mind getting back on turf and he should give it another good go from the front.

stable_tour.quote: He has been a nice horse for connections with seven wins to his name. I am desperate for some rain for him as the softer the better. He cannot handle it quick or even good for that matter - he loves it when the mud is flying. We will have him ready for when he gets his conditions and is one to keep on your side when the ground eases considerably. 03-08-22

runners.comment: Modest form in sprint novice events last year but may leave that behind now handicapping
runners.spotlight: No better than midfield in three sprint novice runs in the latter part of 2025 and his opening mark looks tough on that evidence; looks the type his trainer will do well with now handicapping though and a much more prominent showing could be on the cards.

runners.comment: Two 6f wins at Newcastle this year; too free back there on Monday; up in class today
runners.spotlight: It took a drop into classified company for him to return to winning ways in February (6f, AW; blinkered first time; final run for John Butler); gained a second Newcastle win of the year last month but he raced far too freely back there on Monday; up in class today and likely vulnerable.

racecards.verdict: Cherry Cobbler is intriguing on his turf debut but FISCAL POLICY ran well at Thirsk two weeks ago and edges preference.
racecards.betting_forecast: 9/4 Fiscal Policy, 9/2 Dandy Dinmont, 6/1 Good Earth, 7/1 Cherry Cobbler, 10/1 The Childe Of Hale,  Punchbowl Flyer, 12/1 Judicature,  Andalprofit, 14/1 Harry Mole,  Sedgemoor, 33/1 Margorie

racecards.race_name: Juddmonte EBF Restricted Maiden Stakes (Bands B/C/D) (EBF Qualifier) (GBB/IRE Incentive Race)

runners.comment: Didn't live up to market expectations at Newbury but he should know much more this time
runners.spotlight: January foal; £55,000 yearling; didn't live up to market expectations when seventh on Newbury debut (good; 7-2) last week but he ran green after a slow start; should know much more this time and it wouldn't be a surprise if he took a major step forward.

runners.owner: Heart Of The South Racing 146 & Partner
runners.comment: £24,000 yearling; has plenty of stamina in pedigree and could be a longer-term prospect
runners.spotlight: 32,000euros foal, £24,000 yearling; first foal; dam unraced sister to winners Rhythmic Intent (useful 1m2f-14.5f) and Fortune Triple (HK 1m1f/1m3f), is granddaughter of French Oaks winner Caerlina; has plenty of stamina on dam's side and he could be a longer-term prospect.

runners.comment: Well backed into 3-1 at Wolverhampton but he never got involved; needs improvement
runners.spotlight: 10,000gns February foal; well backed into 3-1 at Wolverhampton (AW) two weeks ago but he never got involved before finishing a well-held fourth of seven; should benefit from that experience but he needs plenty of progress on this switch to turf.

runners.comment: Has speed and stamina in pedigree and interesting to see how he figures in market
runners.spotlight: Ardad colt; third foal; dam 9.4f/1m2f winner (including 2yo; RPR 87), half-sister to 1m Listed winner Staying On, out of maiden half-sister to Rockfel winner Yawl, family of Oaks winner Talent; has speed and stamina in pedigree and interesting to see how he figures in market.

runners.comment: Has speedy pedigree and she needs a close look for yard that that won this race last year
runners.spotlight: February foal; 15,000gns foal, 42,000euros yearling; fifth foal; half-brother to 6f AW winner Black Cab (RPR 56); dam 6f winner (86), sister to 5f/6f Group 3 winner Swiss Diva, half-sister to 5f Group 3 winner Swiss Spirit, out of 5f Listed winner; has lots of speed in pedigree and she's an interesting newcomer for yard that that won this race last year.

runners.comment: Showed ability behind a useful prospect at Thirsk; key player if he can build on that
runners.spotlight: Ran green and hung left from halfway but he was only just run out of third on his debut at Thirsk (good) two weeks ago; that was an encouraging start behind a useful prospect and he's a key player if he can build on that.

runners.comment: £44,000 yearling; yard 2-3 with 2yos this season and she needs a close look on debut
runners.spotlight: 35,000euros foal, £44,000 yearling; Kodiac filly who is closely related to 7f AW 2yo winner Dynamite Katie (RPR 78); dam unraced half-sister to French 1m4f Listed winner Balaythous and useful 7f-1m1f winner Saphirside; yard 2-3 with 2yos this season and she needs a close look on debut.

runners.comment: 4,000gns yearling; could be one for later on and he's probably best watched on debut
runners.spotlight: March foal; 30,000gns foal, 4,000gns yearling; half-brother to winners Bill Silvers (7f; RPR 99) and Gaelic Approach (1m4f; 77); dam placed 1m-1m4f (78), half-sister to 1m4f winners Empyrea and La Joya; could be one for later on and he's probably best watched on debut.

runners.comment: Big market drifter at Wolverhampton and he finished a remote sixth of seven
runners.spotlight: Big market drifter at Wolverhampton (AW; 11-1) two weeks ago and he finished into a remote sixth of seven; should be more streetwise this time but he needs a transformation on his second start.

runners.comment: Yard 20% with 2yos last season and he needs a close look on debut
runners.spotlight: February foal; Land Force half-brother to winners Tribal Craft (1m2f-1m6f including Group 3; RPR 110), Seattle King (7f 2yo/1m2f; 90), Star Maker (11.6f Flat, 81; 2m-2m3f hurdle) and Dream Seeker (German 6.5f); dam 1m/1m2f winner (93); yard has had a 2yo winner this season and had a 20% record with juveniles last term.

runners.comment: 15,000gns yearling; others look more likely and he's probably best watched on debut
runners.spotlight: March foal; 7,000euros foal, 15,000euros yearling; first foal of a 7f 2yo winner (RPR 97), out of French 10.5f winning half-sister to 1m1f Flat and 2m-2m3f hurdle/chase winner Authentic Act; others look more likely and he's best watched unless market suggests otherwise.

runners.comment: 16-1 at Bath three weeks ago and she finished a remote eighth of ten
runners.spotlight: 1,000gns yearling; 16-1 at Bath (good) three weeks ago and she dropped out before before finishing a remote eighth of ten.

racecards.verdict: Clive Cox's won this last year and he may be able to repeat the trick with SKY SECRET who has plenty of speed in his good pedigree.
racecards.betting_forecast: 5/2 Sky Secret, 4/1 Indian Land, 13/2 From Me To You,  Mr Macartney, 8/1 Donegal Rose, 10/1 Parading,  Turnstile, 16/1 Alpha Legend,  Everatease, 25/1 Top Cote,  Postcard, 66/1 Allaboutthelunch

racecards.race_name: Caffreys Black Stout King Richard III Cup Handicap

runners.comment: Group 3 winner over 6f last autumn and he has possibilities back in a handicap
runners.spotlight: Ended last season with a game win in Group 3 at Ascot (6f, soft) in October; repeatedly met trouble when only seventh in Saudi Arabia (a race he'd won two years earlier) in February and things didn't really go his way again in a Listed race at Doncaster last month; has possibilities on this drop back in class and his last handicap win was off 1lb higher.

quotes.race: John Guest Racing Bengough Stakes (Group 3)
quotes.quote: Annaf has come back to form now, which is great to see. I've not been that happy with his work but he's very talented and he's been getting back to where he normally was. We just freshened him up and did a few different things. We'll see where we go now with him now. He could possibly go abroad to Saudi for the race he won last year - Mick Appleby, trainer.

quotes.race: Saudi National Bank 1351 Turf Sprint (Group 2) (4yo+) (Inner Track) (Turf)
quotes.quote: It's all down to Rossa, not my training. Anaaf keeps improving and keeps surprising us. Where we go next, God knows, but he's got that invitation to Japan and we'll possibly go there. These big meetings are becoming quite a habit really. It really feels like the sky's the limit. These international wins mean so much because it really does put the yard on the map -  Mick Appleby, trainer.

quotes.race: John Guest Racing Bengough Stakes (Group 3)
quotes.quote: I love everything about Annaf. He's something else and he loved getting shifted about and being taken off his racing line today. He's really thriving and you have to give it to Mick Appleby and his team. He's been on the go since the start of the year and has not missed one beat - Rossa Ryan, jockey.
