quotes.race: Betfred Portland (Heritage Handicap)
quotes.quote: Annaf has been a star to me this year. My only concern was the ground and I knew the race was going to be ridden to suit him perfectly. He's a classy horse and a lot of people are forgetting he was third in the King's Stand and I'd imagine one of those nice Group races will fall for him. To do this off topweight on ground he didn't like, took some doing - Rossa Ryan, jockey.

quotes.race: BetUK Kachy Stakes (Listed Race) (All-Weather Championships Fast-Track Qualifier)
quotes.quote: It wasn't the plan to miss the break like that with Annaf but he did it well in the end. The plan is to go straight to all-weather finals day at Newcastle, although he could be a nice horse on turf later on - Mick Appleby, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: We bought him out of Owen Burrows' yard as an unraced two-year-old and he has taken his time to get there. He won twice on the all-weather last year and ran some fine races on turf without winning, but he has really thrived on the all-weather this winter. After a break we brought him back in January at Lingfield, where he won over 6f, and he has since added to that with wins at Kempton and in the Listed Kachy Stakes at Lingfield. Clearly he has improved with age and, although he has risen to a mark of 108, there may be a little more to come and I'd hope to campaign him similarly this summer to last. Before he resumes on the grass he'll go for the 6f race at the all-weather finals meeting on Good Friday, where I hope he'll be hard to beat. 22-03-23

runners.comment: Record of 5-12 but he was down the field at Newcastle last time; needs more after a break
runners.spotlight: Record of 5-10 for Harry Charlton and his last win was in a conditions event at Kempton (6f, AW) in October; ran without his declared tongue-tie when fourth on stable debut at Southwell in January but he finished down the field in another Class 2 handicap at Newcastle two weeks later; conditions should be fine on this return to turf but he needs to step up again after another break.

quotes.race: Wokingham Stakes (Heritage Handicap)
quotes.quote: Ten Pounds has run huge, first time back at six [furlongs]. Trevor thought he had the winner in his sights two down. I think in a normal year horses do stop - it's hard to make the running here. I suspect looking at the Jersey, they're not making up ground quite as much. Some of the jockeys were suggesting it's just a bit loose from watering. He's run huge, very happy with him - Harry Charlton, trainer.

runners.comment: Four wins last year but his progress seems to have flattened out; others preferred
runners.spotlight: Won four times during a progressive campaign last year but he's come up short in Listed/Group 3 events this spring; seems ideally suited by fast ground but he's still 4lb higher than for his last win and has some work to do back in a handicap.

quotes.race: Bet Boost At bet365 Handicap (Heritage Handicap)
quotes.quote: I think Prince Of India is ready to step up in class and once he gets some more give in the ground he'll appreciate that too. I think he's fast enough for this distance and as he gets stronger he will develop into a real sprinter. I do think there's more to come - Marco Botti, trainer.

runners.owner: Middleham Park Racing Xii & Mrs G Cowell
runners.comment: Fair efforts in two runs for new yard and he could be dangerous back up in trip
runners.spotlight: Listed winner (5f/6f) for his previous yards and he's run respectably in two 5f handicaps for his new trainer this spring; needs to find some extra spark but he's edging down the weights and this step back up in trip looks a good move.

quotes.race: Dragon Stakes (Listed Race)
quotes.quote: Kylian has been quite a slow learner. Karl always thought he was a good horse, and he was surprised when he got beat at York first time out, but he is probably just a slow learner and he is learning through his racing. Hopefully he will go on to better things. Ryan thinks he could possibly get six furlongs and that is another avenue. The Molecomb could possibly be next - Philip Robinson, assistant racing manager to the owner.

stable_tour.quote: This colt has been showing up well at home and is ready to go now. He has been doing everything we have asked and looks nice, and he is ready to run. 07-05-23

runners.comment: Held in hat-trick bid at Kempton but he still has potential and is not ruled back on turf
runners.spotlight: Dual turf winner who made it 2-2 on AW when completing a double at Newcastle (6f; off 4lb lower) last month; didn't fire in his hat-trick bid at Kempton but he still has potential and is not ruled out in suitable conditions back on turf.

quotes.race: Midnite AWC Sprint Trial Handicap
quotes.quote: Fast Track Harry looks to have improved and matured. That was a solid step forward on the all-weather for the first time. It was a very pleasing comeback. We'd need to run a few more times to qualify for the All-Weather Championships and I'm not sure we'd look to do that. It might be a bit tight but we've won a good prize here - Clive Cox, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: He showed promise last year when he made a winning debut at Newbury, then found the ground a little too soft when we ran him in a Listed race at Doncaster. He's a big, strong horse and is coming to the boil nicely now. We're looking forward to seeing him again. 17-04-25

runners.owner: Berkshire Parts & Panels Ltd No1 Fanclub
runners.comment: Placed off this mark at Newcastle latest and he's still unexposed on turf; in the mix
runners.spotlight: Completed an AW hat-trick when scoring on his handicap debut at Newcastle (6f) last April; held in six subsequent runs but he went close off this mark at Southwell in November and was a creditable third at Newcastle three weeks ago; now returns to turf but he ran well in a fast-ground Listed event last spring and he's still unexposed in this sphere; in the mix.

quotes.race: BetMGM All-Weather 3 Year Old Championships Handicap
quotes.quote: That was brilliant. Oisin gave Berkshire Whisper a peach of a ride and that was real class. I think he's got a lot to give. He could go for the Commonwealth Cup. He may have one more run just to be sure, we don't want to make ourselves look stupid, then I think we'll be there - Paul Spickett, owner.

runners.comment: Chester specialist who is not easy to predict and others are preferred
runners.spotlight: Well handicapped on his best form last season but he's not easy to predict and has been up and down during another spell in Bahrain since December; comes with risks attached back in Britain and most of his wins have been at Chester; tongue-tie worn last time is removed.

quotes.race: Queensferry Stakes (Listed Race)
quotes.quote: Roman Dragon is an absolute star and it was a first-class ride by Jason [Watson]. He read the race supremely well, but the horse was very tough. Turning in I thought we were going to win by even further as we were going so well. He loves it here and he's a sprint handicapper who pulled it out of the bag in a stakes race. I'm not sure he can go to a much higher level than this, but he's turned his love for this track into a massive advantage. He goes so well here and that's worth half a dozen pounds ? it was probably the difference today. Chester made a nice rug for him and he's a history maker - Hugo Palmer, trainer.

quotes.race: CAA Stellar Handicap
quotes.quote: Roman Dragon loves Chester. That's now six wins here for this horse, which has equalled the modern-day track record. We had a nice enough draw [five] and everything went perfectly - Hugo Palmer, trainer.

quotes.race: Grey Goose Essences Handicap
quotes.quote: Nick (Hughes, part-owner)'s ambition is for Roman Dragon to become the winningmost horse around Chester and we think he needs six. We're two-thirds of the way there. I'm delighted, he won off 84 last year and 79 here so maybe we can get another before the season's out - Hugo Palmer, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: He's such a star and has had two good winters in Bahrain. He has a higher rating than he's ever won off, although he did come agonisingly close a couple of times last summer, but I don't think winning off this mark is out of the question. He loves Chester and will go to the May meeting. 09-04-25

He's just an absolute joy. He's the winningmost horse at Chester after two more wins there this season. He's that lucky individual who hasn't seen an English winter for a few years and he's heading back to Bahrain. The handicapper dropped him a couple of pounds for a below-par effort on very soft ground in the Portland, which means he'll get a run or two before he has to step up in grade out there. He's had three fantastic winters there now - he was the series winner this year having been second last year. He's that rare thing - a racehorse who pays for himself. 08-10-25

runners.comment: C&D winner who scored on AW in November but he needs more progress to defy this mark
runners.spotlight: C&D winner who ended his 2025 campaign with a success and creditable effort over 5f at Newcastle (AW); was as good as ever in those two runs but he was well below form on his reappearance at Pontefract (5f, good to soft) 18 days ago; may have needed that run but he needs more progress to defy this mark.

stable_tour.quote: We liked him a lot last year and he looked good when winning on his return last week. We gelded him and it's probably been the making of him. He's a big, scopey horse and physically he's improved again. He likes top of the ground and there are plenty of races for him at Newmarket, including a three-year-old six-furlong race on Guineas weekend. 14-04-25

runners.comment: Returns after wind surgery but has mixed record when fresh and his last win was in 2023
runners.spotlight: Two 5f wins for Roger Varian but latest was in June 2023 and he was quiet last season; returns for new yard after wind surgery but he has a mixed record when fresh and this is highly competitive; down the list.

quotes.race: Market Cross Jewellers Handicap
quotes.quote: Russet Gold is a classy horse, a half-brother to Daahyeh who I won the Albany on. He'll stay six furlongs but his quality got him through the race - David Egan, jockey.

stable_tour.quote: There's no reason to think he won't keep improving with age and I'd love to place him to win a Listed race. He should be ready to start in the second half of May. 11-04-25

runners.comment: Reliable type who is very effective on fast ground and he's respected back from a break
runners.spotlight: Ran creditably at Lingfield in January when bidding for a 6f AW double; 8lb higher than when second at Newmarket (7f) on last turf attempt but he's proved consistent since being gelded and his first two handicap wins were on good to firm; in the mix.

quotes.race: Midnite Aint Your Grandads Bookie Handicap
quotes.quote: It was a perfect trip round. Zoulu Chief jumped to make the running and there was plenty of speed on, so I was happy to sit; he picked up nicely - Billy Loughnane, jockey.

runners.comment: 1-26 on turf but he's been in good form on AW and he's on lower mark back in this sphere
runners.spotlight: Four-time AW winner who has finished close up on Tapeta (5f/6f) in his last three runs; record of 1-26 on turf but he's on a lower mark in this sphere and he ran well in the Great St Wilfrid at Ripon (6f, good to firm) last summer; dangerous.

quotes.race: JenningsBet 200 Shops Nationwide Handicap
quotes.quote: We've not had Fivethousandtoone too long, we've been trying to figure him out. Arguably his best form is at Newcastle, held up, and it all worked perfectly for him today. There was a bit of a headwind and he got plenty of cover - David Allan, jockey.

quotes.race: BetUK All-Weather Sprint Handicap
quotes.quote: Today it all came together and hopefully it will be the beginning of a decent season for Fivethousandtoone. He was good last time and better today - Oisin Murphy, jockey.

quotes.race: William Hill Best Odds Guaranteed Handicap
quotes.quote: Fivethousandtoone has run well without winning. The race worked out well for him today, waiting with him and coming late. That's his level - William Buick, rider.

stable_tour.quote: He was a very smart juvenile, winning over 6f before finishing second in the Mill Reef Stakes and mid-division over 7f in the Dewhurst Stakes. He had a setback earlier this year but that has been resolved and he is now back in fast work. The plan is to go straight to Royal Ascot for the Commonwealth Cup. He is a very smart horse who looks very together this year and is one I am excited about getting back on the track. 19-05-21

runners.comment: Second in Stewards' Cup last summer and runner-up at Newcastle 12 days ago; respected
runners.spotlight: On lengthy losing but he's a smart handicapper on his day and he returned from five months off with a good third at Newcastle (6f, AW) two weeks ago; should benefit from that run and he remains well treated on his second in the Stewards' Cup last August; interesting contender.

quotes.race: Coral Sprint Trophy Handicap (Heritage Handicap)
quotes.quote: Strike Red had a bad injury last year that you wouldn't really see on Flat horses and more on jumpers. He's been better than ever this year and this worked out easily enough. I always told Richard [Fahey, trainer] he feels like a Group horse and he's a top-end handicapper. There's plenty still to look forward to - Billy Garritty, jockey.

quotes.race: Paddy Power Scurry Handicap (Premier Handicap)
quotes.quote: Strike Red has been a good horse for me. He keeps winning these big handicaps so I'm absolutely delighted. I didn't think Ripon really suited him the last day.  When he gets there he doesn't do a lot. He pricks his earls a little bit - Billy Garritty, rider

runners.comment: In good form on AW but this is a step back up in grade and his sole turf win was in 2024
runners.spotlight: Won on stable debut at Southwell (6f, Tapeta) in November and he's posted some solid efforts since then; hard to rule out another good run but this is a step back up in grade and sole turf win was 19 months ago.

racecards.verdict: Plenty have possibilities but the well handicapped STRIKE RED gets the vote ahead of Fast Track Harry and Annaf.
racecards.betting_forecast: 11/2 Fast Track Harry, 6/1 Strike Red, 13/2 Berkshire Whisper,  Zoulu Chief, 7/1 Prince Of India, 8/1 Ten Pounds,  Fivethousandtoone, 10/1 Russet Gold, 14/1 Kylian,  Dark Cloud Rising, 16/1 Annaf, 20/1 Betsen, 25/1 Roman Dragon

runners.comment: Clear winner at Bath (extended 5f) last week; 6lb higher but this mark is not beyond him
runners.spotlight: Has a better strike-rate on AW than turf but he's capable of useful 6f form on grass and made short work of his rivals at Bath (extended 5f, good) last week; now 6lb higher but this mark isn't beyond him on past exploits; would have welcomed rain but still considered.

prev_owners.owner: Ursa Major Racing Ltd And G Tuer

runners.comment: 2-2 over C&D, pulling well clear 12 days ago (good); needs to defy a 9lb rise
runners.spotlight: Winner of both C&D starts, in October (good to soft) and when pulling well clear (good) 12 days ago; has won on good to firm so the warm weather shouldn't be a problem but the new 9lb higher mark might be.

quotes.race: Ripon Yorkshire's Garden Racecourse Handicap
quotes.quote: Wreck It Ryley has done it well. I was just waiting for the gap to appear. He's run in blinkers a few times before and they do help him because he's a bit behind the bridle normally. He keeps breaking half a stride too slowly, but he's soon there on the heels of the leaders and he was there when I needed him. I had plenty of horse underneath me to commit and go - Dale Swift, jockey, speaking to Sky Sports Racing.

stable_tour.quote: He has been a busy lad this season with 14 runs and two wins. On his latest start at Ayr they virtually trotted to the three-furlong marker before sprinting. He wasn't best positioned for that but he came home well to win and has gone up only 2lb for it, which I thought was fair. I'm hopeful he can add to his successes again this season [ran at Musselburgh on Tuesday night after the Weekender went to press]. 30-08-23

runners.comment: 1-1 over C&D; lacks recent run but weighted to go well on best 6f form on good to firm
runners.spotlight: Weighted to go well on best turf form and the drying ground shouldn't cause her any grief, having run so well on good to firm at York (6f) last June; also a winner of her one C&D start, in 2023, and the booking of Billy Loughnane signals intent; has prospects despite lacking a recent run.

stable_tour.quote: She won four times over the winter for us at Southwell and was placed a number of times too. She's having a break and we'll look to go for some nice prize-money pots, possibly in search of some black type too. I think on the right day if the race is run to suit, there's still a bit more to come from her. She stays 7f but is seen to best effect at 6f as she needs a good pace to aim at. 23-04-25

runners.comment: Won at Newmarket (good to soft) in November; well beaten in this race on return last year
runners.spotlight: Said goodbye to 2025 with a Newmarket win (6f, good to soft) in November; has won on good to firm but he missed a recent intended return on the surface and this might be needed anyway (soundly beaten here last April).

prev_owners.owner: Thurloe Royal Marsden Cancer Charity II

runners.comment: Well treated when winning 3 of last 4 on AW/turf (6f) in 2025; good turf run in UAE latest
runners.spotlight: Had ups and downs since showing decent form earlier in career and was well treated when starting out for this trainer in 2025, winning three of his last four 6f starts on AW and turf; went down only narrowly back on turf (good to firm; headgear left off) in UAE during March and he's of interest now back with former yard.

quotes.race: Try Unibet's New Smartview Racecards Handicap (London Sprint Series Qualifier)
quotes.quote: Newmarket the last day didn't work - a straight track and no cover - Dapper Valley needs cover and he got it today. He feels like he's a horse on the upgrade and I don't think he's finished winning yet - Paddy Bradley, jockey, speaking to Racing TV.

quotes.race: Dubai Duty Free Golf World Cup EBF Maiden Stakes (Newcomers' Race) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: I was worried about running Dapper Valley on the ground, but he's always shown up a good bit at home and I loved the way he travelled. He took it in his stride and could be a very good two-year-old. I imagine we'll look at something else - possibly a race back here at the Lockinge meeting - before he is hopefully a Royal Ascot horse -  Richard Hannon, trainer.

runners.comment: Back on the same mark as Windsor win (6f, good to firm) last June; first run on this track
runners.spotlight: Should be all the better for her Doncaster reappearance and she's back on the same mark as for her Windsor success (6f, good to firm) last June; however, all her turf wins have come there and at Salisbury and this is the first time she's run on this track.

quotes.race: Colin Ponting Memorial Handicap
quotes.quote: Under The Twilight likes Salisbury, but I don't know why. If it had been seven furlongs I wouldn't have run her. She's very gutsy and is a credit to herself - Michael Blake, trainer.

quotes.race: William Hill Epic Value Handicap
quotes.quote: I didn't know what Under The Twilight would do on turf because all of her form is on the all-weather, but she's been keen around Wolverhampton and I thought a strong gallop would help her. I was adamant six furlongs was right. No-one else thought so, apart from David Probert, who has ridden her recently. A flat-out stiff six is perfect for her I think - Michael Blake, trainer.

runners.comment: Smart 2yo; humdrum form in three turf handicaps, way back at Bath last week
runners.spotlight: Can lead; smart 2yo who began 3yo season on a mark of 102; has shown just humdrum form in three turf handicaps, despite a sliding mark, and was way back behind Justcallmepete at Bath last week; has it to prove now.

racecards.verdict: This can go to DAPPER VALLEY (nap) who looked ahead of his mark on the AW in the autumn and that's certainly the case on his old form.
racecards.betting_forecast: 3/1 Wreck It Ryley, 100/30 Dapper Valley, 9/2 Under The Twilight, 5/1 Justcallmepete, 6/1 Ormolulu, 9/1 Dashing Dick, 10/1 Mr Lightside

runners.comment: 0-15 but had two close calls over 6f on AW this year; acts on turf and may well figure
runners.spotlight: Not yet off the mark but she's had two close calls on the AW this year, notably when only just failing to get up at Wolverhampton (6f) in February, against one on the fifth leg of a seven-timer; acts on turf, too, and may well figure back from short break.

runners.comment: Two sprint wins (good to soft and heavy) for new yard in the autumn; can find more
runners.spotlight: Well held on AW in November but progressive on turf for new yard previously, following a close second at Yarmouth (6f, good) with wins there (good to soft) and at Bath (extended 5f, heavy); may well do better on good to firm as her dam's best form for this yard came on the same going.

runners.comment: Three wins in 2024; mostly underpowered in 2025 but now 10lb lower than last April
runners.spotlight: Three wins in 2024, at 7f and 5f; mostly rather underpowered in 2025 and no obvious sign fitting headgear was a help in the autumn, but he's 10lb lower than on reappearance last April so there is handicapping hope.

runners.comment: Two AW wins in 2026; long time since he's run well on turf but not out of it on past form
runners.spotlight: Two AW wins in January, over 6f and 7f; just averagely handicapped now and it's a long time since he's run well on turf but he wouldn't be out of it on past form on grass.

quotes.race: Floodlit Fridays At Dundalk Handicap (Div I)
quotes.quote: Von Krolock wants good ground and he loved it out there tonight. He's an ideal horse for here over the winter and there is plenty of improvement in him - Tim Doyle, trainer.

runners.comment: Lightly raced maiden; not disgraced over 5f latest; down 3lb; can do better back at 6f
runners.spotlight: Lightly raced maiden for two yards but he didn't get the best of runs after a slow start at Bath (first 5f run; good) and may well be ready to play more of a part now back at 6f following a further 3lb drop.

prev_owners.owner: Mrs J E Mulhern & David S McGuinness

runners.comment: Close 2nd on AW return; well held since but chance on strong-finishing 3rd here last year
runners.spotlight: Both turf wins on Brighton's sharp track but she made up plenty of ground when a never-nearer third in this race (good) last year and it wouldn't surprise to see her return to form after a low-key Southwell run last time, having gone close there on her reappearance the time before.

runners.owner: David Tate, Danny Lawson & Kevin Broadley

prev_owners.owner: David Tate, Danny Lawson & Kevin Broadley

runners.comment: Well beaten in 2 turf handicaps in 2025; broke duck on AW in March; may do better on grass
runners.spotlight: Well beaten in two turf handicaps either side of a break in 2025 but he was off the mark on the AW in March and has run respectably in defeat since; might well have more to offer on this surface.

prev_owners.owner: New Vision Bloodstock And Miss J R Macey

runners.comment: Likes it here and last 2 wins on this track (7f); needs more on usual reappearance efforts
runners.spotlight: Five turf wins at 6f-7f, the latest two over the latter trip on this track; he's had some excuses for low-key reappearances in the past but it's still a stretch to expect him to be on song for this one.

quotes.race: Tattersalls Ireland Super Auction Sale Stakes (Plus 10 Race)
quotes.quote: Shark Two One is a lovely little horse. I probably got there soon enough but he quickened up well and was maybe getting a bit lonely going to the line - Colin Keane, rider

runners.comment: Sole turf win at 1m2f; three AW wins at 1m/7f; in form but having first 6f run since debut
runners.spotlight: Sole turf win came over 1m2f in 2023 and three subsequent successes have been on the AW (1m and 7f); has continued to run well since the latest of them in February but this is his first 6f run since his debut.

runners.comment: Won 2yo AW maiden; tough in 2025; found some form on AW in March; held latest for new yard
runners.spotlight: Won 2yo AW maiden; his 3yo season never really got going but he was on a much-reduced mark when runner-up on two occasions (7f) in March; well held on yard debut since, though, and likely best watched back on turf.

racecards.verdict: Recent AW winner Von Krolock is respected but CAMELEY DAYS was a progressive 3yo and there's a good chance she can do better yet.
racecards.betting_forecast: 11/4 Von Krolock, 5/1 Instant Bond, 13/2 Just King High, 8/1 Cameley Days,  Call Glory,  Shark Two One, 10/1 Dark Sun,  Dragon God,  Mickey Mongoose, 12/1 Starsong

runners.comment: 875,000gns yearling; striking newcomer and he holds a Derby entry
runners.spotlight: 875,000gns yearling; first foal; dam Listed-placed 1m/8.5f winner (RPR 98), half-sister to winners Bite Of The Cherry (useful 1m5f), Pietra Dura (7f 2yo) and Ever Rigg (1m4f; dam of 1m2f-1m4f Group 1 winner Postponed), out of Moyglare Stud/Lowther winner; interesting newcomer and he holds Derby entry.

stable_tour.quote: He's a second-half-of-the-season horse. He was big and immature last year and I couldn't really get after him, but he's just starting to show up nicely in his work. He probably wants a nice introduction and I thought the ten-furlong novice at Newbury's Greenham meeting would be a good race for him. He'll warm up from there and get better through the year. Who knows how good he is, but I think he's a lovely horse with tons of potential. 01-04-26

runners.comment: 20-1 on Chelmsford debut (1m) in November and he was always in rear; been gelded since
runners.spotlight: 20-1 on Chelmsford debut (1m) in November and he was always in rear; been gelded since and can only be watched on his return.

runners.comment: Sets standard on his debut third at Wolverhampton and he's open to progress upped in trip
runners.spotlight: Brother to 1m/8.5f winner Rowayeh (RPR 94), closely related to 8.6f AW 2yo/1m2f turf Listed winner Falakeyah (106); held in third when odds-on at Wolverhampton (8.6f) in November but he finished well behind two rivals who were ridden more prominently; sets a good standard on that promising effort and he's open to progress upped in trip.

runners.comment: Cost 1,500,000gns as a yearling but he was well held with headgear applied on recent debut
runners.spotlight: Cost 1,500,000gns as a yearling but he's already been gelded and was a remote third with cheekpieces applied on Southwell debut (1m3f, Tapeta) two weeks ago; that was behind a smart prospect but he has quite a bit to find here and others are preferred.

runners.comment: 1,100.000gns yearling; eye-catcher at Newmarket in October and needs close look on return
runners.spotlight: 1,100,000gns yearling; never involved when 3-1 at Newmarket (1m, good) in October but he made some good late headway to finish fourth of seven; that was a promising start and he needs a close look upped in trip on his return.

runners.comment: Brother to smart 7f-1m2f winner Al Mubhir; needs checking in market on debut
runners.spotlight: Fifth foal; brother to 7f-1m2f winner Al Mubhir (including Listed; RPR 115), half-brother to three winners including Yabher (1m-1m4f; 96); dam 7f-1m1f winner (including Group 3; 112); has good standard to aim at on debut but he needs checking in market.

racecards.verdict: An interesting race in which HEYZOOM gets the vote ahead of Superior Choice and the striking newcomer Act Of Generosity.
racecards.betting_forecast: 10/11 Act Of Generosity, 100/30 Superior Choice, 4/1 Heyzoom, 8/1 King Of Thebes, 16/1 Yafreh, 40/1 Astracornus

runners.comment: Won at Chelmsford (1m2f) last month but was only fifth of ten at Wolverhampton last time
runners.spotlight: Off the mark at the sixth attempt when landing a Chelmsford handicap (1m2f, AW) last month; justified support with that convincing win but he was only fifth of ten in his follow-up bid at Wolverhampton (9.4f); has bit to prove again after that and he's struggled in two previous runs on turf.

stable_tour.quote: He's one for readers to follow on the Flat as he's very well handicapped on a mark of 57. He's going to run on March 12 at Chelmsford and we'd be disappointed if he didn't win that. He was unlucky not to win at Wolverhampton last time when he had trouble in running and finished third. Anywhere from a mile to 1m4f will suit and he's definitely worth following. 04-03-26

runners.comment: Bumper winner who is lightly raced on the Flat and could be dangerous back up in trip
runners.spotlight: Bumper winner and a fair maiden hurdler; 0-6 on the Flat but he was a good third in a Chelmsford handicap (1m6f) in February and the drop to back to 8.6f looked against him at Wolverhampton last time; should get a good tow into this race and he could be dangerous back up in trip.

runners.breeder: R Hyland, J T Heffernan & P Hyland
runners.comment: 7yo who has lost her way and has form figures of 9050876 for current yard; opposable
runners.spotlight: Ex-Kevin Philippart de Foy; formerly a useful performer and was successful at Nottingham (8.3f, good to firm) last April; now 24lb lower than for that win but she's struggled since and has form figures of 9050876 for her current yard; opposable.

quotes.race: British Stallion Studs EBF Fillies' Handicap
quotes.quote: It wasn't too much of a surprise they couldn't get to Yokkell after opening up that lead ? she stays well and had been showing plenty of speed at home - Kevin Philippart De Foy, trainer.

quotes.race: Hovis (Prev. Premier Bakeries Ireland) Mares Maiden Hurdle
quotes.quote: Yokkell is a really nice filly. She has that bit of class and has the aptitude for hurdling. Alex thinks there is plenty of improvement - John McConnell, trainer.

quotes.race: Happy Christmas From All At Dundalk Stadium Handicap
quotes.quote: Yokkell is going to get hit a bit now from the handicapper but is entitled to be. We have trip options and we actually bought her to go jumping and that is something to look forward to in the future - John McConnell, trainer

quotes.race: @Tipperaryraces Apprentice Handicap
quotes.quote: Yokkell has shown a nice turn of foot and has been consistent around that trip in 3yo handicaps. Whether or not she can step up against the older ones, we don't know, but we'll find out as the year progresses. I wouldn't rule out jumping hurdles with her - Jarlath Fahey, trainer.

runners.comment: Well held in three qualifying runs and he needs improvement at new trip on handicap debut
runners.spotlight: Well held in sole start for Andre Fabre in France and same outcome in two runs for new yard this spring; still early days and now goes handicapping but he needs improvement at this new trip.

runners.breeder: Arrow Farm & Stud/Miss A Gibson Fleming
runners.comment: Dual AW winner but he's 0-10 on turf and has something to prove back in this sphere
runners.spotlight: Dual AW winner (1m) but he's 0-10 on turf; on reduced mark and was fair third at Wolverhampton (9.4f) last month but he's struggled in his last five turf runs and has something to prove back in this sphere.

stable_tour.quote: He was bought at the February sale and has come from Marco Botti. His work has been good since coming to us and we think he's off a workable handicap mark. He seems to be nice. 23-04-25

runners.comment: Didn't show a great deal in novice events and he needs a transformation on handicap debut
runners.spotlight: Big prices and he finished in rear in three novice events (6f/7f) towards the end of last year; now goes handicapping after a break but he needs a transformation on this step up to 1m2f.

runners.comment: In good form on AW this year and he's in the mix back on turf
runners.spotlight: Dual turf winner who has form figures of 133221363 on AW since Boxing Day and his last win was over 1m2f; still looks feasibly treated on his best form and he's in the mix back on turf (acts on good ground but he's untried on quicker).

runners.comment: Kempton maiden winner but she's struggled in handicaps and has lots to prove
runners.spotlight: Won a Kempton maiden (7f, AW) last spring but she's struggled in handicaps since and was beaten 7l back at Kempton two weeks ago; continues to drop down the weights but she has plenty to prove back up in trip.

runners.comment: Turned things around with a rallying win on Nottingham reappearance (8.3f); key player
runners.spotlight: 5yo who turned things around with a rallying win on his Nottingham reappearance (8.3f, good; 13-2) last Saturday; back up 4lb in the weights but he remains well treated on best form and his penultimate win was over this trip; key player.

runners.owner: Middleham Park Racing Xxii & Da Bin Lo

prev_owners.owner: Middleham Park Racing Xxiii & M Hulin

runners.comment: Won at Yarmouth last summer but has mixed record since and others are more convincing
runners.spotlight: Won a small-field handicap at Yarmouth (11.5f) last August but has mixed record since and was tailed off at Wolverhampton (1m6f) 19 days ago; may have had stamina issues last time but he's now 1-13 and others are more convincing.

runners.comment: In good form over hurdles in last two starts and she's not ruled out back on the Flat
runners.spotlight: Hurdle winner who has finished close up in handicaps at Sedgefield (2m1f, good) in her last two starts; 0-8 on the Flat but she ran respectably in big field at Doncaster (1m2f) last month and is not ruled out back in this sphere.

runners.comment: Back from a break with a good second at Bath but he's now 0-16 and is untried at this trip
runners.spotlight: On reduced mark and he returned from a break with a good second behind an improver at Bath (1m, good) three weeks ago; has claims if he can back that up but he's still a maiden 16 starts and has stamina to prove at this new trip.

runners.comment: Overall record of 1-37 and he's finished down the field on AW in last two starts
runners.spotlight: Back to form with a near-miss at Lingfield (1m2f, AW) in January but he's taken backward steps in two runs since; overall record is now 1-37 and others are preferred.

runners.comment: Hasn't shown much at big prices in six runs under both codes; passed over
runners.spotlight: Struggled at big prices in her four Flat runs and same story in two maiden hurdles this year; this is only her second handicap but she needs major improvement back on the Flat.

racecards.verdict: Top of the list is EVELYN'S PHOENIX who rallied well to score off a reduced mark on his Nottingham reappearance last Saturday.
racecards.betting_forecast: 4/1 He's Our Cracker, 9/2 Beauty Generation,  Evelyn's Phoenix, 11/2 Porter's Song, 8/1 Happy Chandler, 9/1 Not So Sobers,  Silkies Sib, 12/1 Blackwater Lilly, 16/1 Yokkell, 18/1 Shabu Shabu, 20/1 Celtic Spirit, 28/1 Miss Chester, 33/1 Iftikhaar, 100/1 Shifra

runners.comment: On reduced mark and he ran into plenty of trouble at Southwell (6f) latest; not ruled out
runners.spotlight: Won novice/maiden events at Wolverhampton (7f) for Clive Cox on his first two runs; finished in rear in three handicaps for his current yard but he ran into plenty of trouble over 6f at Southwell 18 days ago; now makes his turf debut but he's on a reduced mark and is not ruled back up in trip.

runners.comment: 0-7 but she returned after a break with a close third at Lingfield (7f, AW); respected
runners.spotlight: Seven-race maiden but she returned after a break with a close third in a Lingfield handicap (7f, AW) last month; should benefit from that run and she's respected off only 1lb higher back on turf.

runners.comment: Been gelded and he's a possible improver back on turf on handicap debut; needs close look
runners.spotlight: Close third of four on debut at Pontefract (6f, good to firm) last August; didn't match that in two runs during the winter but he's been gelded since and is a possible improver now returned to turf on his handicap debut; needs close look for in-form yard.

runners.comment: Finished down the field in all four runs and he needs a transformation at this new trip
runners.spotlight: Down the field in three runs for Richard Hannon last summer and was tenth of 12 on his recent handicap/stable debut at Southwell (6f, Tapeta; 11-1); still early days but he needs a transformation at this new trip.

runners.owner: Mrs R G Hillen And Partner
runners.comment: Went close in Yarmouth nursery in final 2yo run; respected with headgear added on return
runners.spotlight: No progress in three qualifying runs but he found improvement upped to 7f on nursery debut when a strong-finishing second at Yarmouth (good to soft) in September; only 1lb higher than for that close call and he's an interesting contender with cheekpieces added on his return.

runners.comment: Unexposed filly but she's not progressed so far and needs improvement back in trip
runners.spotlight: Made a promising start when third at Lingfield (7f, good) last August but she's been well held in three subsequent runs including on handicap/stable debut at Nottingham (8.3f, good) two weeks ago; should be sharper with that run under her belt but she needs improvement back in trip; cheekpieces added.

runners.comment: Has reached the frame in two AW handicaps for current yard; in the mix with hood reapplied
runners.spotlight: 0-6 but he's reached the frame in two handicaps for his current yard and was beaten less than 2l at Lingfield (7f, AW) last month; hasn't looked entirely straightforward but he didn't get the best of runs last time and he's in the mix back on turf; hood reapplied

runners.comment: Record of 2112 in AW handicaps; big player if he can transfer his progress back to turf
runners.spotlight: Beaten a nose on handicap debut at Newcastle (7f), after which he was gelded; won on Tapeta and Polytrack in next two starts and was a creditable second in his hat-trick bid at Kempton (7f) three weeks ago; still lightly raced and he's a big player if he can transfer his progress back on turf.

runners.comment: Handicap newcomer but he needs to raise his game after six months off
runners.spotlight: Third of nine on his debut at Brighton (6f, good) last May but went backwards from that in two subsequent runs last season; still unexposed and now goes handicapping at this new trip but he needs to raise his game after six months off.

runners.comment: Promising second at Lingfield (1m) and he looks interesting back in trip on handicap debut
runners.spotlight: Well held in his first two juvenile runs but he showed clear promise when runner-up in a Lingfield novice (1m, AW) in December; drops back in trip after a break but he pulled hard last time and is open to more progress on this handicap debut; interesting contender with Rossa Ryan booked.

runners.comment: Nine-race maiden who has gone the wrong way in handicaps; others preferred
runners.spotlight: Nine-race maiden who has gone the wrong in handicaps and was always in rear on Newmarket reappearance (7f, good; hood added) 11 days ago; mark continues to fall but she needs a big turnaround on this drop back in grade.

runners.comment: Disappointing favourite over C&D on recent handicap/stable debut; bit to prove
runners.spotlight: Well held in three qualifying runs (6f) for Eve Johnson Houghton last season; 4-1 favourite on handicap/stable debut over C&D (good) 12 days ago but he was always in rear and finished 15th of 17; has good pedigree and is still early days but he needs to leave that latest form a long way behind.

racecards.verdict: The vote goes to LION OF MALI who has a record of 2112 in AW handicaps and is a big player if he can transfer his progress back to turf.
racecards.betting_forecast: 5/2 Lion Of Mali, 11/2 Chelio, 6/1 Circle Of Trust, 8/1 Pretty Danielle,  Great Success,  Castlekeely, 9/1 Yachtsman, 14/1 Horwich,  Venetian Romance, 16/1 Eduardo Calderon, 25/1 Sprinting Speed,  Daretobedifferent

racecards.race_name: British Stallion Studs EBF Novice Stakes (GBB/IRE Incentive Race)

runners.breeder: J A Knox And Mrs M A Knox

runners.comment: February foal; 100,000gns yearling; first foal from 2021 Queen Mary Stks winner Quick Suzy
runners.spotlight: February foal; 100,000gns yearling; first foal from the 2021 Queen Mary Stakes winner Quick Suzy (RPR 106); stable is yet to really get going with juveniles this year but has operated at a 12% strike-rate (24-196) over the last five years; notable candidate.

runners.comment: Hung left-handed when last of four on recent Southwell debut (5f, novice; 10-1; btn 14l+).
runners.spotlight: April foal, and a half sister to a 1m1f Czech winner; hung left-handed when last of four on recent Southwell debut (5f, novice; 10-1; beaten over 14l); will need to improve markedly on that opening AW effort to stake a realistic claim.

runners.comment: Only eighth of 11 at Beverley (5f, fillies' novice; 9-2) ten days ago; could do better.
runners.spotlight: February foal; half-sister to two winners (6f-8.6f); never better than midfield, eighth of 11 to the promising Princesse d'Orange at Beverley (5f, fillies' novice, good to soft; 9-2) ten days ago; is in capable hands though, so could do better with that experience banked.

runners.comment: Showed speed before weakening on recent Beverley debut (5f, fillies' maiden; 12-1).
runners.spotlight: March foal; dam was a 5f winner (RPR 94); showed speed before weakening on recent Beverley debut (5f, fillies' maiden; 12-1, seventh of 11); that race run in a marginally slower time than division 1 - contested by Bluestone Lady - earlier in the afternoon.

runners.comment: April foal; 16,000euros yearling; second foal from a 6f winner (including 2yo; RPR 96).
runners.spotlight: April foal; 16,000euros yearling; second foal from a 6f winner (including 2yo; RPR 96), who was a half-sister to two winners (7.5f-1m4f); trainer is 0-1 with his juveniles this year; let the market guide.

racecards.verdict: This can go to a newcomer. THAI GINGER, a 100,000gns yearling, is the first foal from the 2021 Queen Mary Stakes winner Quick Suzy.
racecards.betting_forecast: 5/2 Navy Light, 9/4 Thai Ginger, 9/2 Pageant Girl, 11/2 Bluestone Lady, 8/1 Mind Those Steps, 10/1 Thunda Struck, 33/1 Bettabebougie

racecards.race_name: Napoleons Casino And Restaurant Leeds Restricted Maiden Fillies' Stakes (Bands B/C/D) (GBB Race)

runners.comment: Promising second on 1m debut; this trip should suit better; the one to beat
runners.spotlight: Teofilo filly who made an encouraging start to her career when second of five on 1m Southwell debut (Tapeta) 23 days ago, keeping on as if this longer trip is sure to suit; leading claims with improvement likely.

runners.comment: Good pedigree and a threat to all if the betting speaks in her favour
runners.spotlight: Good pedigree, being a half-sister to seven winners, including Sheraz (1m3f-1m7f including Listed; RPR 116), Lakota Sioux (7f 2yo including Group 3; 100), Shehiyr (9.5f-1m4f including AW; 99) and Surrey Gold (8.6f-1m6f; 98); dam 1m2f Group 3 winner; doesn't have that high a standard to aim at and market confidence would look significant.

runners.comment: Modest form when placed three times for Alice Haynes last year; more needed
runners.spotlight: Modest form when finishing third on three of her four starts at up to an extended 1m for Alice Haynes last year; improvement will be needed starting out for a new yard after five months off.

runners.comment: Only eighth on 1m debut but this half-sister to Big Orange has potential for longer trips
runners.spotlight: Half-sister to connections' top stayer Big Orange and several other winners; 28-1, 5l eighth of 12 on 1m Lingfield debut in December; has the potential for better over longer trips in 2026.

runners.comment: In good hands but best watched this time unless the betting hints otherwise
runners.spotlight: By Masar and a sister to a 1m winner in Sweden; in good hands but a watching brief is advised this time unless the betting hints otherwise.

runners.comment: Some promise amid inexperience when third on 7f debut; up in trip; likely to improve
runners.spotlight: Showed a bit of promise amid inexperience when 5.75l third of eight on 7f Wolverhampton debut in March; didn't achieve a great deal but is likely to improve up nearly 3f in trip.

racecards.verdict: Recent Southwell runner-up ROMANCE SPIRIT is the one to beat unless the betting vibes are strong surrounding newcomer Triumph.
racecards.betting_forecast: 11/10 Romance Spirit, 5/2 Triumph, 7/1 Miss Malone To You, 9/1 Mudita, 12/1 Always Blue, 14/1 Exquisite Skye

runners.comment: Ready win at Bath last week and 4lb rise if offset by rider's claim; can follow up
runners.spotlight: Ready winner back from a break at Bath (2m1f, good to firm) eight days ago; his 4lb rise is offset by Mason Paetel's claim; likely to follow up.

runners.comment: Two wins at Newcastle at the start of the year but handicapper in charge since
runners.spotlight: Out-and-out stayer who won twice at Newcastle (2m, Tapeta) at the start of the year but the handicapper has been winning the argument since; it remains to be seen whether a return to turf makes any difference in that regard.

prev_owners.owner: Nicolas Longere & Ecurie Haras Des Beaux

runners.comment: Fit from hurdling and feasibly treated on last April's Flat form
runners.spotlight: Arrives fit from hurdling and some of his best Flat form last year came in April, winning at Pontefract before second over C&D (both good).

runners.comment: Drew a blank in 2025 but did reach the frame on both C&D visits; off for 196 days
runners.spotlight: Drew a blank in 2025 but he did reach the frame on both C&D visits, including C&D reappearance; off for 196 days; David Allan partners the other Tim Easterby runner.

quotes.race: John Smith's Stayers' Handicap
quotes.quote: I wasn't worried about losing it in the stewards' room as the second bumped him too. I thought he'd go well but I don't know what happened at Newcastle. Zimmerman loves soft ground and stays two miles, so we'll find something for him if it stays wet - Tim Easterby, trainer.

quotes.race: Sky Bet Sunday Series Stayers Handicap
quotes.quote: Zimmerman did very well, he loves this ground and was very hardy at the finish there. He switched off and I was happy with his position - James Sullivan, rider.

quotes.race: Pertemps Newton Handicap
quotes.quote: Zimmerman ran well on his last two runs as well and is an improving horse. He should handle a step up in trip again and is a nice staying prospect - James Sullivan, jockey.

stable_tour.quote: He ran well all last year and is another who's in the Chester Cup, and he'll be entered for the Northumberland Plate too. He's an improving staying horse and he runs at Ripon first. 23-04-24

runners.comment: Never involved on recent 1m4f handicap debut but remains unexposed now up in trip
runners.spotlight: Unexposed 4yo who was never involved on his recent 1m4f Pontefract handicap debut but did show some promise in his qualifying runs; up 4f in trip now.

runners.comment: Well held on hurdle debut for new yard but progressive on Flat last year
runners.spotlight: Won three of his last five Flat runs for Paddy Butler, including a clearcut success at Bath (2m1f, soft) in October; no impact on hurdle debut for new yard in January but could fare a lot better back on the Flat.

runners.comment: Displayed early promise on Flat in France but hasn't shown much in Britain; tongue tied
runners.spotlight: Displayed early promise on the Flat in France but hasn't shown much since coming to Britain, including back on the Flat at Catterick (1m4f) 17 days ago; up markedly in trip now with a tongue-tie added.

racecards.verdict: James Owen's NO MORE BOLERO is the obvious one on the back of his comfortable Bath success eight days ago.
racecards.betting_forecast: 6/5 No More Bolero, 7/2 Rupert The Prince, 6/1 Tarbat Ness, 7/1 Diamand De Vindecy, 9/1 Treasure Islands, 10/1 Zimmerman, 33/1 Stitching Wheel

racecards.race_name: M.C.H. Hutchinson Memorial Trophy Handicap (GBBPlus Race)

runners.comment: Smart handicapper who ran several good races last year; has gone well fresh before
runners.spotlight: Smart handicapper who won at Haydock (1m4f, good) off 4lb lower last May and recorded several good efforts in defeat later in 2025; has gone well fresh before.

quotes.race: Betfred "Play Fred's £5 Million" Handicap (GBBPlus Race)
quotes.quote: Stressfree has been very consistent, he's got a lot of ability but he's often the bridesmaid. We sent him hurdling through the winter to try to toughen him up more than anything. It was an excellent ride by Danny but I'm never confident with this horse because he has come out on the wrong end of a battle before. He did nothing wrong today and it was a great performance. He could go to Ascot for the mile-and-half handicap and I think he'd get the trip in the Ebor. He keeps a little bit back so you wouldn't know how good he is - David O'Meara, trainer.

quotes.race: Agriculture And Equine Courses At SRUC Maiden Hurdle (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Stressfree is a very talented horse on the Flat. It's only his second go today and Brian (Hughes) was pulling it up in front, and I knew we were going to quicken up the straight, so I was just hoping that his jumping was going to hold up, which it has done. There'll be a bigger picture for this horse I'm sure - Henry Brooke, jockey, speaking to Racing TV.

stable_tour.quote: He should have won at Doncaster last time - he was all dressed up with nowhere to go. I ran him over hurdles over the winter to toughen him up a bit as he's a horse with a lot of ability who can be a bit soft. He could go for the City and Suburban next and might be one for the John Smith's Cup. 14-04-25

runners.comment: Good second in a warm race on AW over Easter and should go well back on turf
runners.spotlight: Last five outings on AW, posting his most encouraging effort when second of 12 in a 2m Newcastle Good Friday handicap; nudged back up 2lb for that but he's still 3lb lower than when runner-up at Chester (2m, good to soft) last September; should go well.

quotes.race: Liz And Izzy's Hoap Podcast Handicap
quotes.quote: That was great, I was delighted with Prydwen. Callum gave him a lovely, confident ride. It was an unbelievable effort carrying that weight. He obviously loves the AW so the Northumberland Plate looks a legitimate next step. He'll be weighted out of something like the Copper Horse at Ascot, but we might try the Goodwood Cup, he's moving into that sort of realm now - George Scott, trainer.

quotes.race: BetUK All-Weather Championships Marathon Handicap
quotes.quote: It was a really good performance. Prydwen has been a light-framed horse so we've given him a bit of time and he's filled into his frame. He's a bit older and wiser and that performance opens a few doors, I think he deserves a go at Royal Ascot in something like the Copper Horse Handicap - George Scott, trainer.

quotes.race: Cazoo Search Drive Smile Handicap
quotes.quote: Prydwen has been a nervous horse in the past and has been slow to come to hand. They didn't go too hard up front which enabled Marco to get a smooth run into it - George Scott, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: He ran a career best on his last start when narrowly second, which is quite a good effort considering he's a six-year-old. He's been pretty consistent considering how much he's run and he might go for a break now, have one run before Royal Ascot, and he'll go for the Copper Horse Handicap. He deserves a chance to run at a meeting like that and going back in trip there would suit him. 29-03-24

runners.comment: Dual winner for Ralph Beckett; new yard runs three and the betting may guide
runners.spotlight: Second career success when shading a tight finish at Goodwood (1m4f, good to firm) last August; ended the year with a poor run at Newcastle (1m4f) in September; subsequently sold out of Ralph Beckett's stable for 30,000gns; new yard runs three and the betting is perhaps the best guide to expectations.

runners.comment: Fine second on reappearance and Ripon form figures are 112; leading claims
runners.spotlight: Close second in this race (good) on her 2025 reappearance and went on to score twice at about 1m6f later in the year; returned with a career-best second of 13 at Musselburgh (1m6f, soft) three weeks ago, arguably deserving extra credit considering she met a bit of trouble; successful on her two other visits to Ripon; reasons to be positive.

prev_owners.owner: Exors Of The Late H H Aga Khan

runners.comment: Pretty useful in France but no obvious short-term encouragement on yard debut
runners.spotlight: Pretty useful at up to 1m4f in France but only eighth of 12 in 1m2f Doncaster handicap on British debut four weeks ago; the type to click for this yard at some point but possibly a bit further down the line.

runners.comment: Hard to derive much encouragement from recent reappearance but he is 2-3 over C&D
runners.spotlight: Soft-ground winner over this trip at Catterick last autumn; hard to derive much encouragement from his recent Thirsk reappearance but the fact he's 2-3 over C&D (all 2022) provides some hope.

quotes.race: Ladbrokes Get Rewarded With Ladbucks Chester Plate Handicap (GBBPlus Race)
quotes.quote: I was supposed to be a bit handier than that but Gibside didn't come away from the stalls very well so I thought to try and be brave and to see what happens. I was stuck where I was for a long time but he crept a few places forward and turning in he came really good. He's a super horse who is really versatile - ground and trip - and a bit of a yard favourite - Duran Fentiman, jockey.

racecards.verdict: Prydwen and DANCINGWITHMYSELF (nap) arrive on the back of good seconds, with the latter's good Ripon record earning her the vote.
racecards.betting_forecast: 2/1 Dancingwithmyself, 3/1 Prydwen, 9/2 Stressfree, 11/2 Ashnak, 13/2 Prince Of The Seas, 10/1 Gibside

runners.comment: Drawn a blank since 2024 Group 3 success but reappearance third quite encouraging
runners.spotlight: Losing spell goes back to his Palace House success two years ago but he has a reduced mark to work with as a result and he ran well when third on his Pontefract reappearance (5f, good to soft) 18 days ago; player if he can build on that.

quotes.race: William Hill Palace House Stakes (Group 3)
quotes.quote: It's been a big team effort with this horse as he's as quirky as they come. Seven Questions spent the night at the racecourse last night as we know when he gets on the horsebox, he gets very stirred up. So, he had an away night about half a mile from his stable. We saddled him about an hour ago and brought him down - he was trying to kick everyone. He's a talented horse on his day and got a brilliant ride. We'll have to re-evaluate where we go now as he was very much at a crossroads. We'll have to see whether he is a Royal Ascot horse - George Scott, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: He was a rock-solid two-year-old and was very unlucky not to win a couple of those big races he was competing in. He ran well on his first start in Dubai this winter then slightly tailed off, but you're not going to get everything right all the time. He's come back in good order and he'll be kept busy this season. I imagine we'll aim him at the Holyroodhouse Stakes and he might just need a couple of runs before then to get him in the zone and spot on for Ascot. He gives me every indication that he's trained on from last year. 29-03-24

prev_owners.owner: L Baudron, Alessandro Botti Et Al

runners.comment: Encouraging return to Britain at Newmarket last week; bold show likely from same mark
runners.spotlight: Three-time winner over 6f in France who ran his best race in Britain when second of eight to same owner's Jakajaro at Newmarket (5f, good to soft) 11 days ago; bold show likely from an unchanged mark.

runners.breeder: G H S Bloodstock & J C Bloodstock
runners.comment: C&D win last summer but might be best watched minus usual headgear after 196 days off
runners.spotlight: Improved when visor was added to her tongue-tie last year, winning over C&D (good) and at Newmarket (good to firm) in August; starts this campaign 5lb above the mark she defied at Newmarket and might be best watched after 196 days off with both the visor and tongue-tie missing.

runners.comment: Won at Southwell this month but career best needed to follow up off 6lb higher
runners.spotlight: Placed three times on AW over the winter before resuming winning ways over 5f at Southwell 18 days ago; hasn't been successful above a mark of 76 so a career best will be needed if he's to follow up.

quotes.race: Josh Mullins Rules Supreme Handicap (Div II)
quotes.quote: I couldn't believe his price. Castan kept going out and I thought I must have got something wrong. He's tough and he loves his racing - Bryan Smart, trainer.

quotes.race: Gamble Responsibly At BetUK Handicap
quotes.quote: Castan has always had loads of speed, but as a two-year-old he was the biggest hooligan I've had in my life! He just took a long time to get mentally right after a break. As soon as you touch the blindfold he comes out of the stalls like a greyhound. They all came at him and he fought back. Hopefully he can give us a big payout someday - Bryan Smart, trainer, speaking to Sky Sports Racing.

quotes.race: Start Racing TV Free Trial Now Nursery Handicap
quotes.quote: Castan did it nicely and Kevin never hit him. He said all day long that Castan would win these types of races and I'm delighted for the owners - Bryan Smart, trainer.

runners.comment: Multiple winner who is on a good mark on return for new trainer; betting informative
runners.spotlight: Ten-time winner down the years for James Evans; drew a blank in 2025 but runner-up twice off marks in the 90s, including reappearance, so well treated starting out for Tony Carroll (same owners); interesting to see what the betting makes of him.

quotes.race: Aston Martin "Dash" Handicap (Heritage Handicap)
quotes.quote: We bought Dream Composer very inexpensively from France three years ago - he'd run as a 2yo there - and he's won for us every year. He keeps stepping up, and obviously this is the icing on the cake, winning one like this. He's won some good races at Grade One tracks; we just felt he was handicapped quite well today, and the cut in the ground helps him. He's pretty good at going up and down dale, because he's won at Goodwood and places like that. We were going along as we found it; he's got an entry in the Wokingham and if a penalty gets him into it and there's cut in the ground, he likes Ascot and has run well there, so that's a possible. But we'll enjoy today and see where it takes us - James Evans, trainer.

quotes.race: Cavani Menswear Sartorial Sprint Handicap
quotes.quote: I think the ground was a bit too lively at Royal Ascot. Dream Composer has been travelling much better in his races so the five seems to suit well now. There is the five-furlong handicap on the first day of Glorious Goodwood which is a 0-105 and that was a thought, and obviously the Stewards' Cup would come into consideration as well - James Evans, trainer.

quotes.race: Peroni Nastro Azzurro Handicap
quotes.quote: Dream Composer has great form here and likes this ground, so everything was in our favour. The race went to plan and he keeps galloping. He probably likes 6f more than five, but the ground helped him - you might as well use his stamina over five - Mollie Phillips, rider.

runners.comment: This 12yo added three more wins last year but has yet to win first time out
runners.spotlight: None of today's opponents were foaled when he won his first race but this 12yo was still pretty useful last year, winning three times over 5f; the fact he's never won first time up suggests it may pay to look elsewhere this time, though.

quotes.race: Precision Facades Handicap
quotes.quote: Copper Knight is a super old boy and a proper racehorse. It's fantastic to win on him after all this time. I've had a few placings on him and he's been around the Easterbys for a long time, but it's a delight to ride him and ride a winner on him - Duran Fentiman, jockey, speaking to Sky Sports Racing.

quotes.race: Pontefract Races Chairman's Challenge Apprentice Handicap (Apprentice Training Race - RE Series)
quotes.quote: It's a fantastic result all round. Copper Knight is a real yard superstar and you couldn't predict what he's going to do - he's a legend - William Easterby, trainer's assistant.

quotes.race: Irish Thoroughbred Marketing Handicap
quotes.quote: Copper Knight is a wonderful little horse and tries like hell. He just loves it here and a bit of juice in the ground - Tim Easterby, trainer.

quotes.race: Edinburgh Gin Rhubarb & Ginger Handicap
quotes.quote: It's unbelievable and I'm not sure how Copper Knight keeps showing up and putting in these amazing performances. He started the season quite high in the handicap and needed to come down a few pounds, but he's still full of it and we'll keep going back to York as he absolutely loves it there - Tom Denham, part-owner.

quotes.race: Sky Bet And Symphony Group Handicap
quotes.quote: Copper Knight is a super horse and wonderful to train. Dave (Allan) said he'd not felt as good as that in a long time. He loves good ground and coasting along. He trains himself really, he just lobs away at the back and we don't do anything fancy with him. He gets himself ready and is an absolute star. We may look at the Portland at Doncaster - Tim Easterby, trainer.

quotes.race: Matchbook Betting Exchange Handicap
quotes.quote: Copper Knight is a star. He ran great first time out last year then he went up 7lb, that snookered him and he went off the boil so he got himself re-handicapped.   He ran well at Chester last week and they dropped him 1lb for being third but he likes it here. He was just cocking his lugs a bit but he was always going to hold on.   We might run him in the Dash at Epsom - Tim Easterby, trainer.

quotes.race: John Smith's City Walls Stakes (Listed Race)
quotes.quote: Copper Knight is a lovely horse, he's been an absolute star for us and he's better than ever. Ideally he'd wants a bit more juice in the ground but he copes with anything. He's in the King George Stakes at Goodwood and he'll probably go there and he could come back here for the Nunthorpe - Tim Easterby, trainer.

quotes.race: Matchbook Betting Exchange Handicap
quotes.quote: Copper Knight is a wonderful horse, he's one of those that tries, he wants to win races. I'd rather have been drawn low because I think the high stalls had a disadvantage but he ran great. He's a super little horse and he'll go to Epsom for the Dash. Eeh Bah Gum will go too, he ran well but he wasn't drawn where the pace was - Tim Easterby, trainer.

quotes.race: Lady Cecil Handicap
quotes.quote: I rode Copper Knight last time at Doncaster and he ran a really good race. Today the race worked out perfectly for him. He wants a strong pace and when the gaps opened he took them - Paul Hanagan, rider.

quotes.race: Parsonage Hotel And Cloisters Spa Handicap
quotes.quote: Copper Knight was niggled a bit early on so they must have been going fast. He likes a bit of ease in the ground - Tim Easterby, trainer.

quotes.race: Stobart Energy Gosforth Park Cup Handicap
quotes.quote: Copper Knight is pretty uncomplicated. He just jumps fast. He seemed to be really enjoying himself in front, he felt like he was at half pace - I was ahead of some quick horses but he felt like he was doing it easily. I fancied him quite a lot for the Scottish Sprint last time but I think he probably just still needed the run to put the fitness on him - David Allan, jockey.

quotes.race: Unibet Sprint Stakes (Handicap)
quotes.quote: Copper Knight isn't very big but he's very quick. He could be a Listed performer - Keith Stone, trainer's representative.

quotes.race: Sustainable Group (UK) Ltd Handicap
quotes.quote: Copper Knight ran a good race at Ripon last month. He's won round Chester before and seems to be getting faster - Anthony Denham, part-owner.

quotes.race: Stellar Group Lily Agnes Conditions Stakes (Plus 10 Race)
quotes.quote: We were hopeful at Windsor, but Copper Knight ran into one of Richard Hannon's. We entered him just to see what would turn up against him and luckily the ground dried a bit and the race could have been stronger, though it wasn't weak. Royal Ascot would be the dream, but we'll have to see - George Boughey, assistant trainer.

stable_tour.quote: He looks great and you'd never know he was ten years old. He'll go back to York for the Dante meeting. He's won seven times there - some hate the track but he loves it. 23-04-24

runners.comment: Recent reappearance sixth of 17 quite encouraging and only 1lb above his last winning mark
runners.spotlight: Reopposing stablemate Vince L'Amour was ahead in second when sixth of 17 at Musselburgh (5f, good to soft) 13 days ago but it was still quite an encouraging return to action from this 5yo who has dipped to only 1lb above the mark he defied at Catterick (5f, good) last September.

quotes.race: ROA Supporting Racing To School's Milestone Handicap
quotes.quote: Equity Law was down in grade but he jumped [off] the best of them all. I can't fault him. He had horses running all over him from all over the place in the final furlong, but quickened nicely, so full credit to him - Sean Kirrane, jockey.

quotes.race: bet365 Handicap
quotes.quote: Equity Law was quick out of the stalls from his wide draw which was helpful and it was an easy race to ride on paper. He's obviously improved for his comeback run on soft ground at Bath - Oisin Murphy, jockey.

runners.comment: Stepped up on reappearance when second in competitive race at Musselburgh latest
runners.spotlight: Took a good step forward from his reappearance when second (Equity Law sixth) of 17 at Musselburgh (5f, good to soft) 13 days ago; respected off only 1lb higher.

racecards.verdict: Fitri Hay had the one-two in a 5f Newmarket handicap last week and may repeat the feat, with DYONISOS preferred to Seven Questions.
racecards.betting_forecast: 5/2 Seven Questions, 7/2 Dyonisos, 11/2 Vince L'Amour, 13/2 Tiva,  Castan, 7/1 Equity Law, 14/1 Dream Composer, 16/1 Copper Knight

runners.comment: Showed a willing attitude to make all at Nottingham (8.5f, good) last Saturday; 3lb higher
runners.spotlight: Built on Wolverhampton comeback run (7f) when showing a willing attitude to make all at Nottingham (8.5f, good) last Saturday; 3lb rise isn't insurmountable but he is set to compete from a career-high mark, so further progress is required.

stable_tour.quote: I was worried about his high draw at Musselburgh last week but it probably helped him as he doesn't like being crowded and he could sit wide on his own. He put in a career-best to win by quite a distance. The handicapper is going to have a say, but he did run through the line hard and he's open to a little bit of progress. That win was over 7f and a mile will suit him better, so he'd have half a chance of defying a rise. 04-09-25

runners.comment: Won from 7lb lower at Musselburgh (1m, good to soft) in September; potentially vulnerable.
runners.spotlight: Lit up by a visor (too keen) when a weakening third over C&D last June; did manage to win twice thereafter (with headgear discarded), including from 7lb lower at Musselburgh (1m, good to soft) in September; potentially vulnerable off a 192-day absence.

runners.comment: Disappointing efforts handicapping (7f-1m); easing mark for return from ten-month absence.
runners.spotlight: Rallied to win a modest maiden at Ayr (1m, good; 11-2) last April; disappointing since introduced to handicapping, scarcely managing to beat a rival in three attempts (7f-1m); an easing mark could aid her cause on return from ten-month absence; stablemate of Poet's Dawn.

runners.comment: Won at Doncaster (1m) & Musselburgh (1m1f) last August; ninth of 13 at Thirsk (1m) latest.
runners.spotlight: Won back-to-back at Doncaster (1m) and Musselburgh (1m1f) last August, running down Drumcondra latterly; held off higher marks since, including when ninth of 13 at Thirsk (1m, good; beaten nearly 6l) latest; Ethan Tindall's 5lb claim is helpful.

stable_tour.quote: He's a nice horse. He went to Southwell on Saturday but there was no pace and it meant that he ran too keen. He's better than that. He's a big, long-striding horse who's better suited to places like Doncaster. He'll probably go on the all-weather next and then he's going to the horses-in-training sale, and I might look to buy him back himself. Some of the jumping folk might be interested in him, so I'll school him before the sale. 01-10-25

runners.comment: Well beaten on recent Yarmouth comeback (1m2f); hasn't run over a mile since late 2024.
runners.spotlight: Both Flat wins came on AW (1m6f-2m); relatively quiet since winning over hurdles at Worcester (2m, maiden) last June; well beaten on recent Yarmouth comeback (1m2f), and he hasn't run over a mile since late 2024; others preferred.

quotes.race: Build Your Acca With BetUK Handicap
quotes.quote: I watched back Currumbin's last few races and it just looks like he stays. Today he relaxed beautifully, he took me there very comfortably and he won well - Kieren Shoemark, jockey, speaking to Sky Sports Racing.

prev_owners.owner: Qatar B'stock Ltd/D Howden/China Horse Club/Ballylinch Stud

runners.comment: 0-14; ran respectably when fourth in a newly applied visor at Catterick (7f, good) latest.
runners.spotlight: Maiden (0-14), runner-up five times, including in a 6f Southwell novice last November; ran respectably (keen) when fourth in a newly applied visor at Catterick (7f, good) latest; should stay a mile (first go) and is on a fair mark, more so if factoring in Mason Paetel's 5lb claim.

runners.comment: Won twice last summer (8f-8.5f); runner-up to Poet's Dawn at Carlisle (1m) in September.
runners.spotlight: In fine fettle last summer, winning at Pontefract (1m) and Nottingham (8.5f); found Poet's Dawn too strong at Carlisle (1m, soft; similar terms) in September; off since finishing third at Newcastle in October, so may strip fitter for this comeback run.

runners.breeder: Mrs J K Powell & Catridge Farm Stud
runners.comment: Veteran (12-121); seventh last year; should strip fitter for Pontefract (1m) comeback run.
runners.spotlight: Veteran (12-121); seventh (beaten 4l; 40-1) in this last year; broadly consistent since accounting for Ravishing Beauty at Carlisle (1m, soft; similar terms) last September; should strip fitter for recent Pontefract (1m; fourth of nine; 33-1) comeback run.

quotes.race: Lady Jane Bethell Memorial Amateur Jockeys' Handicap
quotes.quote: I didn't think I'd won when I crossed the line, I had no idea we'd dead-heated. Poet's Dawn is double the age of Star Start [fellow dead-heater] and had to carry 9lb more [taking into account jockey claims]. He's rarely out of the top three and is a star in the yard - Emily Roberts, jockey.

quotes.race: Join Racing TV Now Handicap
quotes.quote: It felt like the leader was getting away but Poet's Dawn has a big heart and he dug deep. He's a grand horse to have in the yard, he goes on any ground and very versatile - David Allan, jockey.

quotes.race: Ice Co Supporting Macmillan Handicap
quotes.quote: Poet's Dawn slipped coming out the stalls at Beverley last time and couldn't get in the race. He loves a bit of cut in the ground and David said he seemed to go better left-handed than right - Tim Easterby, trainer.

quotes.race: Racing UK In Glorious HD Novice Auction Stakes
quotes.quote: The race that Poet's Dawn ran in at Redcar last time worked out quite well with several winners coming out of it, and this didn't look a particularly good race - Tim Easterby, trainer.

runners.comment: Third at Wolverhampton (8.5f; 10-1) penultimate; backward step at Doncaster (1m2f) since.
runners.spotlight: Last turf win was here (1m2f, good to soft; from 6lb higher) in June 2024; fair third at Wolverhampton (8.5f; 10-1) on penultimate start but took a backward step at Doncaster (1m2f) subsequently; easing mark isn't enough to tempt.

runners.comment: Sits 2lb above last winning mark; fourth in a Class 4 at Southwell (40-1) latest.
runners.spotlight: Resumed winning ways at Beverley (8.5f, soft; from 2lb lower) last September but reportedly ran too freely when soundly beaten at Nottingham next time; caught the eye when fourth in a Class 4 at Southwell (1m; 40-1) recently, but it mightn't be wise to take that form literally.

runners.comment: Off the mark at the 13th attempt at Nottingham (8.5f, good) latest; now 3lb higher.
runners.spotlight: Dropped back in trip when getting off the mark at the 13th attempt at Nottingham (8.5f, good) latest; the winning margin there was just a nose but, with a 3lb rise, he remains on a reasonably competitive mark; Hollie Doyle is back aboard.

racecards.verdict: In a race which lacks a standout contender, the opportunity is there for HOSTILITY. The Sweet Escape is another to consider.
racecards.betting_forecast: 4/1 The Sweet Escape, 9/2 Highland Olly,  Hostility, 13/2 Keats House, 7/1 Ravishing Beauty, 8/1 Up The Jazz, 10/1 Amidst The Chaos,  Kiss Me My Love, 14/1 Poet's Dawn, 33/1 Rosemary May,  Currumbin

racecards.race_name: Watch Sky Sports Racing In HD Handicap

runners.comment: 5f Southwell winner for Ed Bethell; sold for 40,000gns; returns to 6f for stable debut.
runners.spotlight: With Ed Bethell when knuckling down to land the odds in a 5f fillies' maiden at Southwell (runner-up 2-3 since) last September; joined this trainer the following month for 40,000gns; is fairly weighted back over 6f in handicap company.

runners.comment: Scrambled home in 5f novice at Leicester (6-5 fav) last October; gelded; back from a break
runners.spotlight: Rewarded for a series of consistent efforts when scrambling home in a 5f novice at Leicester (6-5 favourite) last October; gelded, and back from a winter break with the possibility of more to come; shouldn't be troubled by returning to 6f.

runners.comment: 0-8; fifth of eight on Kempton return (7f; 14-1, beaten 4l) six weeks ago; 1lb lower.
runners.spotlight: 0-8; lost out in tight finishes at Musselburgh (5f novice) and Lingfield (6f nursery) as a juvenile; gelded over the winter and fifth of eight on Kempton return (7f; 14-1, beaten 4l) six weeks ago; 1lb lower but likely needs a fraction more.

runners.owner: Exors Of The Late Sheikh Mohammed Obaid
runners.comment: Newcastle novice winner (6f); possibly needed comeback run at Southwell (7f) ten days ago.
runners.spotlight: Shaped well on Haydock debut (third) and off the mark next time in a modest three-runner Newcastle novice (6f; 2-1; made all); possibly needed her recent comeback run at Southwell (7f; fifth of seven), and dropping back in trip looks sensible; chance, despite a poor draw.

runners.comment: 6f Wolverhampton maiden winner; twice narrowly beaten since; merits respect on turf debut.
runners.spotlight: Made the breakthrough at Wolverhampton (6f, maiden; 4-1) in February; has bettered that since (on RPRs) with narrow defeats at Lingfield and Newcastle; 2lb higher again, but possible he can stake a claim if proving as effective on turf (debut).

runners.comment: Off the mark at Lingfield (5f novice) in December; retains potential off four-month break.
runners.spotlight: Runner-up at Hamilton and Catterick (6f fillies' maiden; first-time cheekpieces) prior to being slowly away at Lingfield (7f) in early December; took her chance - always handy - back there (5f novice) a fortnight later, and has been given a four-month break since; retains potential.

runners.comment: Bumped at the start but recovered to do solid late work at Catterick (5f) latest; 6f fine.
runners.spotlight: Yet to win (0-10), going closest when beaten a head at Newcastle (6f nursery) in December; bumped at the start but recovered to do solid late work at Catterick (5f, good; third of ten, beaten 1l) 17 days ago; same mark (holds Contorno) for return to 6f.

runners.comment: Hung left-handed and dropped out accordingly on recent stable debut at Beverley (7.5f).
runners.spotlight: Failed to progress for Brian Ellison (0-4; 5f-6f); hung left-handed and dropped out accordingly on recent stable debut at Beverley (7.5f; 13-2, eighth of ten); may draw benefit from that comeback run but others make way more appeal.

runners.comment: No excuses when a weakening fifth (Liverpool Star third) on turf return at Catterick (5f).
runners.spotlight: Dictated a steady pace to maintain his unbeaten Newcastle record (5f; 2-2) on penultimate start; no excuses when a weakening fifth (Liverpool Star third) on turf return at Catterick (5f, good; 6-1) 17 days ago; 2lb above last winning mark (AW).

runners.comment: Closer when fifth on handicap debut at Pontefract (6f; first-time tongue-tie) last October
runners.spotlight: Didn't offer much initially, but did at least get closer to the principals when fifth of ten on handicap debut at Pontefract (6f, nursery; soft; in a first-time tongue-tie) last October; hasn't that many miles on the clock but does lack a recent run; others preferred.

racecards.verdict: The suggestion in a tricky finale is the moderately progressive ARISHKA'S DREAM, who races on turf for the first time.
racecards.betting_forecast: 4/1 Arishka's Dream, 9/2 Siouxpersonic, 5/1 Koffee And Kale, 11/2 Liverpool Star, 6/1 Blue Nguru, 15/2 Vencedora, 10/1 Contorno, 14/1 Ecclefechan, 20/1 Solar Cooper,  Hares Bredth

racecards.race_name: Changing Young Lives At Jamie's Farm Fillies' Juvenile Handicap Hurdle (Premier Handicap) (GBB Race)

runners.comment: Readily landed the Adonis, taking record to 3-4; the class angle and has earned top weight
runners.spotlight: Developing into a useful filly and readily landed the Adonis (2m, good to soft; Grade 2) at Kempton most recently, taking record to 3-4; the class angle on handicap debut and has earned top weight; respected.

quotes.race: Ladbrokes Adonis Juvenile Hurdle (Grade 2) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: La Luna Artista was a replacement for a horse the syndicate lost at Newbury last season. I was really upset by it and we managed to keep the syndicate together with her. She was inexpensive but is by Spanish Moon and is a lovely big filly who has done absolutely nothing wrong. She is very professional. I thought the ground might be a bit soft for her today but clearly not. She jumps and you'd think she was a two and a half mile chaser. What an achievement. It's all about the pedigrees for me. I like to concentrate on a type of horse and what their pages say, then try and match the horse to the page - Jane Williams, trainer.La Luna Artista is a very, very smart filly and Jane [Williams] has done a wonderful job training her. She is a very fast filly and I am quite glad they went quick. She jumped very well - she can be a bit guessy - but I reminded her after that and she was good afterwards. I felt like I was picking up everywhere down to two out and she was very clever over the last two - Ciaran Gethings, jockey.

quotes.race: pricedup.bet EBF Fillies' Junior "National Hunt" Hurdle (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: La Luna Artista is a really nice horse with a big future. I wasn't surprised she won today because she's very professional. She came out of the bumper a completely different horse and understood her job as a racehorse. She didn't put a foot wrong.
