She's an exceptional jumper at home and I think she'll be a chaser in time, and having a mare to take chasing is a lovely thing - Jane Williams, trainer.

runners.comment: 2-3 over hurdles for new yard, bagging Listed honours at Musselburgh most recently
runners.spotlight: Successful in final Flat attempt and is 2-3 over hurdles for new yard, most recently bagging Listed honours at Musselburgh; one for the shortlist, with further progress plausible.

quotes.race: bet365 Scottish Triumph Hurdle (A Juvenile Hurdle) (Listed Race) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Made U Blush ran a cracker. It was a faster race than when she won at Doncaster last time and she jumped brilliantly, so I'm hoping Dan [Skelton] decides to go to Cheltenham with her. We've taken our time with Secret Force and we're aiming him at Cheltenham, so he's not run a bad race as he will come on for the run - Jimmy Fyffe, owner.

stable_tour.quote: A decent horse on the Flat, she's won her last two for us, including in Listed company at Musselburgh, and has improved run by run. I'm really happy with her progression and it would be nice to get her in the race. 17-02-26

She just arrived here from Ireland because the owners thought there were more opportunities in Britain. She made her debut for us at Salisbury and was a creditable second in a 1m2f handicap. But I'm still feeling my way with her and see no downside in running her again this week in the £50,000 maiden at Goodwood on Saturday. She's an exciting addition. 20-08-25

runners.comment: Had her limitations exposed to some extent last time; others are more appealing
runners.spotlight: Had her limitations exposed to some extent at Haydock last time when bidding for a hat-trick; questionable whether she'll be ahead of her mark in this first handicap hurdle attempt.

runners.comment: Clearcut success at Stratford took her hurdles record to 2-3; improving filly
runners.spotlight: Had further wind surgery prior to Stratford success (2m2f, soft) last time, beating a solid yardstick in clearcut fashion and taking hurdles record to 2-3; improving in this sphere and looks one to consider.

runners.comment: Consistent; rallying second against males over C&D most recently; very solid claims
runners.spotlight: Successful on debut over hurdles and has proved very consistent since, most recently a rallying second in 4yo handicap over C&D when the only filly in the field; very solid, back against her own sex.

quotes.race: SpraycladUK NE Ltd Juvenile Maiden Hurdle (Go North Night Nurse Series Qualifier) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: I thought Only One Blue was good on the whole. She was understandably a bit green and Tom [Broughton] gave her a lovely ride. We needed a good jump at the last and she responded with her best and winged it, which probably won her the race. She's out of a very good mare [Missunited] who was a thorough stayer and a good jumper, so the pedigree was bang there for what she's done today - Max Comley, trainer.

runners.comment: Interesting handicap debutante, even though Harry Skelton prefers Made U Blush
runners.spotlight: Thrice-raced filly who represents notable connections and may be capable of big improvement now handicapping; interesting, even though Harry Skelton prefers stablemate Made U Blush.

runners.comment: May progress now handicapping, especially if settling better
runners.spotlight: Has tended to take a good hold since racing over hurdles but managed to bag silver medals the last twice; in good hands and may progress now handicapping, especially if settling better.

runners.comment: Appears to have a difficult task on second start for new stable
runners.spotlight: Four-race maiden who left Dan Skelton prior to Chepstow last time when bouncing back from a disappointing effort; however, even off bottom weight this looks a difficult task.

racecards.verdict: Very solid ONLY ONE BLUE gets the vote ahead of her improving stablemate Cloaks Of Gold.
racecards.betting_forecast: 5/4 La Luna Artista, 4/1 Made U Blush, 7/1 Cloaks Of Gold, 10/1 The Procrastinator,  Siorai, 12/1 Love Sonnet,  Only One Blue,  Queen Maeve, 40/1 Whitletts

racecards.race_name: bet365 Novices' Championship Final Handicap Hurdle (GBB Race)

runners.comment: Scored in tidy fashion at Chepstow (handicap debut) last time, taking rules record to 2-3
runners.spotlight: Scored in tidy fashion at Chepstow (2m, good to soft; handicap debut) last time, taking rules record to 2-3, and is probably still well treated even after a 6lb rise; improving.

runners.comment: Has a solid record at 2m and likely still has more to offer; respected handicap debutant
runners.spotlight: Non-stayer over 2m4f last time; solid record at 2m otherwise, including two efforts behind smart Sober Glory; this Skelton runner likely still has more to offer; respected handicap debutant.

quotes.race: Best Odds Guaranteed Still At BetVictor Maiden Hurdle (Novices' Championship Series Qual') (GBB)
quotes.quote: Kadastral is a very talented horse. We've seen a lot of improvement, but I'll look after him now. I don't think you'll see him at Cheltenham - he's more likely to wait and go to Aintree. That's not because he's not Cheltenham standard - I feel he is - but he's a tall and narrow horse, and the right thing to do is to tread carefully as a novice hurdler. I don't want to go and find out what he can't do, I'd rather get him in the right races and make him the best he can be. He's a very good horse, but some are going to be significantly better over a fence, and this one puts himself into that category. If we're going to win a Graded race, I feel like it'll be at Aintree rather than Cheltenham - Dan Skelton, trainer.

quotes.race: Goffs Hundred Grand Bumper (An Open National Hunt Flat Race) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Kadastral was always going to appreciate going on slightly better ground at this point in his life. He's improved since Kempton, where the ground was soft enough for him. He's quite a big horse and probably went a bit weak that day. He hit the front a long way out but it was a good performance. He'll start at two miles over hurdles and we'll go up if its appropriate. He's really a chaser. I can see him aiming at some nice hurdles without going crazy unless he keeps beating everyone. We'll look after him and I'd love to see him over a fence in two seasons - Dan Skelton, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: A really nice horse who won the Goffs Hundred Grand Bumper in the spring. He ran well on his hurdling debut at Chepstow, finding only a useful horse of Philip Hobbs's [Sober Glory] too good on the day, and will improve a lot for that. I'm mostly looking forward to him as a chaser but there are plenty of good days to be had with him before then. I won't be running him much but there's plenty of progress to come. 10-11-25

runners.breeder: A Peltier, D Juste & J Houdin
runners.comment: Made all at Newbury most recently but is far from sure to get an easy lead in this field
runners.spotlight: Proving consistent and, following a good effort in a Grade 2, he made all at Newbury (2m, good to soft) back down in class last time; far from sure to get an easy lead in this bigger field, however.

quotes.race: Castle Windows Newbury Anniversary Novices' Hurdle (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Kocktail Bleu has been a tough, consistent horse, and he's been very easy to train. He's no bother, which makes my life so much easier. The form in the races he's been running in has stacked up - Chris Gordon, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: He ran well in two strong bumpers last season, getting placed both times. He's come out and won his maiden hurdle at Fontwell this season, doing it very nicely. He has a tendency to jump to the right, but I feel very much he could be an EBF Final type. He'd go in the Sandown mud, which it generally what you get on that day, and I think he'd act on the track and would probably enjoy the trip. We'll try to get him qualified for that. 01-12-25

runners.comment: Improving 4yo whose record is 3-4; scored easily at Taunton last time; major contender
runners.spotlight: Improving 4yo whose record is 3-4; bought for £360,000 after sole Irish hurdles start; ran well in Grade 2 for sole defeat; easily justified favouritism at Taunton (2m, good) last time; major player.

quotes.race: Coral "Daily Rewards Shaker" "Introductory" Hurdle (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: You can imagine I loved that. Without a shadow of a doubt, Minella Yoga is one of the best youngsters I have. I thought I'd have half a chance to run him against Act Of Innocence, and I couldn't have had a better result! I'm really thrilled with that. We liked what we've seen at home, and he went very nicely during a gallop at Wincanton. He's got a lot of class. He'll definitely have an entry in the Triumph, and we could see him galloping up that Cheltenham hill, but it's not the be-all and end-all. He'll be a nice horse for the future. We could have a look at Trials day [Cheltenham, January 24] and see where we stand, but you have to mind these young horses - Paul Nicholls, trainer.

quotes.race: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Academy Hurdle
quotes.quote: Minella Yoga is a fine big horse who we bought as a yearling, but was always going to be too big for the Flat. We did a bit with him last year and he worked with Minella Study, who won a Listed hurdle in Wetherby last week. I was a little worried about the ground but Darragh said he went through it and that he jumps for fun. He has a future and I'd imagine he's for sale - John Nallen, owner, speaking to RacingTV.

stable_tour.quote: He actually ran well but was just a little green at Cheltenham. I think a mark of 129 is acceptable and at this stage of his career we thought the handicap would be a better option than the Supreme or the Triumph. 15-02-26

runners.comment: Made all in small field at Sedgefield last time; faces stiffer task in this deep handicap
runners.spotlight: Made all in small field at Sedgefield (2m1f, good) last time, taking hurdles record to 2-3; however, he faces a stiffer task in this deep handicap with competition for the lead.

quotes.race: Roxyfet Sports Lounge For Private Hire Novices' Hurdle (Novices' Championship Hurdle Qual') (GBB)
quotes.quote: We probably pitched Desertmore News in a bit too deep at Kempton, but I do hope he's going to get to that level at some point. It might well be when he has fences in front of him, but the final of this series will be the aim for now. He's a big, scopey type who likes nice ground and is very straightforward - it's exciting. - Tom Ellis, trainer.

quotes.race: Book The Bistro In Seasons Restaurant Maiden Hurdle (GBB Race) (Div II)
quotes.quote: I met James [owner] in a bar at Cheltenham before Christmas. We had a drink together and he said he likes to support people getting going in life. I put forward another horse to James from an Irish point-to-point when he said he would like to buy one, but he liked the horse that finished third, so he's got a good eye for one. Denis Leahy [former owner and trainer] said not to run Desertmore News on too soft ground and he's been a lovely, straightforward horse who is easy at home. - Tom Ellis, Trainer, speaking to Sky Sports Racing.

runners.comment: Made all at Ayr last time; may do better still but dominating this race will be harder
runners.spotlight: Made all in small field at Ayr (2m, soft) last time, taking hurdles record to 2-4; in good hands and may do better still but dominating this race seems likely to be harder.

runners.comment: Scored comfortably in Fontwell maiden last time; further progress is possible
runners.spotlight: Finished behind Kadastral on penultimate start but may fare better in this rematch, having scored comfortably in Fontwell maiden (2m1f, good to soft) latest; further progress is possible.

runners.comment: Return to 2m looks a plus but he's still seeking first rules win away from Hereford
runners.spotlight: Had wind surgery since failing to convince over 2m4f in the EBF Final on this track last time on stable debut; return to 2m looks a plus but he's still seeking first rules win away from Hereford.

quotes.race: BetWright Bet The Wright Way EBF "National Hunt" Novices' Hurdle (Qualifier) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: We were hoping Race To Base could do it easily, especially with how his Uttoxeter form has worked out. I'm pleased David was here to see him do it. Broadway Boy was always a pleasure for him, but this fellow is a bit different. He's very quick, one of the pacier ones at home, so it wouldn't be a surprise to see him stay at the minimum trip - Sam Twiston-Davies, jockey.

runners.comment: Came up well short on handicap debut last time; can be opposed
runners.spotlight: Dual novice winner but came up well short at Newbury (2m3f) on handicap debut most recently and can be opposed in this competitive field.

stable_tour.quote: A lovely horse. I was actually pleased with his bumper campaign, even though he didn't win one. We pitched him into a £10,000 race at Haydock on his final bumper start and we went there thinking he'd run well, which he did (fifth behind So Proud), but the race wasn't run to suit. I was never disappointed, although you would say his hurdle form is far better. He won on his first run over hurdles at Newton Abbot, then split two nice horses of JP McManus's (Harry Lowes and Aguellid) down at Exeter. Then, last time out, he bumped into another in-form horse of Paul Nicholls' called Calvino at Taunton. Where's he going to go now? Well, I think we'll go for another novice under a penalty - the handicapper has quite rightly given him a mark of 118 - as I don't think he's quite ready for the hustle and bustle of handicaps yet. If everything was right he might go for one of those nice novice handicaps at Sandown in the spring because he's a horse who would handle a bit of good ground. He's a nice type who will jump a fence in time as well. 21-01-26

runners.comment: Chance of gaining a first hurdles win depends on how well he responds to wind surgery
runners.spotlight: Has consistent hurdles form; however, his chance of gaining a first success in this sphere largely depends on how well he responds to a physical tweak (wind surgery since last run).

runners.comment: Scored readily at Newton Abbot last time and may improve further; yard also runs Kadastral
runners.spotlight: Posted consistent efforts prior to ready win in Newton Abbot maiden (2m2f, good to soft) last time; may improve further and can't be dismissed, even though Harry Skelton prefers Kadastral.

stable_tour.quote: A very nice horse who was third in a bumper at Warwick in the spring. I was a bit disappointed he didn't win but things didn't quite work out for him in the race, and although I think he'd win a bumper if we went that way, he's more of a jumper and we'll go straight over hurdles this season. 10-11-25

runners.breeder: Al Shira'Aa Farms S A R L
runners.comment: Broadly too free for his own good since switched to hurdles; needs to settle better
runners.spotlight: Showed smart Flat form as a 3yo; managed to win in December but has otherwise broadly been too free for his own good since switched to hurdles; ideally needs to settle better.

quotes.race: Sky Bet Super Sub Novices' Hurdle (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Ambiente Friendly has been a challenge. He is a horse with an extreme amount of ability. He has had two massive runs in the English and Irish Derby, but he has gone off the rails since then. It has been small steps on the way back. It is just nice to see him progress from that first Cheltenham run over hurdles. He is enjoying this now. If we can keep getting his form to rise over hurdles, we will come back on the Flat as he is still a young horse. We have always thought he is a horse that stays well and to be placed in an English and Irish Derby you have to stay well. It is just teaching him to run at fifteen seconds a furlong and not twelve seconds, but he is starting to do it. I was worried coming here on soft ground, but they have got to learn, and it was nice to see him do it today. It is a relief. He settled better today and I just love the way he battled. Usually, flat horses give up when they get headed, but he battled well and stayed well. We are still a long way off, but it is another small step back. He will get another couple of days' practice and the County Hurdle will be a right race for him at Cheltenham. There will be a big field, and they will go quick enough for him early on, and he will stay on well up the hill. We are a long way off, but he has got the class if he puts that together - James Owen, trainer.

quotes.race: Dubai Duty Free Irish Derby (Group 1) (No Geldings)
quotes.quote: Ambiente Friendly travelled really well to the two pole and just got outstayed in the last furlong. The winner and the second are both very good horses. I still think we'll probably be dropping back in trip next time - James Fanshawe, trainer.

quotes.race: Betfred Derby (Group 1) (British Champions Series) (No Geldings)
quotes.quote: I'm really thrilled with his run. Ambiente Friendly did absolutely nothing wrong. I thought coming to the two-furlong pole we had a real chance, and then obviously City Of Troy was back to his best, so we got beaten fair and square. No excuses, he ran a really good race and I'm delighted with him, and with the team back at home, who have done a great job. City Of Troy on his day is a very good horse, and so are we, but I hope there is more to come from him because he's still got a lot of maturing to do, so I'm looking forward to the rest of the season with him. He's taking his racing so much better now - he settled well today and stayed well, so there's a lot to look forward to - James Fanshawe, trainer.

quotes.race: William Hill Lingfield Derby Trial Stakes (Listed Race) (Colts & Geldings)
quotes.quote: That was exceptional. I've been riding Ambiente Friendly in lots of his work and he had come on so much from his run at Newmarket. They were much quicker conditions here, which he was unproven on, but he handled it beautifully. I couldn't speak highly enough of him - that was excellent. It felt to me like a proper trial. There was a nice even gallop and we got racing on the turn in, but I can't believe how he split the field so comfortably - Callum Shepherd, jockey.

quotes.race: British EBF 40th Anniversary Newcomers Maiden Stakes (For horses which have never run) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Ambiente Friendly showed us a little bit of ability at home, but you never know until you get them on the track and I'm delighted for the Gredleys that he's looked as impressive as he did. He'll have really enjoyed that today. They haven't gone quick and Tom has got him relaxed and in a rhythm and he went through the gears. It's a field of newcomers so you don't know what you've come up against but he's done it in nice style and hopefully he'll be a horse to follow - Tom Fanshawe, trainer's son and assistant, speaking on Racing TV.

stable_tour.quote: He hasn't lived up to the heights of his two great Derby runs and has run nowhere close to that form since. Now he's been gelded it makes sense to run him under both codes and we're going to start him off somewhere like Huntingdon early next month in a maiden hurdle. If he takes to it we'll carry on. If he doesn't we'll go back to the Flat. He schools really well and jumps very fast. If it goes to plan at Huntingdon, he'd go to Cheltenham for the November meeting. 24-10-25

runners.comment: Chance of finding the necessary progress largely depends on the effects of tongue-tie
runners.spotlight: Reasonably consistent but is 0-5 over hurdles, finishing fourth to Wilstar at Warwick most recently; chance of finding the necessary progress largely depends on the effects of first-time tongue-tie.

stable_tour.quote: He goes very well indeed and is one of our standout bumper horses. He's by a miler, but we're not just seeing loads of speed at home and I think he's a stayer as well. He fills the eye and hopefully he's a proper horse. 21-11-24

runners.comment: Made all at Wincanton most recently but this scenario is more demanding
runners.spotlight: Made all in Wincanton maiden (1m7f, good) in latest hurdles attempt, adding to his point/bumper wins and taking overall record to 3-6; however, this scenario is much more demanding.

runners.comment: Knocking at the door; possibilities, provided he shows progress on handicap debut
runners.spotlight: Flat winner in France and knocking at the door over hurdles for new yard, second to Wilstar at Warwick (2m) most recently; possibilities, provided he shows some progress on handicap debut.

stable_tour.quote: He's a nice horse from France. He won his maiden for Francis Graffard just before we bought him. He's by Golden Horn out of a High Chaparral mare so he's a real nice type. He looks to stay very well and handles a bit of cut. He's only just over 16 hands but he seems to grow a couple of inches when he gets moving. He's a very athletic horse and a lovely, flashy type. He seems to have taken to his hurdling very well. While we're obviously very much focusing on hurdling going into the spring, I can see him being a dual-purpose horse too and I wouldn't be surprised if he shows up on the Flat in late summer. He might need a break at some time but we'll play it by ear. He looks a real nice type for a couple of new keen owners. I thought he was exceptional value for €40,000 at the sales. 17-12-25

runners.comment: Related to several winners for his connections; may have potential off his opening mark
runners.spotlight: No match for Minella Yoga at Taunton, taking record to 0-6; however, he's related to several winners for his connections and may have potential off his opening mark; one to consider.

runners.comment: Prevailed in second-time hood at Taunton and may have more to offer in this headgear
runners.spotlight: Prevailed in second-time hood at Taunton (2m, good) most recently, adding to his Flat win, and may have more to offer in the retained headgear; in deeper waters today but could go well.

runners.comment: Even off bottom weight, this looks a difficult task upped in class
runners.spotlight: Flat winner whose hurdles form comprises a couple of second-place finishes and a late fall (beaten at the time); even off bottom weight, this looks a difficult task upped in class.

stable_tour.quote: He won on the Flat at Brighton last month and we're hoping to start him off over hurdles at Warwick next Tuesday in the same race Salver won a couple of years ago. He took to hurdling straight away and should make a nice juvenile. 28-10-25

racecards.verdict: Improving COSMIC CONNECTION is first choice ahead of Wilstar and Minella Yoga in a deep handicap.
racecards.betting_forecast: 7/2 Kadastral, 9/2 Cosmic Connection, 5/1 Minella Yoga, 10/1 Wilstar,  Kocktail Bleu, 12/1 Secret Sniper, 14/1 Talakan, 16/1 Stanners Glen,  Last Round,  Way Of Stars,  Dutch Corner, 20/1 Desertmore News, 25/1 Bespoke Tailor, 33/1 Legal Weapon,  Ambiente Friendly,  Race To Base,  Love You Back, 40/1 Kapitein Kool

racecards.race_name: bet365 Oaksey Chase (Grade 2) (For The Menorah Challenge Trophy) (GBB Race)

runners.comment: Two handicap wins this term but faces a stiffer task under 4lb penalty in this grade
runners.spotlight: Has registered a couple of useful handicap wins this season, including at Kempton (2m4f, good) on penultimate start; faces a stiffer task conceding weight all round in this grade, with 4lb penalty incurred.

quotes.race: Virgin Bet Supports Safe Gambling Handicap Chase (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Paul [O'Brien] said, which I think sums it up really well, that he's never had such a mad experience during a race of thinking Teddy Blue is too keen, now I'm going to pull up, now he's not going, now he's overracing, and then just around the home bend he's just thought 'oh I'll do it now'. He did the exact same thing here last year. I don't know what to say. Yesterday morning Rebecca, who rides him every day, was about to walk down the gallop and he just refused, so I said just take him to the warm-up area and do something else. He's just his own man. His owners are incredibly sporting - they ask me if he's in good form and I always say I don't know, because I don't! My travelling head girl Amy leads him out and if he sees the jockey before he gets on he refuses. Paul said when he got down to the start and saw the other horses he thought he was having none of it, and then he started running away with him. He's as mad as a march hare. This is a big pot and he won a big pot at Ascot at the start of the season. He's a really good horse. If he wasn't he'd be a right pain in the backside - Harry Derham, trainer.

quotes.race: Grundon Waste Management Handicap Chase (Premier Handicap) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Teddy Blue is a quirky horse. I trained him until about last March horrendously. I was trying to train him like a normal horse and one day it occurred to me that he's a bit mad and I needed to understand that. It took me a year to get to know him. All this spring I had it in my head that this horse is so well. He's very talented but just a bit mad. He could have another stone in hand, or no more in hand, he's his own man but I knew I had him right today - Harry Derham, trainer.

quotes.race: Virgin Bet Daily Price Boosts Novices' Limited Handicap Chase (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: If I'd gotten any more detached I probably would have given up hope too, but I was never that far back that I was going to have to pull up. Teddy Blue stayed and once he turned for home he knew the stables were ahead, and he duly took off. I think the hardest part was getting on him and getting him down to the start. He takes a bit of knowing and Harry and Paul O'Brien told me all about him, so it's a lot of thanks to them for the help - Brendan Powell, jockey.

stable_tour.quote: He's a fascinating horse and I've just about worked him out now. I've tailored his way of training - he doesn't do normal pieces of work, he likes following one. I think I train him less now and trust him more and it works well. He was very good when winning at Ascot and he'll go to Newbury on Coral Gold Cup day over two miles. 19-11-25

runners.comment: Defied top weight in Chepstow handicap last time, looking better than ever; leading claims
runners.spotlight: Has shown good form for new stable, mostly in handicaps, including at the Cheltenham Festival (3m1f); defied top weight at Chepstow (2m3f, good to soft) most recently, looking better than ever; leading chance at the weights in his bid for a second Grade 2 success.

quotes.race: Russell Property Consultants Handicap Chase (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Blow Your Wad and Freddie [Mitchell] suit each other, they have a good partnership and he's a quality horse. He was giving weight away, but his class shone through - Josh Moore, joint-trainer.

quotes.race: Coral Pendil Novices' Chase (Grade 2) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: We don't have any fancy plans and will bypass Cheltenham. Blow Your Wad likes a flat track and loves it here, which is why we came to this race. He's the best horse in Tom's yard, but he's been tricky to work out. He's quite quirky, but we've found the right track and right way round for him, so we'll keep doing that, although if we go to Aintree that's the other way round - Jerry Hinds, joint-owner.

quotes.race: Ladbrokes Boost Your Odds On Racing Novices' Limited Handicap Chase (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Stan Sheppard came in for some unfair criticism for his ride at Sandown. Some were saying that he let Le Patron have it all his own way in front, but it wouldn't have been fair for the horse to eyeball him on his first run over fences at the course. A flat track like here may suit Blow Your Wad too although he was on and off the bridle through the race. That said, all the way down the straight today I thought he would win. He's a lovely horse for the future and there's no doubt his owners will want him to go to Cheltenham. How we get there and what race we run in is for another day though - Tom Lacey, trainer.

quotes.race: Bet In-Play On Racing With BetVictor Novices' Handicap Hurdle (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: We've always thought an awful lot of Blow Your Wad, but he's shown his quirks. He'd never shown any signs of a wind issue, but we tracheal washed him one day and underneath his palate he had an ulcer, which suggests the constant flipping of his palate caused it. We sorted that out and he's galloped in a straight line all the way home, which is something he's never done before, so you wonder if his wind was catching him. The owners are very sporting and will probably want to go to Aintree for the two-mile-four handicap hurdle there. He could go back into a Graded race, but I think he's got quite a nice mark. I'd have thought he'd be chasing next season and we've loved him from the moment we had him, while I think he wants better ground - if anything that testing ground takes the speed out of him - Tom Lacey, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: He had a successful novice season over hurdles last term, winning twice, and made a pleasing start over fences when second to Le Patron at Sandown last month. The form has been franked with the winner going on to land the Grade 1 Henry VIII. He jumped really well at Sandown and the plan is to go for the 2m4f novice handicap chase at Kempton on Boxing Day. Cut in the ground suits him. 20-12-23

runners.owner: Exors Of The Late N W Lake

prev_owners.owner: Exors Of The Late N W Lake

runners.comment: Useful novice chaser who has Grade 2 form at Sandown and Windsor; one of the main players
runners.spotlight: Useful novice chaser whose form features second-place finishes in 3m Grade 2 events at Sandown and Windsor; came up rather short in Grade 1 at Aintree last time but looks one of the main contenders returned to this level.

quotes.race: ICL Conscious Of Our Impact 'Future Stars' Silver Bowl Novices' Chase (Excellence Initiative) (GBB)
quotes.quote: We sort of felt at Chepstow Doyen Quest waited for the others a little bit, so Harry [Skelton, jockey] was keen to be quite aggressive on him today, which he was. Credit to the horse, but even more credit to the jockey as that was a fantastic ride. We had a penalty and had to give weight to all the other horses and on official ratings we were wrong at the weights. He had a willing partner in Harry. He was aggressive on him, and he jumped fantastically, but it was one we probably nicked a little bit. We had to think outside the box a bit and it was good to watch. He could now go for the Coral Gold Cup. He needs a few to come out, and unless lots of rain comes, it will cut up a little bit. It is worth having a go at that, but I don't think we will make the running like that mind you! - Tom Messenger, assistant trainer.

quotes.race: From The Horses Mouth Podcast Handicap Hurdle (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: I was far enough back but we hadn't gone that quick and he jumped on the bridle straight away and put the race to bed quickly. You wouldn't know how good Doyen Quest is as he keeps a bit back for himself - Harry Skelton, jockey, talking to Racing TV.

quotes.race: Kingston Stud Handicap Hurdle (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: That was lovely. Doyen Quest was probably going to improve for a step up in trip and he likes a bit of better ground. A fast-ish run race round here suits him and he doesn't do a lot when he gets to the front so a lovely ride from Harry [Skelton] - Dan Skelton, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: I was gutted to see him get beat in the Listed novice chase at Chepstow last month - a decent jump at the last might have turned it round - but he put it right in a nice race at Exeter and he has an entry in the Coral Gold Cup, or we could look at another better novice chase. It's good to see him doing well over fences and I think there could be plenty more to come. 10-11-25

quotes.race: Phil Nelson Capercaillie Handicap Chase (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Etalon has not had the greatest winter but he's brought it all together when needed - Harry Skelton, jockey.

quotes.race: Team Forces "Ubique" Handicap Chase
quotes.quote: Etalon pulled a muscle right at the start of the season, so we just gave him a bit of time and he's come good. He was always going to improve for a fence and you can ride him any way and on most ground. Now we've given him that time he's very straightforward. We ran him in the EBF Final last season and while he did stay two and a half miles he's more of a two miler and will stay at that for now. I should think we'll go to Aintree for the Grade 1 race [Maghull Novices' Chase] -

quotes.race: Unibet Edward Courage Cup Novices' Limited Handicap Chase (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Etalon is a good horse, chasing was always going to be his game and he's now beginning to repay Ian's (Lawrence, owner) patience. It was good to get him some more experience and we'll likely keep him to handicaps and maybe look for something a bit bigger in the spring. He jumps well and is an exciting horse for the future - Tom Messenger, assistant to trainer Dan Skelton.

stable_tour.quote: He had a frustrating season last term but got it all together at Perth late on and I was very happy with how he ran on his latest run at Fontwell. He has a few issues we have to work with, but he's got plenty of ability and hopefully he can have a productive year over two miles to two and a half miles. 10-11-25

runners.owner: C Nightingale & Hold My Beer Partnership
runners.comment: Consistent in handicaps for current yard but faces a harder task upped in class
runners.spotlight: Broadly consistent in handicaps for current yard and ran respectably in the Topham at Aintree (2m5f) most recently; made all, despite jumping left, at Huntingdon (2m4f; also on good to soft) the time before; this is a harder task.

quotes.race: Green Diamond Handicap Chase (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Mahons Glory is great, isn't he? He gets in a rhythm out in front from fence to fence and is such a nice horse to ride. I thought with the two fences being dolled off it might cost us a bit, but he travels out on his own and loves it. It rode slow enough on the chase course, which helped. He seems to have lumped 12st round there nicely, so hopefully Dylan can find an opportunity somewhere to try and pick up a nice prize - Lee Edwards, jockey, speaking on Racing TV.

quotes.race: Betting And Gaming Council Novices' Limited Handicap Chase (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: You wouldn't say Mahons Glory was sour, but he needed a change of scenery, so we said we'd give it a go. Lee [Edwards, jockey] schooled him a few weeks ago and was very confident that he'd run well - Dylan Cunha, trainer.

quotes.race: Ladbrokes Get Best Odds Guaranteed Handicap Hurdle
quotes.quote: It didn't go to plan the last day but Mahons Glory still ran a cracker. We came here knowing he was in super form and the last day just knocked some of the gas out of him as he was very fresh. We've changed a few things like putting a new bit in his mouth for today and I think he'll have a future over fences. I think he's a graded horse and I'm not sure the three mile hurdling division is that deep and he'd be rated high enough to be thinking about those sorts of races - Patrick Neville, trainer.

quotes.race: Jewson Birkenhead, Price Street Maiden Hurdle (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: We didn't really expect it because we thought Mahons Glory would need it, like lots of mine who are needing the run. There are a few quirks in there but he's got a lot of ability. He's not the easiest horse to keep sound, and that's the challenge, but he's definitely got an engine. I think we'll look for a novice with a penalty somewhere - Dr Richard Newland, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: He's had a couple of little issues, but we've sorted them out now and he seems to be in great form. We put him over fences and he was second on his first run. Then we took him to Perth and he got a bit worked up. He's settling better now and we've freshened him up, and he might go back to Kempton on Boxing Day for the handicap hurdle he won last year. Otherwise, he might have an option over fences. He's got loads of ability if we can get his head right. 11-12-24

runners.comment: Ran well in notable handicap at Plumpton last time; possibilities if he stays the new trip
runners.spotlight: Chase record is 5-11, the most recent win at Uttoxeter (2m4f, good) last spring; seen only twice since but ran well in a notable handicap at Plumpton (2m1f) the latest time; possibilities at the weights, provided he stays the new trip.

quotes.race: Clarke Chase (A Handicap Chase) (For The Sir Stanley And Lady Clarke Challenge Trophy) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Matterhorn was a little better up in trip and it seems to suit him. He was a bit outpaced last time at Plumpton, but that was a good performance off 12st. He needs goodish ground and that was perfect for him. He's run two good, solid races and he's beginning to relax in his races, which has been the key. I'll come up with a plan with Johnny [de la Hey, owner] to see whether we run somewhere in the summer or wait until the autumn. He seems to be improving and we were thrilled with his performance - Paul Nicholls, trainer.

quotes.race: BetGoodwin Sussex Champion Chase Handicap Chase (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: We're thrilled, both horses ran blinders. Matterhorn has probably run a career best and he'll keep going on this ground - Paul Nicholls, trainer.

quotes.race: John Murtagh 60th Birthday Handicap Chase (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Matterhorn is going the right way very rapidly and we've got 12 months with him as a novice as well. His jumping is fantastic and that'll put him in good stead in the handicaps or novice chases. What we might do, subject to a discussion with Johnny [de la Hey, owner], is go for a 25,000GBP chase in August. We might then give him a break and try to pick up a nice early October novice chase if the ground is fast - Paul Nicholls, trainer.

quotes.race: Racing To School Bridgwater College Novices' Hurdle (GBB Race) (Div I)
quotes.quote: Matterhorn is a smart horse, sadly he struggles a fraction with his breathing. Hence flat track good ground is made for him. I think there's another race two weeks today in a National Hunt novices' hurdle he can run in with a 10lb penalty, and then I dare say we'll go chasing with him, because after December 1 he's not a novice any longer - Paul Nicholls, trainer, speaking to Racing TV.

stable_tour.quote: He's made his name as the flagbearer among our summer jumping team but he's better than that and has improved into a pretty smart chaser. Last season he was over the top by the time the big autumn prizes came along, so we've saved him this year in the hope of getting dry autumn ground, and he's had a break since putting up a career-best when defying top weight in a valuable handicap at Uttoxeter in May. We were just stepping him up in the work when he had a little setback last month; nothing serious, but it held us up a bit and I hope we haven't missed the boat as the one thing he must have is decent ground. 04-11-25

runners.comment: Ex-French 6yo who has the worst chance on RPRs in this British debut
runners.spotlight: Formerly trained in France; recorded a chase win at Auteuil (2m6f) last May but has failed to repeat the form since; has the worst chance on RPRs in this British debut.

racecards.verdict: Solid-looking BLOW YOUR WAD has the best chance in a substandard edition of this prize. Doyen Quest is second pick.
racecards.betting_forecast: 7/4 Blow Your Wad, 15/8 Doyen Quest, 7/2 Matterhorn, 9/1 Etalon, 16/1 Mahons Glory, 25/1 Teddy Blue, 33/1 Ventura Highway

runners.comment: Difficult to place and has the worst chance at the weights back up in class
runners.spotlight: Has proved difficult to place since last win in March 2025 and form has taken a downturn of late; has the worst chance at the weights back up in class.

quotes.race: Virgin Bet Every Saturday Money Back Handicap Chase (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Brookie hasn't run badly all season and has been freshened up after taking on Sir Gino at Kempton last time. I knew conditions would suit and it's worked out perfectly - Ben Godfrey, rider.

quotes.race: Boodles Novices' Limited Handicap Chase (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Brookie had three goes over fences in Ireland so we thought jumping around here would be okay. He was safe and sound and there should be another day - Sam Twiston-Davies, rider.

quotes.race: Adare Manor Opportunity Maiden Hurdle (Div I)
quotes.quote: Brookie is a nice horse and he's had plenty of experience. Hopefully, he'll make a nice chaser. He jumps very well - Tony Martin, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: We were quite keen to run in the Shloer but the ground was too toiling for him and instead we went for the Hurst Park at Ascot on Saturday. If you watch him, he was literally getting shoved along after three fences, and it was just the ground. It's the first time for a long time that he's let us down, but it had been raining all day and that's the first time we've tried him on ground like that. He seemed all right after the race and perhaps we'll look at something back at Doncaster, where they tend to get decent ground. 23-11-25

He's new to us from Tony Martin. The owners are based in the Isle of Wight and wanted to have him closer so they could see him more. He won well at Fontwell on his first start for us last week. We'll have a crack at a decent race now, possibly the £60,000 2m handicap hurdle at Ascot on November 4. We'll also keep chasing in mind and we could make that switch this season. He's most effective on good ground. 12-10-23

runners.comment: Admirable veteran but perhaps needs further now; beaten twice in this contest
runners.spotlight: Admirable veteran, albeit isn't quite the force of old and gained this season's win in substandard Grade 2 at Kempton (2m4f); also perhaps ideally suited by further than about 2m nowadays; beaten twice in this race.

quotes.race: Coral Silviniaco Conti Chase (Grade 2) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Edwardstone is been the best horse I've ever ridden.  I was wishing it was two miles halfway round, because you cannot go quick enough with him in a race. He won well, but it's tinged with sadness and condolences to connections of Kalif Du Berlais. For everything he's done for my career he holds a special place with us. Whether or not we see him again I'll leave it up to [Alan] Kingy and the owners. Retirement was something I was talking to the travelling head lad on the way out about, because if he'd been beaten today he would have been on a nice mark for the Grand Annual. Now he's won, unless the handicapper reads into it probably and we get dropped a few more then it might be slightly difficult to place him now - Tom Cannon, jockey.

quotes.race: Sky Bet Peterborough Chase (Grade 2) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: I'm delighted. I came here today thinking are we going to be retiring Edwardstone or not, but I don't think we will be retiring him put it like that. You always want to win, but that was great. We are not going to come back in trip, but I might even go up in trip - Alan King, trainer.

quotes.race: Shloer Chase (Registered As The Cheltenham Chase) (Grade 2) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Edwardstone ran very well. As he's getting older it's a little harder getting the weight off of him but I think he's run a grand race. We left a bit of work on, no doubt Nicky [Henderson] is the same [with Jonbon] but we'll take him on again in the Tingle Creek. It's probably pointless as it's 4-0 to Jonbon but there's a lot of money at stake. I think we'll stick at two miles. I'm very satisfied - Alan King, trainer.

quotes.race: Betfair Exchange Game Spirit Chase (Grade 2) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Edwardstone enjoyed it. We've come back in trip with him and it's worked out. He felt like a proper machine. He won the race in the first mile and had plenty under the bonnet. On his day he's as quick as I've ridden. I've always been his biggest supporter and on his day he can do things like this - Tom Cannon, rider, speaking to Sky Sports Racing.

quotes.race: Betfair Tingle Creek Chase (Grade 1) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Tom [Cannon, jockey] thinks Edwardstone is still as good as ever, we've just got a superstar in front of us. I couldn't be happier with him. This really wouldn't be his ground but he's run a hell of a race and we're very proud of him. We'll have a chat with the owners and we might try one run at the start of next year over two and a half miles and decide whether he goes Ryanair or Champion Chase. The Ascot Chase is probably in my mind but we'll see, I would like to avoid today's winner if I can - Alan King, trainer.

quotes.race: Betway Queen Mother Champion Chase (Grade 1) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: I have never been happier with Edwardstone and he has never missed a day at home, but he was beaten after two fences and just never going at any stage of the race. I cannot blame the ground as he has won on it before - I  just don't know what it is, I am at a total loss. But something must be amiss and hopefully something will come to light - Alan King, trainer.

quotes.race: Albert Bartlett Clarence House Chase (Grade 1) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: I'm not happy to have got beat but I'm very happy with the run. Edwardstone was just a bit fresh and started to tank down the hill. Tom (Cannon) said he had to bring him back just a wee bit. He's probably used a bit of energy up getting there and probably at the last I thought we'd go away and win, but full marks to the winner. I'm happy, I needed to get this into him to try and get him right for the March meeting. He's perfectly fit but he needed this just to get the edge off of him. In the Kempton race he only got to the fifth, so that did nothing. He was just a bit gassy. I did stress to Tom beforehand that this wasn't the be all and end all so I'm perfectly happy - Alan King, trainer.

quotes.race: Ladbrokes Desert Orchid Chase (Grade 2) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: They're both fine and there will be another day. Normally Edwardstone is very good but Tom said they just weren't meeting it right. He's got to have his flu jab next week and I'd imagine we'll stick with the game plan and go to Newbury for the Game Spirit next - Alan King, trainer.

quotes.race: Betfair Tingle Creek Chase (Grade 1) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: I owe Nicky a huge thank you for letting me take Edwardstone to Seven Barrows last week as we got a proper bit of work into him over a mile one. It was just to get him away and get a proper blow into him. Whatever he did today he was going to come on for it. He is a big heavy horse and that is why we couldn't risk him earlier in the season. I know there has been a lot said about it but we do know what we are doing with these horses. I had in the back of my mind that we would go to Kempton Park for the Desert Orchid but I will see. We are working back from the Queen Mother now. Whether we go one or two runs I don't know. The Game Spirit will come into it but it is a nice problem to have. I really wanted to get today out of the way. He has exceeded my expectations. The Tingle Creek is one of my favourite races - Alan King, trainer.

quotes.race: Poundland Maghull Novices' Chase (Grade 1) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: I think Edwardstone has run his race, I just think the winner is a very good horse and perhaps a fresher horse as well. The best horse on the day has won but I'm thrilled with our horse - Alan King, trainer.

quotes.race: Sporting Life Arkle Challenge Trophy Novices' Chase (Grade 1) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Edwardstone had a break after Kempton, and Warwick is what we wanted. He was running very well in those big handicaps last year but we used to have to put him out the back but he was still finishing fourth or fifth making up 20 lengths. Now over a fence we can ride him just off the pace and that is lot easier. People have doubted his jumping but I've not had to many worries about it - Alan King, trainer.

quotes.race: Virgin Bet Kingmaker Novices' Chase (Grade 2) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: That was lovely, they went a good gallop and Edwardstone jumped superbly so we were thrilled with him. He looked foot perfect so I'm delighted and relieved to come through it. It's a long time between Kempton and Cheltenham so it was important to get a run into him. It was a proper test and he came through it well, so we'll enjoy today and worry about Cheltenham when it comes - Alan King, trainer.  Edwardstone was very good today and loved that ground, it was as quick as he's been on for a while. His jumping was electric and he saw it out nicely. He's always had an engine and everything he's done in his career has built up to this season. He's the best horse I've sat on - he's a horse of a lifetime and they don't come around very often - Tom Cannon, jockey.

quotes.race: Close Brothers Henry VIII Novices' Chase (Grade 1) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Edwardstone has got a great cruising speed. I'm thrilled with him. We couldn't win a bumper but he met some superstars along the way. He was progressive over hurdles and we tried him over fences last year. He unseated at Doncaster and it was too late to keep going but his form back over hurdles last season was as good as ever. He was always hopefully going to make a chaser. We got a nice confidence-booster into him last time. I didn't really want to come here. If I could have found a two-miler with a penalty I probably would have gone somewhere else but they weren't around. He's bred for a trip but doesn't need any further yet. He's had three fairly quick runs so it's a nice problem to have now. I hope and think he's an Arkle horse so we'll work backwards from there. The Kingmaker would be the ideal one but he'll probably want a race in between - Alan King, trainer.

quotes.race: Highflyer Bloodstock Novices' Chase (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: His jumping was super and we were delighted with him. We're relieved and we can look ahead now, though I have no plans for Edwardstone yet. I just wanted to get today out of the way. It's only 12 days since his last run so we'll go home and have a think - Alan King, trainer.

quotes.race: Sky Bet Supreme Trial Rossington Main Novices' Hurdle (Grade 2)
quotes.quote: I thought Edwardstone had done enough, he's still a good horse. I maybe should have waited a fraction longer but I didn't think I was going as well as Gavin Sheehan. I thought he was the horse to beat and then he stopped down to the last - Tom Cannon, jockey.

quotes.race: Play Casino At Virgin Bet Novices' Hurdle (Novices' Championship Hurdle Series Qualifier)
quotes.quote: Edwardstone did a lot wrong today and he still won. I could have done with them going a bit quicker but he has plenty of gears and he stayed well. A better race, when they go quicker, would suit him well. Two miles is his trip for the time being - Tom Cannon, jockey.

quotes.race: Frome Scaffolding Group EBF Stallions "National Hunt" Novices' Hurdle (Qualifier)
quotes.quote: I think I've been trying to win this race for 20 years and have had horses placed in it. Edwardstone is a very nice prospect and, with his seconds in bumpers, he was beaten by some good horses. He's a scopey horse and did a lot wrong in the first half of the race, ferociously strong and fresh. He will stay at two miles for the time being. - Alan King, trainer

stable_tour.quote: He's back in good order and seems to be working as well as ever - the whole team is very happy with him. The plan is he'll start in the Shloer Chase at Cheltenham in November, then we'll look at the Tingle Creek or the Peterborough. He won the Game Spirit and generally ran up to his best last season, and although he'll be 11 in January he hasn't been over-raced and I hope there are a few more races in him. 25-10-24

He's been a star for us back and I'm glad to say he seems to be working as well as ever - the whole team are very happy with him. He'll probably start in the Shloer Chase at Cheltenham in November, with a view to looking at the Tingle Creek or the Peterborough afterwards. He won the Game Spirit and generally ran up to his best last season and although he'll be 11 in January, like Trueshan hehasn't been over-raced and I hope there are a few more races in him. 07-11-24

runners.comment: Multiple Grade 1 winner; good record at Sandown includes form figures of 112 in this race
runners.spotlight: Multiple Grade 1 winner whose excellent record at Sandown includes form figures of 112 in this contest; perhaps ideally needs further now, having been upped to 2m5f for the second leg of this season's Ascot double, then posted a Ryanair effort (2m4f) that took his Cheltenham Festival form figures to 2222; leading player provided the drop back in trip doesn't backfire.

quotes.race: Ryanair Chase (Registered As The Festival Trophy) (Grade 1) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Jonbon has done his best and tried his heart out. He wants to protect that record (never out of the first two). It's amazing isn't it. He still wants to fight and I've never seen him jump better. We were umming and aahing about whether to get a bit more time into him after those two hard races at Ascot, but he did everything to tell us he was in great form at home. Take nothing away from the winner. If he was a bit below the boil there we are hardly going to come back at Aintree, but let's just see how we go. Look how he finished there. On that you'd say three would help. He could do three at Punchestown, but he'll tell us. They can tell us 90% how they are, but that 10% you need to be winning races like that, if it's missing because they haven't got over their last race...Those were two hard races at Ascot in proper winter ground and that probably told on him - Nicky Henderson, trainer.

quotes.race: Betfair Ascot Chase (Grade 1) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Jonbon ran the same sort of race that he did in the Clarence House. He looked in trouble on the bend but it was his stamina that got him home over two miles last time and it was his stamina that got him home today over two miles five, so there's no doubt he stayed. He's something very special and you don't get many like him. His record of never finishing outside the first two says it all. Even if he doesn't win he never lies down. You'd love to go to Cheltenham and win there, because he deserves to. We'll enjoy today and think about it. I remember when JP told us to buy him and we picked him up - we're lucky boys. He's something very special - Nicky Henderson, trainer.\We both missed three-out and then Harry [Cobden] kicked on, injected a bit of pace on the home bend and I was thinking, 'We're going to have to work here', and so it turned out. I trusted that Jonbon was going to keep staying and, although we met the last all wrong, he's very nippy with his feet and he keeps finding. He's just class. was very special and I think it lived up to everything it was billed to be. What a fantastic horse - Nico De Boinville, jockey.

quotes.race: BetMGM Clarence House Chase (Grade 1) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: There was a moment where I was kind of going through the motions on Jonbon thinking I wasn't going to get anywhere, but he came home strong anyway. It's a great feeling. I hit the wall turning in and I could feel him gaining and the crowd could obviously see it, so it's brilliant - James Bowen, jockey, speaking to ITV Racing.

quotes.race: Betfair Tingle Creek Chase (Grade 1) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: When the winner beat us here last year it was at the end of a long season, but today proves that over two miles he is a sharper horse than we are. You have to be tempted to look at going over further with Jonbon now. But let's just see. Nothing is in and nothing is out. We put the cheekpieces on him today and were always going to lead. The horse loved it today - he jumped and galloped. He has come on from the Shloer at Cheltenham to do what he has done today ? which probably would have been good enough to win the last two Tingle Creeks. There are no excuses with the ground. If you can't go on the ground on the chase course here today, you can't go on anything - Nicky Henderson, trainer.

quotes.race: Shloer Chase (Registered As The Cheltenham Chase) (Grade 2) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: I think Jonbon found it hard work. I think it's fair to say we're a little bit behind and Dan's horses are pretty fit, he just served it up to him today. I don't think his jumping is as brilliant as it can be in that ground, but we've got the run into him and that was the vital thing to do. If he didn't run today he wasn't going to get to the Tingle Creek and he's got to run there. We'll see them all in three weeks' time - Nicky Henderson, trainer.

quotes.race: bet365 Celebration Chase (Grade 1) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Jonbon is fine. It possibly came down to the fact he's been at it all year in all those Grade 1s. I think a high-class fresh horse has beaten a high-class, not-so-fresh horse. It's sad to end the season like that but well done to Willie [Mullins] and his team. I'd have thought stepping up in trip is possible. He got the two and a half miles  well at Aintree and he went flat out there. I wouldn't be surprised if we looked at three miles too but we've got a long summer to think about it. We'll be back for another campaign but I don't know over how far - Nicky Henderson, trainer.

quotes.race: My Pension Expert Melling Chase (Grade 1) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: You've got to admire two things there - Jonbon, who is amazing when he's doing that, and Nico [De Boinville, jockey]. He's been very brave, because it's been a tough little session, and to go out and ride him like that, that's a guy who had no fears. They went some clip - I don't know what the time was, but it must have been quick. Whether he's short or long [at his fences] - he's very clever when he dances, isn't he? To be able to do that - when he's long it's great, and when he's short, he's just very quick and in and out. It just went all wrong at Cheltenham, and it was proved today, he just loves doing that. That's what he does best. At Cheltenham the start went wrong, and he was on the back foot the whole way. He loves his own space. It was unfortunate, the tape went straight across his face and he went backwards. That was some gallop. Not many horses can jump that well that fast. We'll certainly think about going to Sandown again - Nicky Henderson, trainer.Jonbon was an absolute superstar today. He was incredibly brave and courageous when I needed him to be and he made the job easy. Credit to him, he's got us out of a tough period - Nico de Boinville, jockey.

quotes.race: BetMGM Queen Mother Champion Chase (Grade 1) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: We were stood up against the tape and the tape pinged back and went under Jonbon's nose. It just startled him for a moment then you are on the back foot and they have gone hard. I would say there was a stride there [at five out] but I think he might have lost his sight slightly and he decided to chip in and didn't think it was there. Then you are just trying to do what you can. He is some horse to manage to finish where he did - Nico De Boinville, jockey.

quotes.race: BetMGM Clarence House Chase (Grade 1) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Jonbon is not the most straightforward horse, but he's just a joy. What a performance. Nico [De Boinville, jockey] said he was very fresh and nearly too much on it. He was out and really up for it. He just wanted to do it and loves the game - Nicky Henderson, trainer.

quotes.race: Betfair Tingle Creek Chase (Grade 1) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Jonbon was up for a battle today. He's a very classy terrier because he just loves the scrap. He is the two-miler that I think can represent our country. We've got to fight against the enemy, who are going to come over in force - Nicky Henderson, trainer.

quotes.race: Shloer Chase (Registered As The Cheltenham Chase) (Grade 2) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Jonbon really enjoyed himself. I expect Nico will tell me he had a good blow between the last two and we now have three weeks until the Tingle Creek. That would be the perfect prep I would say. Like a lot of horses, as they get older they get further and he won over two and a half at Aintree last year which was no problem. But as JP [McManus, owner] said at the end of last season, we are a two-miler and we'll stay at two miles - Nicky Henderson, trainer.

quotes.race: bet365 Celebration Chase (Grade 1) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: It's great to see Jonbon come back and put on a display on like that. He's a brave horse as he had a hard race at Aintree and I'm proud of him. We had a three-week blip around Cheltenham but the horses are finishing on a good note. Jonbon is a flagship horse and there's a lot to look forward to. He means a lot to JP [McManus] and a lot to me - Nicky Henderson, trainer.

quotes.race: My Pension Expert Melling Chase (Grade 1) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Jonbon got into a lovely rhythm, that was perfection. I've never seen him jump better. He travelled well. I think the two and a half miles is probably ideal. I'm trying to get Nico (de Boinville) to say that he will stay three, but he is reluctant to say that at the moment, but we can think about those things throughout the summer. Should we have been thinking about the Ryanair this season, I don't know? When we did that with Shishkin and jumped him up to two and a half miles, we soon realised he wanted three miles. I'm not saying that about Jonbon at the moment - Nicky Henderson, trainer.

quotes.race: My Pension Expert Clarence House Chase (Grade 1) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Jonbon didn't see a nice stride at the last and if he'd have winged that he might not have let the other horse back. He's lost the battle but not the war.  He's quite a busy person, he lives on his wits a little and the extra wait from Ascot wasn't exactly what he wanted. He's a clock that you can wind up, now we can unwind him and go again. We were really looking forward to El Fabiolo last weekend and I don't think that's changed anything dramatically. We've got to let him off for a little bit and start the preparation for March - Nicky Henderson, trainer.

quotes.race: Betfair Tingle Creek Chase (Grade 1) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: There's only two options for Jonbon really - the Clarence House Chase at Ascot and the Game Spirit Chase at Newbury. He's growing up all of the time. I've mentioned before that we had a gallop at Windsor with him earlier this year and he was quite geed up by that and in his preparation. But at Cheltenham and since then he has been more settled and grown up. It was always going to be tough in this ground. We said to hang on to him for as long as we could as it is the sort of ground you can get caught out in. It was essentially to keep our power a little bit drier today. He's an attacker and you can really let him rip at fences but that would've been dangerous in these conditions. He's jumping very well this year - Nicky Henderson, trainer.

quotes.race: Shloer Chase (Registered As The Cheltenham Chase) (Grade 2) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: They went a good gallop and it wasn't a tactical race. It was a sensible, good, honest gallop in that ground. It was going to find Jonbon out first time if he wasn't ready, but he was (ready). You have to be very pleased. He was just pricking his ears on the run-in. He has had a nice time and he has enjoyed himself. He should come on for it. He looked like a two-miler there, and he has got to stay there for now because of the Tingle Creek. There is the conundrum as to how far he will get as I'm convinced he will get further but you don't need to - Nicky Henderson, trainer.

quotes.race: bet365 Celebration Chase (Grade 1) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Jonbon is exceptional. He's such a good horse. You can do whatever you want on him - he's so good, I've been saying that for two years - Aidan Coleman, rider.  My final deciding reason for running was we'd find out if he could take these two-milers on who he'd be meeting next year. If he can cope with them, around here, now, then we can start thinking of Tingle Creeks next year - and that's what he's answered - Nicky Henderson, trainer.

quotes.race: EFT Systems Maghull Novices' Chase (Grade 1) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Jonbon was good today wasn't he? I think he loves that slightly better ground after it's dried out a bit today. I think he was a better horse here than he was at Cheltenham, and that's in part because of the ground. That's the way he jumps when he's right. He jumped from fence to fence today and he didn't at Cheltenham. Aidan said on good ground he feels like a two-miler, although I've always thought he'd go as far as you like. We don't have to make any decisions today though - Nicky Henderson, trainer.

quotes.race: Sporting Life Arkle Challenge Trophy Novices' Chase (Grade 1) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: I've always thought he'd be better on better ground. Jonbon gallops like that, but he's done nothing wrong. He's come to have a crack at it and we were tracking Dysart Dynamo, whom I'm glad to see is okay - that's important, but El Fabiolo was doing the same to us. We'll definitely go further - I think he'd go as far as you'd like on good ground. We'll think about Aintree and you could certainly go two and a half miles as it's an easy two and a half there. All being well, they'll stay in Ireland and we'll go to Aintree. You wouldn't know how far he'd get in time though - Nicky Henderson, trainer.

quotes.race: Virgin Bet Kingmaker Novices' Chase (Grade 2) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: I'm going to look on the bright side. Jonbon has had such easy races, I think it took him by surprise when the other horse attacked him like that and he just shook his head. But he's done nothing wrong, he's not had a race since Aintree last year and I'm going to look on the bright side of it. It was his prep, it looked like it shook him a little bit and I'll get all the feedback off Aidan and AP - Nicky Henderson, trainer.

quotes.race: Close Brothers Henry VIII Novices' Chase (Grade 1) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: There's a certain amount of relief, I think everyone was expecting and hoping to see that and like at Warwick Jonbon was as good as you could wish to see, he's very clever with a very high cruising speed.  He was enjoying himself and can go both ways, when you're under no pressure you can afford to be careful and if you want to be showy and have a yahoo, he can do. He's a genuine two miler at the moment but I'd love to find out how far he can stay. Don't worry, we're not going anywhere else at the moment - we'll stay at two miles for now because he's so quick. He's doing everything right so far - Nicky Henderson, trainer.

quotes.race: Highflyer Bloodstock Novices' Chase (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: This was always going to be his game but Jonbon was a very high-class novice hurdler last season. There was only one horse better than him and he's safely tucked up at Seven Barrows hopefully ready for Saturday (Constitution Hill), so this was always going to be his game. It's what we hoped for but it's just a huge relief now it's over. He jumps and he gallops and it's a great racecourse and beautiful ground, so it was a good test for him. The fences have to be jumped here so it was a perfect start for him. This isn't a racecourse to take lightly for a novice over fences, but he was pretty flawless there. I liked how he was a bit long at the ditch and then he sort of danced in and he was perfect all the way. Most of our hoses are needing the run and coming on for it and I don't see why he won't be the same. He was fit enough to do what he had to do today minding that the timing wasn't ideal, as we couldn't find many races that could lead us into the Henry VIII at Sandown. We've got two and a half weeks now and it just gives us a bit of time before Sandown. You couldn't go there first time out so this has served its purpose - Nicky Henderson, trainer.

quotes.race: Betway Top Novices' Hurdle (Grade 1) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Jonbon has had a good campaign. He's a lovely, big, young horse and his future probably lies over fences. You have to admire him for the way he battled there, that was tough. He had to brave and he was, very much so. Constitution Hill was the only horse to lower his colours but you can't take that out on him, he's unbeaten otherwise. He's finished up getting his Grade 1 here. I'm pretty certain he'll go over fences next season and he'll get further, I'm sure he would. We had him in the two-and-a-half mile races at Cheltenham and here. He'll get that trip easily - Nicky Henderson, trainer.

quotes.race: Sky Bet Supreme Novices' Hurdle (Grade 1) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: That was a special performance by the winner, but Jonbon ran incredibly well. He's a free sweater but that's it - he's always the same. He's a pleasure to ride - Aidan Coleman, rider.

quotes.race: Sky Bet Supreme Trial Rossington Main Novices' Hurdle (Grade 2) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: It's a sharp two miles round here. The ground is tacky, and it was very hard work. Jonbon was flat out turning in but picked up well. I was very happy with the performance. He's such a pleasure to ride. I winged the third last and landed in the back of the other horse. He's so straightforward and we can stop talking about him being precocious because he's not. He's a lovely ride and he's beat a good field - Aidan Coleman, jockey.

quotes.race: Howden Kennel Gate Novices' Hurdle (Grade 2) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Aidan said you can do anything with Jonbon and he's extraordinarily professional for a horse that had so little experience. He was a cool dude the whole way around and he had them off the bridle a long way out off no gallop as his cruising speed is so high. We'll enjoy today, and I'd say it'd be one run before Cheltenham - Nicky Henderson, trainer.

quotes.race: Play Ladbrokes 5-A-Side On Football "National Hunt" Maiden Hurdle (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Jonbon's a brother to Douvan so he's got plenty of boot. He was on his toes and I call him a fidget, but he doesn't do anything wrong. We'll take it step by step and see where we want to go. He wasn't over-keen, but his jumping took him there. He was only in second gear and Aidan said he had to go on - Nicky Henderson, trainer.

quotes.race: BetVictor Standard Open National Hunt Flat Race (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: We're very lucky to be sent horses like this. You feel the pressure that comes with it. We were waiting and hoping for what we thought would, and luckily did, happen. There are plenty of these horses who don't turn out to what they're thought to be and it's just lovely to see him do what he did today. Jonbon relaxed, raced beautifully and quickened up well. Thanks to JP for letting us have him. He'll go back to JP's Martinsntown stud for the summer and we've all got a summer where we can dream of what might happen next season - I think he is a bit special. He's a gorgeous horse who has the looks and pedigree. I spoke to Derek O'Connor, who rode him in his point this morning and he came with big recommendations. It's only the first step of what I hope will be a long and successful career - he's something to look forward to. He's a bit of a fidget at home and wouldn't stand still for long, but he looks magnificent on it and is not a horse who worries about it. He can anticipate things a bit, but I was pleased with how he relaxed in the race and got on with the job - Nicky Henderson, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: The Ryanair is what we're thinking, but we'll see ? he doesn't have to go to Cheltenham. He's just been fantastic, and to get two Grade 1s in a month is incredible. It was a month between the Clarence House and Ascot Chase, so he can go to Cheltenham as it'll be another month. He's had two tough races, and I had thought that his tough race in the Clarence House might undo him for last Saturday, but there he was, fighting away. He's come out of it well and looks as fresh as paint. I want to go because the one thing missing from his CV is a festival win. He's won at the track, but he does get beaten there too. Robin [Land], who looks after him, and Paddy [Murphy], who rides him every day, are my eyes and ears, and if they say he's up for it, then we'll go. 18-02-26

runners.comment: Return to shorter may not be an issue but he ideally needs a drop back in class
runners.spotlight: Form since upped to 2m4f comprises a handicap win at Musselburgh and fourth-place finishes in Grade 1 events at Cheltenham and Aintree; return to shorter may not be an issue but he ideally needs a drop back in class.

quotes.race: Ryanair Chase (Registered As The Festival Trophy) (Grade 1) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Lovely run. We knew what we were coming into it, but JPR One got us excited. He loved it up front and he ran as well as he could ever run. It's where he is, really. The horse has had probably his best ever season, he brings us to day like this and he gets your blood up coming down the hill. He just didn't quite see it out, but if he's alright we'll take him to Aintree then we'll take him to Punchestown, round flat tracks, and just enjoy him. He's been a solid horse all his life - Joe Tizzard, trainer.

quotes.race: bet365 Scottish Champion Chase (For The Bowes-Lyon Trophy) (A Handicap) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: It was a really good effort. We came up here for the ground and JPR One loved stepping up in trip. It was a classy performance. Even though he's the best horse in the race, he still had to give all that weight away and I'm chuffed to bits with him. He's going to get hiked up the ratings again and he's not going to win a Champion Chase, but, without discussing it with anybody, we'll probably have a look at the Ryanair - Joe Tizzard, trainer.

quotes.race: BetMGM Haldon Gold Cup Handicap Chase (Grade 2) (Limited Handicap Chase) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: JPR One is a really good horse. He is my future and he could go right to the top, but I won't run him lots of times. The second half of last season he never really got his ground - it was as simple as that. He will have an entry in the Tingle Creek. Today was what we were thinking about though. He has won over two and a half miles over hurdles, but I don't think we need to think about that just yet - Joe Tizzard, trainer.

quotes.race: Download The Racing App Now Lightning Novices' Chase (Grade 2) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Today was the best we've seen JPR One and it was quite a comfortable watch because he travelled great and he's got a fair bit about him on his day. We've always held him in really high regard. Had he not had that stumble at Cheltenham, he was going to look majorly impressive, and the ground took its toll in the Henry VIII at Sandown. He's only a novice for one year and he's beaten the best of the English novices today, so we'll have a crack at it (Arkle) - Joe Tizzard, trainer.

quotes.race: SSS Super Alloys Arkle Challenge Trophy Trial Novices' Chase (Grade 2) (Reg' As The November) (GBB)
quotes.quote: That's racing. Luckily the horse and Brendan are alright and JPR One looked like he was going to win very impressively. He jumped from fence to fence and jumped the last well but just crumpled a little bit. We know we've got a horse to go to war with. This was the lovely next step and he didn't come down five out leaving us without knowing more. He was about to put up a proper performance, I've no doubt about that, and these things happen. I half thought about the Henry VIII but I might need to give him a confidence boost so we'll see - Joe Tizzard, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: He travelled well enough and stuck at it well in the Haldon Gold Cup last week. The two in front of us were race-fit and put us in our place a little bit, but the handicapper has dropped us a couple of pounds and I'm going to take him to Ascot next week for the Hurst Park as he's been bucking and squealing on the gallops. I might just change tactics with him, too, as he could enjoy pinging along in front. He was going to make all when he fell at the last in the Arkle Trial, so it's definitely worth revisiting. 12-11-25

He's in great form and schooled pleasingly last week. He's set for the Lightning Novices' Chase at Lingfield on Friday and a dry forecast is good for him. I felt in the Henry VIII, he travelled like the best horse everywhere, but didn't get home and I think he was just struggling on the testing ground when he made a mistake two out. I wasn't massively disappointed with that, but he does have a good action and skips off the ground. Hopefully we'll have a strong spring campaign with him and he'll be entered in the Arkle. 18-01-24

runners.comment: Needs to prove he can back up the form of 50-1 success in Grade 1 novice at Aintree
runners.spotlight: Belied his 50-1 odds with 6l success in Grade 1 novice chase at Aintree (2m, good to soft) two weeks ago; however, needs to prove he can back up that form and Harry Skelton prefers solid stablemate Thistle Ask.

quotes.race: Hallgarten & Novum Wines Maghull Novices' Chase (Grade 1) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: I've no idea how that happened, but I said to the lads beforehand that the only time Mirabad has run moderate for us was at Bangor, where he probably got stuck in the ground, and you can have a bad day. I said to Tristan 'drop him in, go thieving, and nick what you can, and you never know'. It was always going to be a strong pace and Be Aware has probably run better there than he has done all season in third. It's just amazing - Dan Skelton, trainer.

quotes.race: JCB Hydrogen "Chasing Excellence" Beginners' Chase (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Mirabad jumped particularly well. It was his first time over fences and I wanted to pop him out and get into a nice rhythm. He can race quite keenly but the hood helped, and the fences backed him off a bit, so it was a good performance. On the rising ground he just relaxed on me. Joyeuse came by me but he's tough and he picked up again - Tristran Durrell, jockey, speaking to Racing TV.

stable_tour.quote: He's made a great start to his chasing career and is one of those horses who will always give his running, so we'll leave him in the Arkle until the 11th hour to see if it cuts up a little, but at this stage it looks as though there are five or six strong contenders in there and we wouldn't want to turn up hoping to be fifth or sixth. If a few came out, we'd go there looking for the best place we could get, but otherwise he'd be more likely to go to Aintree. 17-02-26

runners.comment: Close second in similar event at Aintree last time, showing career-best form; major player
runners.spotlight: Smart front-runner whose Grade 1 form features three wins at Leopardstown (2m1f) in 2024/2025 and neck second, showing career-best form, at Aintree (2m4f, good to soft) on latest start; one of the main contenders back down in distance.

quotes.race: JCB Melling Chase (Grade 1) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: When he's on his A game Solness is a very good horse. We skipped Cheltenham to come here. It was a really good run but the winner is a very good horse - JJ Slevin, jockey,

quotes.race: Paddy's Rewards Club Chase (Grade 1)
quotes.quote: Solness is particularly good at Leopardstown and is tough as nails. I feel sorry for J J [Slevin] but a fantastic ride from Sam [Ewing]. Looking forward to coming back here in February - Joseph O'Brien, trainer, speaking to RTE.He took me everywhere, got in a nice breather down the back and Solness was as game as you get from the back of the last. He's a very clever jumper - Sam Ewing, jockey, speaking to RTE.

quotes.race: Ladbrokes Dublin Chase (Grade 1)
