quotes.quote: I could see Solness running a big race in the Champion Chase. He'll jump and go and they'll have to come and get to him to beat him. That's the way he likes to run. Aggressive tactics worked, he jumped brilliantly and I thought what he did from the last to the line showed real tenacity because he was there to be shot at the whole way. He has a will to win, and Danny got a breather into him between the third-last and the second-last and that was probably the winning of the race in the end. He just keeps going forward - Joseph O'Brien, trainer.

quotes.race: Paddy's Rewards Club Chase (Grade 1)
quotes.quote: At one stage I was planning to run Solness in a maiden at Dundalk last Friday, but we decided to supplement him. We thought he had a real live each-way chance but the ground was a little bit slower than he maybe ideally likes. We said we'd go as wide as we can to get the best strip we can - Joseph O'Brien, trainer.

quotes.race: Bar One Racing Fortria Chase (Grade 2)
quotes.quote: Solness ran great. He's been really consistent over the last while. The ground will probably be getting a bit too soft for him in the coming weeks. While the ground stays dry, he will stay on the go. We will see, he might go to the Hilly Way too if he has his ground - Joseph O'Brien, trainer.

quotes.race: Kerry Group Handicap Chase
quotes.quote: Solness travelled well the whole way and toughed it out when the other horse came to him. He is a class horse - Sean Corby, assistant trainer.

quotes.race: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Beginners Chase
quotes.quote: Solness had a nice run first two when he was very keen. In a stronger race we would probably drop him in, but if there was no gallop today he was going to let him bowl along. He's a very good jumper and he likes soft ground - Brendan Powell, assistant traibner

stable_tour.quote: He might go to Aintree but he'll remain entered at Cheltenham and it'll be a last-minute decision with the owners. Majborough's aggressive style kind of broke his heart at Leopardstown, so it might make sense to avoid him, but we'll see closer to the time. 19-02-26

runners.comment: Progressive; may reverse Ascot placings with Jonbon returned to better ground; 5-5 on good
runners.spotlight: Front-runner who has shown excellent progress over fences and whose record for current stable reads 11112, the last two wins in Grade 2 handicaps; collared by Jonbon in soft-ground Grade 1 at Ascot (2m1f) when last seen; may turn the tables returned to forecast ideal ground, being 5-5 on good; possibly hasn't reached his ceiling yet; respected.

quotes.race: Ladbrokes Desert Orchid Handicap Chase (Grade 2) (Limited Handicap Chase) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Some horses are a bit timid when they get taken on but Thistle Ask gets his teeth out for that kind of thing. He's fabulous; someone wants to go as fast as me, let's go!'. He's an absolute credit to the whole team because before today he'd gone up 35lb. He's going to go up against different types of horses now, but we'll welcome all-comers and we'll give it our best shot. It's very tempting to have a go at a Champion Chase, but if you want all ticks in your boxes, then he's got to go right-handed. If he wins a Clarence House he'd have to go for it, but if he didn't and still ran well, then you'd have to keep him super fresh for the Celebration Chase - Dan Skelton, trainer.

quotes.race: BetMGM Haldon Gold Cup Handicap Chase (Grade 2) (Limited Handicap Chase) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: This is down to Dan [Skelton, trainer]. I go out there to do a job but it takes a set of balls to do what he has done. Thistle Ask is a horse that likes to gallop, jump and run. He is made for me, he's a bit numb, and just keeps going. We had a light weight and plenty of experience with some runs under our belt. We just wanted to make use of that. The way Dan has placed this horse - it takes some bravery to do what he has done - Harry Skelton, jockey.

stable_tour.quote: Three weeks ago I didn't think I'd even be running him in a Haldon Gold Cup but he's thrived on his racing and what he did on the day was quite remarkable. He received two good rides from Tristan Durrell when winning at Kelso and Wetherby and another from Harry [Skelton] at Exeter, where he took our breath away. We'll give him a little freshen up now, he'll go to Kempton over Christmas for the Desert Orchid and there should be more good days to come. He's a real credit to the whole team. 10-11-25

racecards.verdict: Back on good ground, THISTLE ASK is taken to reverse Clarence House placings with Jonbon.
racecards.betting_forecast: 6/4 Jonbon, 7/4 Thistle Ask, 7/2 Solness, 12/1 Mirabad, 16/1 JPR One, 33/1 Edwardstone, 66/1 Brookie

racecards.race_name: bet365 Gold Cup Handicap Chase (Premier Handicap) (GBB Race)

runners.comment: Won this race (good ground) last year in first-time cheekpieces off a 10lb lower mark
runners.spotlight: Won this race (good ground) last year in first-time cheekpieces off a 10lb lower mark; first and second in two small fields this season, alongside two heavy defeats in top handicaps; tried blinkers when fading right out of it at the Cheltenham Festival last time and now reverts to cheekpieces; also back on firmer ground but a new career best is needed.

quotes.race: Colin Parker Memorial Intermediate Chase (Listed Race) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Resplendent Grey feels like he has matured a bit. I was wary that Ben's [Pauling] horse was having a good look, and I didn't want to challenge too early. He picked him up well from the back of the last. It just turned into a sprint and for a horse that has won over three and a half miles, he sprinted pretty well from the back of the last. Ben's horse is a stayer as well, and I was conscious that I would catch him on the hop and when Gavin [Sheehan, rider of the third Hollygrove Cha Cha] came round my outside I said make sure you don't challenge him too early as he was having a good look. My lad managed to pick him up because he was looking round. Hopefully the Coral Gold Cup is where he'll go next and that was a lovely prep run. I said at the start of the season that I hope he will end up as my Grand National horse. Hopefully he will get there and turn up in that form - Sean Bowen, jockey.

quotes.race: bet365 Gold Cup Handicap Chase (Premier Handicap) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: We rode Resplendent Grey differently today to Cheltenham. He got an exhibition ride from Sean and the cheekpieces helped him. He came home strongly and that was a good way to win a big one - Olly Murphy, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: He's a massive price for the Gold Cup. He ran very well at Windsor last time and we'll freshen him up and go straight there. If there's a small field for the Gold Cup, we might just roll the dice. When he's good, he's very good, but when he's bad, he can throw in a stinker. He got a bad start in the Coral Gold Cup and needs things to go right for him early, but, when they do, he's got the ability to run well. The Ultima is an option as well, and we've given him an entry in the Grand National. 12-02-26

He ran a cracker to finish second in the Persian War but he had a hard race. He's getting 7lb off the handicapper, so we'll have a look at a handicap or a novice hurdle at Cheltenham this month before potentially jumping a fence with him, as he loses his novice status at the end of the month. He has grown up an awful lot and went through his race at Chepstow better than ever, so there's lots to look forward to. 01-11-23

runners.comment: Six races in last 14 months were a mixed bag, Ascot 3m win in November the clear highlight
runners.spotlight: Seems best making the running or racing prominently; his six races in the last 14 months have been a mixed bag, with an Ascot win (3m, good) in November the highlight; just 1lb higher today and ran respectably on penultimate start, but his two earlier attempts at 3m6f/4m did not work out; a tongue-tie (worn twice in 2023, with a win on first occasion) returns.

quotes.race: Sodexo Live! Gold Cup Handicap Chase (Premier Handicap) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Henry's Friend just got in such a good rhythm. He was jumping and travelling beautifully, and he wouldn't be fit. Ben Jones was just filling him up when he could and it was a class ride. When that horse is in that form, he's not for passing. That was an absolutely awesome performance. He's going to get a mark that would probably get him in the Grand National. He's obviously got the right sort of profile for Aintree and we'll have to make a decision - Ben Pauling, trainer.

quotes.race: Coral Mandarin Handicap Chase (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Henry's Friend jumped well today and we know he stays all day. He's got a good heart and he tries, and I was pretty confident from three out. It was nice to see him pull out and hit the line hard. He loves it here. He looks to be improving again and it's onwards and upwards with him. He was an improving novice but he went off the boil when he got to the festival last year. The National Hunt Chase was probably the wrong race, but the Coral Gold Cup has put him right and he's going the right way - Tom David, assistant trainer.

quotes.race: Sodexo Live! Reynoldstown Novices' Chase (Grade 2) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Henry's Friend didn't jump well early doors and we were fortunate they didn't go a good early gallop. He was brave from the back of the last, his jumping got better and he keeps improving. He wants every yard of that trip and he'll be a lovely staying chaser in time. He's got an entry at Cheltenham but I doubt he wants to go there at this stage. We might look for something at Aintree - Ben Pauling, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: I was delighted with his win at Ascot and he'll now go back there for the Howden Silver Cup in December. He seems very well suited by that track and he's only gone up 3lb, so hopefully he'll be competitive again. 07-11-25

He is an interesting horse as he has only had the one run for us when romping home by 20 lengths at Aintree in May. He had not shown a great deal at home prior to that outing so to see him win so easily was a very pleasant surprise. It is on the track where it matters and hopefully he will continue to progress. He was very green at Aintree but he has done well over the summer and is almost ready to start off again this season. I'm not sure the race he won was up to much, but he could not have done it more easily and should be interesting. 26-10-22

prev_owners.owner: Nick Case, Syd Hosie, John Romans

runners.comment: Hacked up at Ascot and second in 4m2f Midlands National; jumped to his left two runs ago
runners.spotlight: 2-14 record over fences includes some big runs, including when he hacked up at Ascot (3m5f, good) in November and took second in the Midlands National at Uttoxeter (4m2f, soft) on latest outing; the Ascot race was going this way round but so was his penultimate start when he kept jumping to his left at Musselburgh (12l second to Transmission); that's a niggling concern but he's handicapped to go well if this is another good day.

quotes.race: JenningsBet Midlands Grand National (Handicap Chase) (Premier Handicap) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Rock My Way ran a blinder. He travelled great and jumped like a stag. When he gets into a rhythm like that, he runs big races. I thought he had them beat three out but he couldn't quite shake Paul's horse off. We'll probably go to Punchestown for the staying handicap chase on the Saturday - Joe Tizzard, trainer.

quotes.race: Windsor Horse Rangers Berkshire National Handicap Chase (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: The Welsh National has always been the plan. The handicapper will have his say after that but Rocky My Way jumped like a stag and bolted up. He's always been consistent but he's never done anything like that. It was a beautiful performance to watch and he actually put himself in the Grand National picture after that - Joe Tizzard, trainer.

quotes.race: Ballymore Novices' Hurdle (Registered As The Classic Novices' Hurdle) (Grade 2) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Speaking to Tom (Scudamore) there we will probably step Rock My Way up in trip. He wanted a bit more of a lead and he got to the front early enough and he had a look around. We could have done with a bit more of a pace there. We had Way Out in the race as well and at home he runs all over this horse every day. I might need to put a longer gallop on! I thought if we can get him in the top three I won't look stupid for the entries we have made for the Ballymore and the Albert Bartlett and I'm glad about that. We will get him home and see where he is really - Syd Hosie, owner-trainer.

stable_tour.quote: He's a smashing horse. He got tired on his first run of the campaign at Cheltenham, having travelled into it well. I might just look to drop him in grade for his next run to get his head in front, and then aim him at the Welsh National. I'd like to think there's a big one in him - he ran extremely well behind Haiti Couleurs in the National Hunt Chase, and in the Scottish National. 12-11-25

runners.comment: Neck 2nd to Ask Brewster in the Kim Muir at Cheltenham (3m2f, good; furthest he's been)
runners.spotlight: He was set to be the only Willie Mullins runner in last week's Scottish National but was withdrawn due to the heavy ground; 7yo who was delivered with what seemed a winning challenge under Patrick Mullins in the Kim Muir at Cheltenham (3m2f, good; furthest he's been) six weeks ago only to find that Ask Brewster battled back; up 6lb but has to be in serious calculations.

quotes.race: Happy Birthday Margaret Watling Maiden Hurdle (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Road To Home's jumping at speed needs work as at the second-last and the last he was a bit careful. I don't mind that too much, but I wanted to win as easy as I could because we might go to Fairyhouse and Punchestown with him. I think he's a nice horse - Patrick Mullins, rider, speaking to Sky Sports Racing.

runners.comment: 12l win at Musselburgh (3m7f) with a first-time visor; fair third to Havaila at Plumpton
runners.spotlight: Tapped back into last season's initial promising form, and then some, to win by 12l in the Edinburgh National at Musselburgh (3m7f, good to soft; from Rock My Way) in February with a first-time visor, which has been kept since; ridden by 7lb claimer when fair third off this 8lb higher mark behind Havaila in the Sussex National at Plumpton 19 days ago but needs to hit new heights again.

quotes.race: bet365 Edinburgh National Handicap Chase (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Transmission can jump a bit right but has form around Cheltenham. We'll be looking at races like the Midlands Grand National, Scottish Grand National and bet365 Gold Cup, which we won with The Young Master. Conor's [O'Farrell, jockey] been a part of the team for the last year and a half now, and he knows the horses and the owners. He's in three or four times a week and he's doing a great job - Neil Mulholland, trainer.

quotes.race: Steel Plate & Sections Ltd Amateur Jockeys' Handicap Chase
quotes.quote: We could maybe look at the National Hunt Chase now long-term. Today was the plan as we wanted to give Transmission a couple of runs around Cheltenham. His last run was good, he had a run under his belt and has course and distance form, so we tried to tick as many boxes as possible, and the ride was second to none - Neil Mulholland, trainer.

quotes.race: Extech Racing To The Cloud! Handicap Hurdle
quotes.quote: I'm not too sure this was an easier ride for Joe than in January - he was flat out from the word go and had to push him for a long way today. Transmission loves Plumpton and was very gutsy. They went fast enough for him today and fingers crossed he'll be an exciting staying chaser for the future. We'll see how he comes out of the race and we'll speak to his owner Paul McKeon about if we want to run him again this season - Neil Mulholland, trainer.

quotes.race: BetGoodwin Sussex Stayers Handicap Hurdle (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Thank god that's over and done with. I lost my irons and I thought Transmission was going down, so he did well to stand up. I kept going for one of my irons but it went over the other side of my saddle as I was trying to get it back. Every time I moved he started lighting up, but when I jumped the last with a circuit to go he settled away and was able to get it then. It's a good job that he's very good at jumping. He took a massive step forward the last day, he did again today and is going the right way. He has a lot of ability and we've put it together for a good pot - Joe Anderson, jockey, speaking on Sky Sports Racing.

stable_tour.quote: He's a good, solid horse who took well to chasing and had a very good season last term. The ground was a little bit quick for him on his return at Cheltenham, but we expect our horses to improve for their first runs - it's a long season - and he may go back this weekend, when he has a couple of options. He could be a horse for the bet365 Gold Cup. He was in it last year but the ground was a bit quick and Willie Mullins' topweight kept him out of the handicap. 12-11-25

He goes to Uttoxeter on Midlands Grand National day for the £100,000 2m7½f handicap hurdle. It's a good pot and it needed to be looked at as the prize-money is the same for the Pertemps. We wouldn't be looking at the Albert Bartlett. He missed the second-last hurdle at Sandown when he was just starting to get into it. He ran on well but it didn't go 100 per cent according to plan. We won the £75,000 race at Plumpton and fingers crossed he can still be competitive and make his presence felt. You'd think he'd make a nice chaser - perhaps he could be a Welsh National horse given he likes soft ground. 06-03-24

prev_owners.owner: Walters Plant Hire & James & Jean Potter

runners.comment: Not firing on all cylinders this term; first-time blinkers replace his usual cheekpieces
runners.spotlight: Withdrawn from Scottish National last week due to the heavy ground; 6lb lower than this time last year (when third in the Scottish National) as he's not fired on all cylinders this term, but excuses can be made; he's won two major 3m handicaps going right-handed (Ascot and Kempton) on good ground, back in the 2022-23 season admittedly but this 11yo may be dangerous to dismiss, including as first-time blinkers replace his usual cheekpieces.

quotes.race: Coral Trophy Handicap Chase (Premier Handicap) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: I've got no real faith in the runners at the moment just with how the form of the yard is. However, this lad stays forever. I was a bit worried down the back straight but when I saw Our Power turning in, I was quietly confident. He would have run in the Ladbrokes Trophy at Newbury but he had a little setback and we had no other option but to train him for this, which is a fantastic race itself. I'd say he would be doubtful to get in at Aintree so it will be Cheltenham for the Ultima then he will either go for the Scottish National or the bet365 Gold Cup - Sam Thomas, trainer.

quotes.race: Bateaux London Gold Cup Handicap Chase (Premier Handicap) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Our Power will never win by too far. He's your typical horse off the Flat - he's streetwise and is not ever going to over-exert himself. But he's genuine and we'll aim him at the Coral Gold Cup. We wouldn't have got in off a mark of 137 so he had to win. Fingers crossed that will sneak us in. You'd think a flat track like Newbury will suit him. Sam Thomas, trainer, speaking to Sky Sports Racing.

quotes.race: Racing TV Novices' Limited Handicap Chase (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: There was a lot of pace on (at Doncaster) and Our Power reached for the first but didn't quite get there. Sam (Thomas) had said he had been fantastic since and thankfully he was right. It was very tacky holding ground and I'd say he would get a bit further. He has a good way of racing as he doesn't use energy up and his jumping is getting better - Sam Twiston-Davies, jockey.

quotes.race: St. James's Place Juvenile Hurdle
quotes.quote: I was slightly disappointed with Our Power at Exeter, but I think he's a better horse this way round; he went badly left at the first at Exeter, but we've done a lot of schooling since. That was much better and he probably outstayed the second. I'll speak to the owners but we might look at Cheltenham at the end of January. The Finale comes too soon and Wayne said he wouldn't want it any softer than today; he's handled it only just - Alan King, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: He had a nice prep run and then ran in the Coral Gold Cup. He was in a good rhythm and Adam Wedge was very happy with him before he fell - it was too far out to know how he would have fared. He came back sore from that and we're trying to get him back to 100 per cent before deciding on where to go next. I wouldn't have thought we'll be aiming him at the Grand National at the end of the season as he didn't quite get the trip last year. 05-01-24

runners.comment: Good third this winter in 3m handicaps here and at Ascot; needs to build on that
runners.spotlight: 3m6f for the NH Chase at Cheltenham last March was his only attempt beyond 3m and he was below form; that was also his last run for Venetia Williams (bought for £220,000 in October at the David Maxwell dispersal) and he's been a good third this winter in 3m handicaps here and at Ascot; needs to build on that, as he's edging up the weights, but he's not fully exposed.

quotes.race: BetMGM Handicap Chase (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: I never thought In D'Or would jump a fence but he's actually got a lot of scope. He could make into something quite nice in time but Venetia is an expert at letting them grow into it. Trying to find these lovely, young staying chasers is why we do it - David Maxwell, owner/rider.

stable_tour.quote: He could be an interesting one. We were going to run him at Ascot last weekend but the ground was going to be too soft. He hasn't won for us yet but his two runs have been very good and we're thinking about the Ultima. 19-02-26

runners.comment: Plenty of best runs have been at this track but other runners have more pressing claims
runners.spotlight: Seventh in this race in 2023 and fourth on good ground in 2024; missed all of 2025 and although he ran encouragingly on reappearance here (3m, soft; 50-1) seven weeks ago, still disputing the lead when making a mess of the second last, others have more pressing claims.

quotes.race: Read Nicky Henderson's Unibet Blog Handicap Chase
quotes.quote: Certainly Red stays further than three miles so we knew he'd get home on soft ground. He's coming on nicely and will be on the go until about April - Lydia Richards, trainer.

quotes.race: Weatherbys nhstallions.co.uk Handicap Chase
quotes.quote: We were fed up about Certainly Red's last run, he was brought down but it wasn't his fault at all. We've had to wait two and a half weeks for another race and he's been stood in his box wondering where he's going. I was pleased with that. Marc [Goldstein] said he was a little keen to start with, jumped well and then cantered away. He's been to Henrietta Knight's which has been the secret weapon. She did a little bit of work with him and his jumping today wasn't a problem at all - Lydia Richards, trainer.

quotes.race: Virgin Bet Free Bets For Winners Handicap Chase
quotes.quote: The drying ground and the combination of that and going right-handed meant Certainly Red started hanging. He can jump better than that - Marc Goldstein, rider.

runners.comment: Won easily by 7l at Newbury and 5l at Plumpton (3m5f Sussex National, good) last two races
runners.spotlight: A rising force in the last 15 months and that's gained serious momentum in his last two starts, when winning easily by 7l at Newbury (extended 2m7f, good to soft) and 5l in the Sussex National at Plumpton (3m5f, good); strong-travelling sort who's now seeing out his races really well too; up another 10lb but could still have more in the locker.

quotes.race: BetGoodwin Sussex National Handicap Chase (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Havaila travels very strongly and jumps superbly. He seems to love this better ground and he's still on the up. He has lots of scope and it would be nice if he could get in the Scottish National. It could suit him as they go quick - Caoilin Quinn, jockey.

stable_tour.quote: Consistent over fences and at a range of trips last season, he might do well again this term. He's a big horse and dad likes the idea of running him at Ascot. There could be a bit of improvement in him. 28-10-25

We bought him out of Sir Michael Stoute's yard after four runs on the Flat. I have given him a bit of time and he should be ready in the next three weeks. He gallops like a real staying three-year-old, and I like his willing attitude to please, which is a big plus in any horse. 13-10-22

runners.comment: Bit to prove right-handed but otherwise lots to like, likely to be suited by trip/ground
runners.spotlight: 3m4f resulted in an 8l win at Cheltenham last April and he's won over 3m/3m2f in two of his three starts this season; latest was the Kim Muir at Cheltenham in which he was always front rank under Shane Cotter and responded admirably when Road To Home joined him on the run-in; up 7lb but this trip makes plenty of appeal and all five chase wins have been on good ground or good to firm (withdrawn from Scottish National last week due to the heavy); has a bit to prove going right-handed, with a run here in December prompting concern, but otherwise lots to like.

quotes.race: Rosconn Group Fulke Walwyn Kim Muir Challenge Cup Amateur Jockeys' Handicap Chase (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Yesterday we needed soft ground for Libberty Hunter and today we needed good ground for Ask Brewster, so when it rained this morning we thought 'oh no'. But we knew they were both in great shape and we've come away with a first and a second. Ask Brewster stays, and we had a very good boy on board. I don't know him, but I think Evan [Williams] and Conor Ring spoke to a couple of the Irish lads and that's who we got - Cath Williams, trainer.I watched a few replays, and any time Ask Brewster was in front he seemed to love it and winged his fences. I jumped him out nice and handy and he ran away nearly to the first, and I knew it was his day then. He was very game when Patrick [Mullins] came to us - Shane Cotter, jockey.

quotes.race: Brooklands Watches Golden Miller Racing Holman Handicap Chase (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: I thought Ask Brewster won well on spring ground at Chepstow and he travelled, jumped and stayed well. My concern was if he'd stay but he was strong at the line. He's a young horse and there's no doubt he's improved. We can train him for next spring and he could be a horse for the Scottish National next season. Evan Williams - trainer.

stable_tour.quote: A progressive sort who ran well at Sandown last time despite the ground being far too soft for him. Before that he won over 2m7½f at Chepstow, a good effort considering he'd gone up 9lb since his previous run at Cheltenham in April when he won a 3m4f chase. He must have a fast surface and, when he gets it, he's a really good staying handicap chaser. 14-01-26

runners.comment: Firmly on upgrade; can prove well handicapped if he gets this trip, which is feasible
runners.spotlight: Half-brother to top-class Protektorat; withdrawn from Scottish National last week due to the heavy going; made three notable steps forward on varied ground over 3m at Ascot (unraced here) this season, including for a good prize on latest start when he led two out for a clearcut win; raised another 4lb but he's firmly on the upgrade, likely to prove well handicapped if he gets this trip, which is also feasible; a bold show is on its way.

quotes.race: Full Circle Series At Punchestown Festival Handicap Hurdle
quotes.quote: I was really disappointed with Montregard at Newcastle but I think the cheekpieces have helped him here and he's toughed it out well - Tom Lacey, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: He's a nice horse of JP McManus's who won his maiden at the second attempt over hurdles when last seen at Warwick in April. I was really pleased with him that day; he was green but toughed it out and stayed on nicely. I'd say he's progressed through the summer and is set to return in a 0-105 handicap hurdle at Uttoxeter on Friday. He'll ultimately jump a fence too. A nice prospect. 20-12-23

runners.owner: J P McGrath & R N Pallas
runners.comment: Jumped poorly on heavy in Scottish National (40-1) last week; this race also looks tough
runners.spotlight: Ex-Irish 11yo (six races for current yard) who has not won since 2022 but went close with first-time cheekpieces (kept since) over 3m2f at Newbury in February; second of three at Ascot (3m) in another veterans' race next time was creditable in the end, after he'd been detached at one point; that helps to envisage him as a stayer but he jumped poorly on heavy in Scottish National (40-1, pulled up) last week and this race also looks tough.

quotes.race: Guinness Galway Blazers Handicap Chase
quotes.quote: I thought Gabby's Cross was fantastic there. He's a funny sort of a horse but he relaxed lovely today and he did it really well. He's quite quirky at home and he can be difficult to ride but the lads have done a brilliant job with him in Knockeen - Rachael Blackmore, jockey.

quotes.race: BetVictor Novice Handicap Chase (Grade B)
quotes.quote: Gabbys Cross really tanked with Rachael but she settled him. I was thinking of the novice handicap chase at the Punchestown festival for him - Henry de Bromhead, trainer.

quotes.race: Shop Local Online Rated Novice Hurdle
quotes.quote: Gabbys Cross got a great ride from Rachael. He was a bit weak last year but seems to be really improving this year. There is a novice handicap hurdle at Leopardstown which we will look at is he's eligible - Henry De Bromhead, trainer

stable_tour.quote: Hopefully he can win off his hurdles mark soon. He ran really well at Galway and the plan is to go for the Pertemps qualifier at Punchestown this coming weekend. 20-11-23

runners.comment: Commendable over 3m3f/3m7f in three of his four starts this season; place claims
runners.spotlight: Failed to fire in the Eider at Newcastle on penultimate start; commendable otherwise this season, making all in the Southern National at Fontwell (3m3f, good to soft), fourth in Welsh Grand National at Chepstow (3m7f, good to soft) and short-headed at Exeter (3m7f, good) five weeks ago; raised another 2lb but has place claims.

quotes.race: BetGoodwin Southern National Handicap Chase (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: We're delighted with Livin On Luco; he's possibly a horse who goes better fresh. He won first time out last season. He jumped particularly well, so we're delighted with him - Philip Hobbs, joint-trainer.

stable_tour.quote: It was a great win at Fontwell first time out - he's possibly a better horse fresh and won first time out last season as well. I'm not sure where we'll go with him next. 20-11-25

runners.comment: Won over extended 3m4f last term; this from 2lb out of handicap demands big personal best
runners.spotlight: Won Sussex National at Plumpton (extended 3m4f, soft) last February in his first long-distance race but less convincing since in forays over 4m2f, C&D and 3m5f; had a small-field 2m4f win on good ground here in November but this race, from 2lb out of the handicap, demands a big personal best.

quotes.race: BetGoodwin Sussex National Handicap Chase (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Invincible Nao saw out the trip well and Caoilin [Quinn] gave him a very good ride. I think he was pretty confident with what he had underneath him to get up. He's not a straightforward horse and huge credit has to go to Archie Silburn, who rides him at home. He's really made a difference to him as he was freegoing two-miler before - Josh Moore, joint-trainer.

stable_tour.quote: One for the regional nationals. He disappointed us in the Midlands National last season, but the ground was horrible. He's come back looking better than he did last season and we'll probably target the London National at Sandown in December. He wants soft ground. 28-10-25

racecards.verdict: A right-handed track might inconvenience Ask Brewster, so MONTREGARD (nap) is selected ahead of Havaila and Road To Home.
racecards.betting_forecast: 4/1 Montregard, 9/2 Havaila, 5/1 In d'Or, 7/1 Road To Home,  Ask Brewster, 12/1 Resplendent Grey,  Livin On Luco, 14/1 Rock My Way, 16/1 Henry's Friend,  Transmission, 20/1 Our Power, 25/1 Certainly Red,  Invincible Nao, 66/1 Gabbys Cross

runners.comment: Has become an exciting force for current stable and is the one to beat, back down in trip
runners.spotlight: An exciting force since joining current stable and sent beyond 2m, gaining impressive wins at Haydock (2m3f handicap) and Cheltenham (2m4f Grade 2) then shaping like the best horse in the Grade 1 Stayers' Hurdle (3m) until his tank emptied late on; the one to beat, back down in trip.

quotes.race: Paddy Power Stayers' Hurdle (Grade 1) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Kabral Du Mathan just didn't stay. He travelled unbelievably, jumped brilliant but just didn't see it out. We're proud of his effort and we did the right thing running him, the result didn't quite work out. We'll go two and a half miles with him. He's put too much in so we won't ask him to go to Aintree. I think we'll go over fences, that's what Harry [Skelton] said when he got off him. That'll be exciting - Dan Skelton, trainer.

quotes.race: Dornan Engineering Relkeel Hurdle (Grade 2) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: If we were going to step up the ladder Kabral Du Mathan had to go and win today and he has, very nicely. We've got to remember how young he is and it's never the wrong thing to take the patient approach. We'll have to have a debate now about what we do. In my heart I think I trust him enough to relax enough and get the three-mile trip, but the question is can he stay three miles hard as a six-year-old when you're against those battle-hardened horses who have been doing it for eight to ten runs over many years. It's not an easy call. If you come back in trip you make two bad decisions: one is that in the short term he's not a two-miler and in the long term when he goes up to three we've been teaching him to race over two, so we definitely won't be doing that. It will be Cheltenham or Aintree - Dan Skelton, trainer.Kabral Du Mathan was very good. He was obviously favoured at the weights today, getting the weight off the other, but he put the race to bed really well and winged the last. He doesn't race like a three-miler, he's got a bit of boot and our options are probably now open where we go with him. But that was a big race for him, Grade 2, and they're hard to win. But it looked coming into the race like he would take a bit of beating and so it was - Harry Skelton, jockey.

quotes.race: Betfair Racing Podcasts Handicap Hurdle (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: I hoped Kabral Du Mathan would win. He did a very good bit of work in a gallop about three weeks ago, which suggested to us that he had a big engine. But to be honest his form last year suggested that, and we are lucky to have inherited him in such good shape. Hopefully he is a horse that can continue to progress as he goes up in trip. He's been crying out for a trip. We have to look forward now. I think we might go for the Relkeel with him and then maybe on to the Stayers' Hurdle - Dan Skelton, trainer.

quotes.race: Ladbrokes Handicap Hurdle (Premier Handicap) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: We're thrilled and for a four-year-old it was a mighty run. Kabral Du Mathan will go straight to the Betfair Hurdle [February 8] now, we won't run him before then and we'll look after him. It's hard for four-year-olds in their second season, but that was a very good run and he's a progressive horse - Paul Nicholls, trainer.

quotes.race: Weatherbys Chatteris Fen Juvenile Hurdle (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: It was a very pleasing performance. Kabral Du Mathan has done everything nicely in Ditcheat. When they come over from France you don't know what to expect, and we were very nervous about having to give all of these eight pounds. He has jumped brilliantly, done it all very professionally, and I think he has done it quite cosily. Hopefully he might be one for the Fred Winter in March. I think he is more a Fred Winter horse as to be a Triumph Hurdle horse you have got to be a really good horse, and you would have to take on Burdett Road, and Sir Gino looked very smart the other day - Charlie Davies, assistant trainer.

stable_tour.quote: I'm still not saying we'll definitely go to Cheltenham but I'd say we're more likely to head for the Stayers' Hurdle than we've been at any time so far. His work has been very good and we only didn't run him at the weekend because of the ground. He comes into the race from a pace angle, needing to prove he gets the trip against some guaranteed stayers, so we were thinking of going to Aintree instead, but Cheltenham is now a distinct possibility. 17-02-26

runners.breeder: E Aubree & Mrs J Goffin Van Aken
runners.owner: Mrs G Van Geest & M George
runners.comment: Finished behind Kabral Du Mathan and Jingko Blue on penultimate start
runners.spotlight: Dual Grade 2 winner last term; finished third at the same level on penultimate start but was behind Kabral Du Mathan and stablemate Jingko Blue in that Cheltenham race; seems set for another bronze medal at best.

quotes.race: Dornan Engineering Relkeel Hurdle (Grade 2) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Lucky Place is an absolute terrier. He doesn't know when he's beat and galloped all the way to the line. I think we'll be stepping up in trip again because he saw out today's trip on soft ground. On spring ground in March, I think three miles [in the Stayers' Hurdle] is where we'll end up - Nico de Boinville, rider.

quotes.race: Howden Ascot Hurdle (Grade 2) (Registered As The Ascot Hurdle) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: That was plan B unfortunately. I'm not going to bang on about it but Lucky Place was meant to be going novice chasing but I couldn't see anywhere to go, so we brought him back into here instead. He jumps fences beautifully but maybe we'll keep that until next season now.  We're going to have to have a look if he stays three and whether he's a Stayers' horse. We could look at the Relkeel Hurdle on New Year's as a stepping stone - Nicky Henderson, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: The intention was to go novice chasing last year as he jumped beautifully at home, but we had nowhere to run him so we slipped him into the Ascot Hurdle, which he won. He then won the Relkeel on New Year's Day and we went to the Stayers' Hurdle, but I don't know if he stayed or not. He's going novice chasing this season, staying at two and a half miles for now, and I think we'll be very disappointed if he doesn't take very high rank this season. He has a wonderful temperament and is a very kind horse in every way, so I think he can go to the top. 21-10-25

runners.breeder: B Decouz & S C E A Du Bas Bugey

prev_owners.owner: SAS Racing D & Olivier De Seyssel

runners.comment: Raced mostly at about 2m and isn't crying out for this step back up in trip
runners.spotlight: Form dipped in Cheltenham Festival handicap returned to fences last time; multiple Grade 2 winner but has raced mostly at about 2m and isn't crying out for this step back up in trip; first go beyond a sharp 2m4f.

quotes.race: Ladbrokes Christmas Hurdle (Grade 1) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: I was pleased with Rubaud, he's finished behind last season's Champion Hurdler and horse who could win this season's. I might leave chasing until next season. We'll look at races like the National Spirit and the Kingwell if the ground is right - Paul Nicholls, trainer.

quotes.race: BetMGM Elite Hurdle (Grade 2) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Rubaud had a very hard race the other day at Kempton Park, and he knew he had a race the other day, and it took a while for him to get over it. I could tell in the paddock that he didn't look great in his coat, and he has been a bit flat this week. We have had to do the best we could to get him right. When we went to Kempton, he had a lot of hard work and he was ready for his life. This week we have had to do things a bit different to freshen him up. He is a good horse that is tough and keeps galloping. Testament to him as what a class horse he is that he can come back from a very hard race and win today. We know he is not going to win a Christmas Hurdle, so I don't want to waste a run. He has won two good races now and if he doesn't run until after Christmas I don't mind. He is the sort that could run well in the Silviniaco Conti Chase over two and a half miles as he won the Pendil there last season. There are no more Grade Two races like this until the Kingwell Hurdle back here or the International Hurdle at Cheltenham, but the ground is too soft for him there. The Kingwell will be a possibility - Paul Nicholls, trainer.

quotes.race: Ladbrokes Pendil Novices' Chase (Grade 2) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: I am amazed Rubaud has won. I thought down the back he was in a bit of trouble. As Harry said, he hates ground that like. It's the first time he has won on soft ground and he's a much better horse on better ground. He had a hard enough race at Warwick the other day and two weeks is quick enough but he toughed it out and stayed on really strongly, which was a doubt over this trip. I'd say we'll freshen him up now and go to Aintree for the two and a half mile novices' chase (Manifesto Novices' Chase) - Paul Nicholls, trainer.

quotes.race: BetMGM Elite Hurdle (Grade 2) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Rubaud is a fantastic horse and is improving. We'll go chasing now. He's a brilliant jumper, he's a big, scopey horse and that's his future now. We'll go to Kempton for the Wayward Lad but if we found a beginners chase we could look at that. I'd be happy to go straight to Kempton though.    He beat two good horses that are rated higher than him and giving them 6lb. He'll be brilliant when we go chasing - Paul Nicholls, trainer.

quotes.race: TrustATrader Approved And Reviewed Trades People Hurdle (Listed Race) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: That was awesome. Rubaud is going to be a chaser at some point, but I don't need to when there are good hurdle races and there are no novice chases at the moment. Wincanton is the obvious target, then go chasing after that - Paul Nicholls, trainer.

quotes.race: JenningsBet Elite Hurdle (Grade 2) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: The plan is to go to the Christmas Hurdle on Boxing Day then come back here for the Kingwell after Christmas. When these horses start improving you don't know where they'll end up and the Christmas Hurdle will give us a marker where we are. Someone has got to take Constitution Hill on. We'll go there and if we finished second we'll be delighted. Rubaud will be be a lovely two-mile chaser next season and we'll just pick our races with him this season - Paul Nicholls, trainer.

quotes.race: Trustatrader Approved And Reviewed Trades People Hurdle (Listed Race) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: I thought Rubaud looked big enough for his first run of the season, so he's going to improve and he'll go to Wincanton in three weeks for the Elite Hurdle. That was always the plan; here and Wincanton. He stays on strong and goes a good gallop, so I'm thrilled with him. It suits him going right-handed and we'll probably run him in the Christmas Hurdle as then as something has got to finish second to Constitution Hill. It's good prize-money so we'll go there and we'll stay hurdling this season and then go chasing next autumn as he's only five. We did think about fences, but I thought he'd improve hurdling and we just lacked a horse of what I'd call his calibre to do those Wincanton races, the Elite and Kingwell, which would suit him quite well. He doesn't want a bog, while he's not slow, but is a staying two-miler  - Paul Nicholls, trainer.

quotes.race: Coral Scottish Champion Hurdle (A Limited Handicap) (Grade 2) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Rubaud had been a bit keen earlier in the season but we still thought we'd try to ride him positively. He's been improving all the time, it was the best thing I ever did not running him at Aintree last week on the soft ground. He'll be some two-mile chaser next season, I can't wait - Paul Nicholls, trainer.

quotes.race: Sky Bet Dovecote Novices' Hurdle (Grade 2) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Rubaud won twice earlier in the season making all at Taunton. The ground was a bit soft here on Boxing Day, and the whole thing went wrong in the Betfair Hurdle as he got a bit lit up. Today was much better. He relaxed and jumped great and galloped on strong. He had a bit of form in France before he ran here last year but he made a bit of a noise and he bled that day, so he had his wind sorted out and we gave him some time. That was what he done earlier in the season at Taunton, he absolutely bolted in by going from the front. He is a good horse - he has just got to learn to relax a bit more. We won't go for the Supreme as we have Tahmuras for that and he is probably not ready for that. You are not going to dominate around there. Aintree is probably a bit easier for a front runner. I think a flat track suits him nicely and we will keep him nice and fresh, and though it is a big step up we will go for the Grade 1 over two miles at Aintree. The exciting thing is he will be a lovely two-mile chaser next season - Paul Nicholls, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: What a wonderful horse! He began his season in the now usual manner, by winning the Listed hurdle at Kempton for the third year running. It was disappointing the feat merited little more than a passing mention in the press. We'll now seek to continue following a well-worn path and look at the Elite at Wincanton on Saturday, a race he has also won for the last two years. Alternatively, he could switch to the Haldon Gold Cup a day earlier if the ground at Exeter came up too fast for Kalif Du Berlais. His chasing career, which I'd long looked forward to, had been delayed last season because he was doing so well over hurdles, mopping up those Grade 2 prizes with regularity. He finally got to jump fences in public at Christmas when outclassed behind Sir Gino. We then lowered his sights and he gave L'Eau Du Sud a fright in the Kingmaker before winning the Grade 2 Pendil, a contest we love to target. That victory, over 2m4f, gives us more options for this season, as does the fact he coped surprisingly well with the soft ground at Warwick and Kempton. Whatever happens later this week, it will be fences after that and we'll look for a valuable pot on a flat, right-handed track - something at Ascot would suit ideally. In January, the Grade 2 Silviniaco Conti Chase over two and a half miles is another decent prize I'd consider. He's so tough and consistent that I have no doubt he'll be adding to his tally. 04-11-25

runners.breeder: Mrs J Rainer, Mr F Jereczek & Mr Rainer
runners.comment: One of the main contenders, albeit may struggle to reverse placings with Kabral Du Mathan
runners.spotlight: Has shown good form over 2m4f/2m5f at Cheltenham this term, finishing second to Kabral Du Mathan in Grade 2 and recording an emphatic success from the front in Festival handicap; failed to get home in 3m Grade 1 at Aintree last time; one of the main contenders, back down in distance.

quotes.race: BetMGM Cup Handicap Hurdle (Premier Handicap) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: I thought James [Bowen] was interesting - it wasn't exactly the plan to make the running, but he did it exceptionally well, didn't he? It was great. Jingko Blue is not the easiest horse to keep on the right side of - when he's good, he's very talented, but he's not the easiest. His jumping has never been? We tried him over fences and he won over fences, but? This was the obvious race to come for. He's not a slow horse, but he got an easy lead there - normally the pace is flat out. Great pace-making by James! At least the owner [Tony Barney] has got a day to calm down before Jango Baie in the Gold Cup - he might need it ! - Nicky Henderson, trainer. Plan A went completely out of the window, then B and C! I never intended to make the running but I winged the first and the next thing I was there, doing nothing. It felt good when I winged the last because he doesn't always come for you, but he did today. He got in a great rhythm and I was able to take him back the whole way, then when we got between four out and three out I was able to roll on into it. I jumped that one well and from the top of the hill to turning in it just worked out well. It's quick ground and I feel like we went slower today than yesterday when I won the National Hunt Chase. It was always going to suit the ones on the front end and I'm just glad it was me - James Bowen, jockey.

quotes.race: Hampton Novices' Chase (Grade 2) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: We were hoping Jingko Blue would stay three miles so I think he'll continue down that road. This was never the plan but then they put this race on and it's a great effort. We weren't really prepared for this because we were waiting for the Reynoldstown. I think there's every chance he'll still go there and then onto Cheltenham. I was chatting with Nico [de Boinville, jockey] and he's very happy that we do that. I think he's going the right way and he's a talented horse - Nicky Henderson, trainer.

quotes.race: 2025 Uttoxeter Annual Membership Now Available Novices' Limited Handicap Chase (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Jingko Blue was great. He jumped really slickly; he's not very big but he certainly respects those fences a lot more than he did hurdles. He's gone through that ground easy enough. I thought it was the perfect start - Nicky Henderson, trainer, speaking to Sky Sports Racing.

quotes.race: Virgin Bet Daily Price Boosts Novices' Handicap Hurdle (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: That caught me unaware. I thought it was quite a big test off top weight in a competitive race. I've had the odd issue with Jingko Blue at home and not been unable to run him but that was a good performance. You'd love to mind him a bit this season. He's a nice big horse who will jump a fence - Nicky Henderson, trainer.

quotes.race: Coral Committed To Safer Gambling Novices' Hurdle (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: I think Jingko Blue did well to get back up. It deserved to be a dead-heat and I think the first two are both smart horses. It's a juggling game at the moment with the novices because they are a good bunch and spreading them out is important. I think he is good but he's only young and let's go one step at a time. He's growing up all the time - Nicky Henderson, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: He won at Uttoxeter and then in a Grade 2 Windsor last season. We were thinking about the Brown Advisory at the festival, so we went to the Reynoldstown at Ascot, but his jumping got a bit muddled. He made a shocking mistake going down the hill and that was lights out for the season. It transpired that he had significant kissing spines and he's had back surgery, which we're hoping can make a difference. He's grown into a fine, big horse, and he's physically improved. 21-10-25

prev_owners.owner: Charles C Walker And Jonny Craib

runners.comment: Latest effort suggests this scenario will prove ideal; could go well
runners.spotlight: Completed a 2m3f handicap double at Ascot last season; best effort since when second in useful event at Windsor (2m4f) on last appearance, leaving the impression today's scenario will prove ideal; could go well.

quotes.race: Betfair Exchange Handicap Hurdle (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: It's a shame they don't have a festival here in four weeks. Altobelli is on an upward curve and hopefully he can keep climbing now. I imagine we'll enter him in the Coral Cup and another step up in trip would be a plus if anything - Harry Fry, trainer.

quotes.race: Brown Novices' Hurdle (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: We're delighted to see Altobelli progress from his first start over hurdles, we've done a lot of work with his schooling and there's definitely improvement in that department. Ordinarily we would've liked to have kept him for Exeter later in the week but they're good, good to firm and it's the challenges we're facing with the conditions as he's a big horse who needs some cut in the ground - Harry Fry, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: We were delighted with his bumper win at Exeter last season and he's schooled so well that we'll go straight over hurdles in the next few weeks. We've been waiting for softer ground and will start off over two miles. He's one of our leading novice hurdle prospects. 11-11-22

He improved from his first run over hurdles to win by a wide margin at Carlisle but on reflection I think that left its mark as he ran no race when we pitched him in the Grade 1 at Aintree. We can forget that run and we've got a second-season hurdler who's still unexposed. I'd like to give him experience in a handicap, possibly at Ascot's first fixture in November, with a view of aiming him for the £150,000 Betfair Exchange Trophy there just before Christmas. I'd like to think he'll progress. 04-10-23

runners.comment: Form has gone awry in last three starts but progressive otherwise; may rebound
runners.spotlight: Form has gone rather awry in last three outings but he has been progressive otherwise, culminating in 2m4f handicap wins at Cheltenham and Newbury in the autumn; may rebound and run a good race.

quotes.race: Foresters Garden Buildings Novices' Hurdle (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: French Ship is shaping into a really nice prospect and is learning all the time. He still didn't jump as slickly as we'd like but it's all part of the education. He was progressive in his bumpers and he's proving to be the same over hurdles - Johnson White, joint-trainer.

quotes.race: Pertemps Network 'Junior' Open National Hunt Flat Race (Category 1 Elimination) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: French Ship has improved a lot since his first bumper at Kempton and took a step forward at Taunton last time. He's finished for the season and will go novice hurdling later in the year - Philip Hobbs, joint-trainer.

stable_tour.quote: It was great to win with him at Cheltenham last month, and that was a great performance. We looked at taking him back there but instead we'll go to Newbury next weekend for a two-and-a-half-mile handicap hurdle. He's in good form ahead of it and I'd like to think there's still plenty of improvement to come from him. 20-11-25

He's a promising horse. He won a bumper at Haydock in May, having finished second the time before. Probably in retrospect, he was too far out of his ground in the novice hurdle at Chepstow in which he finished second last time, but at least he got the experience of a run under his belt and hopefully he'll be winning before long. 30-10-24

racecards.verdict: Back down in distance, KABRAL DU MATHAN should be difficult to beat. Jingko Blue is next best.
racecards.betting_forecast: 4/9 Kabral Du Mathan, 11/2 Jingko Blue, 11/1 Lucky Place, 12/1 Altobelli, 14/1 Rubaud,  French Ship

racecards.race_name: bet365 Josh Gifford Novices' Handicap Chase (GBB Race)

runners.comment: Didn't jump well enough last time; contender if judged on Musselburgh win two runs ago
runners.spotlight: Didn't jump well enough when well beaten in Kempton Grade 2 novice in February last time but had doubled his chasing tally with ready success at Musselburgh (2m4f, good to soft) three weeks earlier, and will be dangerous if back in similar form.

quotes.race: Join Racing TV Now 'National Hunt' Novices' Hurdle (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Go West was very good and jumped well. I felt the other one made mistakes behind us, I couldn't really see what was going on but I could hear him! He's a horse that's improving and he'll be a nice chaser next season. He's not the biggest but he's compact and he's all there - Harry Cobden, jockey, talking to Racing TV.

quotes.race: Sky Bet Super Week, Supersized Maiden Hurdle (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Go West was entitled to be a bit fresh last time but he travelled well, jumped great and never really saw a rival all the way round. He's a nice horse and he'll keep improving. It's a good bit of placing by the boss to send him here - Harry Cobden, jockey.

quotes.race: Salisbury Hospice Open Maiden National Hunt Flat Race (Category 3 Elimination) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Go West isn't really a bumper horse, but I didn't want to go novice hurdling this season. We could give him another run but he'll be hurdling in the autumn and the rain was ideal for him because it put a bit of emphasis on stamina. He'll be going over a trip when he's hurdling - Paul Nicholls, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: We placed him well to win three on the bounce over hurdles last season, when he never once saw another rival. We upped him in class for his final run but he was too free and didn't get home on his first attempt at three miles. He should make his mark in novice chases round the smaller tracks. 04-11-25

runners.comment: Won in Ireland in the autumn but pulled up on stable debut just ten days ago
runners.spotlight: Signed off for Gavin Cromwell in Ireland with hard-fought win at Galway (2m6f, yielding) in the autumn but was pulled up when reappearing for new stable at Haydock (3m1f, good to soft) ten days ago and needs to turn things around quickly.

stable_tour.quote: He went chasing this summer and it was great to win with him at Galway last month when he showed a good attitude. He's going to go on a break now as he wants nice ground. We'll look at 3m handicaps with him later in the season. 04-11-25

He won nicely at Bellewstown and put in a good run when second at Cork last month. He then ran a bit flat at Cheltenham but I think we ran him back a bit too soon in hindsight, so we'll freshen him up. He's a nice, big horse and we think he's better than his last run. 13-11-24

runners.comment: Scored over 3m here last month and is now 2-2 over fences; should have more to offer
runners.spotlight: Low-mileage 7yo who is 2-2 over fences, the latter win gained here (3m, soft) last month; recently withdrawn with good ground deemed unsuitable but his first two wins (one over hurdles) were gained on good; should cope with this drop back in trip and has plenty of scope for further progress; respected.

stable_tour.quote: He's another to go chasing. He had a good season last term, winning at Doncaster in February, before being pulled up at Ayr at the end of the season. He's ready to go over fences. 21-10-25

runners.comment: Landed a big punt at Bangor last month and could still be well treated after 10lb hike
runners.spotlight: Returned to form and rewarded heavy market support at Bangor (2m4f, good; tongue-tie refitted) last month, his fifth start for Dan Skelton; just a respectable sixth under penalty in the Red Rum at Aintree (2m, good to soft) nine days later and his mark is another 5lb higher here, but he remains very much of interest.

quotes.race: PADDY MAC Maiden Hurdle
quotes.quote: Palamon ran in the Boodles at Cheltenham and the ground was too slow, but he got his ground today ? it's proper quick ground. He jumped well and battled well. He was untidy at the last, but he was still quick through it, he didn't lose any momentum. He showed a good attitude and he always has done. We've always thought a bit of him, so it's good to get that done - Sean Flanagan, jockey.

quotes.race: jigsawsportsbranding.co.uk Handicap
quotes.quote: I wasn't quite expecting that. We went slow, I travelled through the race very well and I waited until the two and then Palamon's gone and done it very easily. He ran a very nice race on his first run and he's never really built on that promise but he's a nice horse - Alec Voikhansky, jockey.

runners.comment: Clear second at Kelso this month but is 3lb higher in a stronger race here
runners.spotlight: 0-13 since winning over hurdles on debut in France in 2024; runner-up in three chases since fitted with a tongue-tie this year, most recently at Kelso (2m7f, good) three weeks ago, but he is 3lb higher in a stronger race here and needs to find something extra.

stable_tour.quote: The French horses don't normally do that well in the same season they come over, but he was second twice and could be quite nice. He was going very easily at Bangor last week when unseating his rider and it was just unfortunate. He'll be winning soon and should have some better targets coming up. 20-11-25

He ran much better to be beaten by just a head at Carlisle on Sunday, principally because of the ground drying out. He's an improving sort and came out of the Carlisle race in good shape. Next up is the Go Norths Final at Kelso this month. 13-03-26

racecards.verdict: The drop back to 2m didn't pay dividends at Aintree but PALAMON appeared to have plenty in hand when landing a big punt two runs ago.
racecards.betting_forecast: 6/4 Calimystic, 11/4 Palamon, 7/2 Go West, 5/1 Kahavari, 16/1 Millforce

prev_owners.owner: Exors Of The Late Trevor Hemmings

runners.comment: Career-best form when close third of 22 at Aintree a fortnight ago
runners.spotlight: Seen only twice this season but posted career-best performance when close third of 22 at Aintree (2m4f, good to soft) a fortnight ago, despite Tom Bellamy's saddle slipping after the last; respected.

quotes.race: Coral Scottish Champion Hurdle (A Limited Handicap) (Grade 2) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: For the last four months I've been saying I want Favour And Fortune on good ground. He's been running very well on heavy but he's a beautiful-actioned horse. His jumping was so much better today. He ran very well at Cheltenham and he nearly fell at the first and was only beaten ten lengths in a good Supreme. I've always loved him and he's certainly the best of my novices. It's been a difficult season for him and this was the last chance we had to run him. I'd like to stay over hurdles with him, he's not had a lot of racing - Alan King, trainer

quotes.race: William Hill Formby Novices' Hurdle (Grade 1) (Formerly Registered As The Tolworth Hurdle) (GBB)
quotes.quote: It looked a proper race and Favour And Fortune jumped super and travelled into it. He handles this ground but I'd love to see him on good ground with the action he's got on him. We've got to think about the Supreme and we'll speak to the team to see what we want to do. If we went to Cheltenham, we might go straight there - Alan King, trainer.

quotes.race: Join Racing TV Now 'Introductory' Hurdle (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: It was a bit of a messy race with no-one wanting to go on and Favour and Fortune was a touch keen and a bit novicey. It probably did him the world of good today as he had to go through softer ground and grind it out on his own up the straight. He's got a lot options now. Two miles is his trip for the time being and he's got the scope to make a nice chaser - Tom Cannon, jockey.

quotes.race: Vickers.Bet EBF "National Hunt" Novices' Hurdle (Qualifier) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: We've always thought Favour And Fortune was a very good horse ? it's great when they go and do it like that first time. He came home lame from Cheltenham, he pulled some muscles between his front legs, so you really want to put a line through that. He'd had a good summer and we've been happy with his work this autumn. He missed the second-last a little bit but he'll learn from that. He's quite a light horse and he wouldn't want a lot of racing, so we'll give him a bit of time and find another small novice where he can carry a penalty - Alan King, trainer.

quotes.race: Virgin Bet Open National Hunt Flat Race (Category 2 Elimination) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Favour And Fortune was very impressive with a penalty. He put a lot of distance between him and the other horses and it didn't look a bad bumper on paper so he's obviously smart. I don't know whether he goes to Cheltenham or Aintree but whichever it is he's probably up to that level. I got the split turning in and he was very honest and straightforward, galloping right through the line. He's really powerful and has a good future. He's learning as he goes but having a big engine helps! - Tom Cannon, jockey.

stable_tour.quote: Unfortunately he's had a bit of a setback. He got cast in his stable and injured his hock. He was going to be trained for the Greatwood Hurdle - all summer I thought he was an ideal horse for it - but he may not now be out until the second half of the season. He's still an exciting horse and we just have to take our time and get him right; he's too good to be rushed. He's a horse we've always rated and was terrific in the Scottish Champion Hurdle so I hope we can look forward to 2025 with him. 25-10-24

My hopes of aiming him at the Greatwood, which would have been the perfect race for him, were ended when he got cast in his stable and injured his hock. But there are plenty of good races to aim for in the second half of the season. He's still an exciting horse and we just have to take our time and get him right, he's too good to be rushed. He's a horse we've always rated and he was terrific in the Scottish Champion Hurdle so I hope we can look forward to 2025 with him. 07-11-24

runners.comment: Narrow winner off today's mark in October but pulled up both starts since
runners.spotlight: Returned from a break with narrow win at Uttoxter (2m4f, good) in October but pulled up on both starts since, latterly at last month's Cheltenham Festival; younger rivals have much more persuasive profiles.

quotes.race: Pertemps Network Handicap Hurdle (Pertemps Hurdle Series Qualifier) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: From the start of the season this has been a big target for Dargiannini mainly because I know a lot of horses use this as a prep race. He is really good fresh and it was on nice ground around a flat track so I thought it would be a good race to start in. It is nice when a plan comes together. He has been an absolute star for me. He has won three races and I've not been training him for a year. He has been a proper yard star. There is a possibility he could run in the Lanzarote Hurdle here back after Christmas, but there are a few options - Harry Derham, trainer.

quotes.race: BetVictor Non-Runner-No-Bet At Cheltenham Seniors' Handicap Hurdle
quotes.quote: I wasn't sure Dargiannini would win at Uttoxeter because he'd fallen the time before and I didn't know if he'd need a run to get his confidence back, but he won well there and this was the plan after he'd fallen. I said to the owner if he won well today we'd then go to Aintree for a day out and there's a two-and-a-half-mile handicap hurdle there, so we might do that - Harry Derham, trainer

quotes.race: Paxtons Supporting Sedgefield Racecourse Novices' Hurdle (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: I thought Dargiannini was a bit keen over the first two but once he got in front after the third he started to relax. He put the race to bed a long way out. He's still a proper baby, we need to go steady away with him. - Gavin Sheehan, rider

stable_tour.quote: He ran really well and won at Uttoxeter first time out when he was nice and fresh. He then disappointed at Newbury in November, but we've freshened him up again and prepared him for Cheltenham. He's 11 now and has been a great horse for us, so we thought if we were going to get him at his absolute best to run in a big one, this is what we had to do. 19-02-26

He was a complete star for me last season having won two really nice Saturday races. He'll start at Kempton on November 13 in a 2m5f Pertemps qualifier. He's done well at the track before. I haven't really planned past that but that race is a big target for him early on in his season. 18-10-23

runners.comment: Good winner at Taunton two starts ago but others in this field look better handicapped
runners.spotlight: Seemingly back in prime form when clear winner at Taunton (2m, heavy) in February; also suited by good ground and stays at least 2m3f but he disappointed on latest outing and others in this field look better handicapped.

quotes.race: Best Odds Guaranteed At BetVictor Conditional Jockeys' Handicap Hurdle
quotes.quote: I think they went too quickly, but I'm very pleased. Aurigny Mill looked the part - Robert Walford, trainer.

quotes.race: Ladbrokes Boost Your Odds On Racing Handicap Hurdle
quotes.quote: I've always thought Aurigny Mill was up at this level. This is the second run of his career that we have had a problem-free run up to. He had bruised feet all last season between every run, but we have got on top of all that. My son's partner rides him out most days and she said he was as good as ever, and she has got it right. Sean Bowen finished fourth on him in a bumper, and he said he would win loads of races, but he was backwards, and it took him time to get his breathing right. Fergus (Gillard) said he was off the bridle down the back straight, but he is settling now. He only had the hood on to help him settle. He is just a lovely horse - Victor Dartnall, trainer.

runners.owner: S T Racing - The Founders' Syndicate
runners.comment: Landed big prize at Windsor on New Year's Day but not quite in same form either run since
runners.spotlight: Just held on to land big prize at Windsor (2m4f, good) on New Year's Day but wasn't in quite the same form on next two outings (2m3f/3m) and probably needs to find hidden reserves.

quotes.race: Fitzdares New Year's Day Handicap Hurdle (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: I rode Listentoyourheart last time and unfortunately the hurdles were out and that didn't really benefit her because her jumping's so good. With the two quick hurdles up the straight I knew it would benefit her today. She's genuine and we rode her a bit more forward today and that helped too. When the other horse came to her she picked up again. She's good and gutsy - Tristan Durrell, jockey.

quotes.race: Play Coral 'Racing-Super-Series' For Free Mares' Novices' Hurdle (Listed Race) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Listentoyourheart was good there, she snipped through that gap. She's tough, she's hardy and has a little bit of experience under her belt. We got on with it and got some racing into her early in the season. Today was always going to be harder, but we were preparing her for it. When they turned the taps on, she took about five strides to pick up when the others picked up immediately in front of her. Some would back out of that hole, but she's not like that - Dan Skelton, trainer.

quotes.race: CSP Mares' Novices' Hurdle (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Two and a half miles will be no issue and Listentoyourheart actually ran well on softer ground at Aintree, but I'm not in a massive hurry to pitch her in. While the ground is like this we don't have to - Dan Skelton, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: She won at Windsor in a valuable race over this trip [2m4f], showing a gritty attitude in the process, but was on the front end a bit too strong at Ascot at the weekend. If she got into the Martin Pipe there's a chance she'd go, but we may wait for Aintree. 17-02-26

runners.owner: The Time On Our Hands Boys' Syndicate
runners.comment: 3-5 hurdles; below form when upped to 2m4f this month but may still have potential
runners.spotlight: 3-5 over hurdles, the latest win gained at Ascot (1m7f, good) in November; never really got involved when upped to 2m4f at Aintree a fortnight ago but could plausibly still have untapped potential over this trip.

quotes.race: Ascot Partners Handicap Hurdle
quotes.quote: The bookies didn't give Trustintimes any chance. The favourite had won a Grade 2 and was only rated 5lb higher than us, so we were either far too high or he was very well in. We weighed up sticking to novices or dipping our toe into handicap company, so we'll see how the handicapper reacts now - Harry Fry, trainer.

runners.comment: Placed off 7lb higher in this race two years ago; returns from long layoff today
runners.spotlight: Dual 2m winner here; absent since finishing fifth in a beginners' chase in May 2024 but was placed off mark 7lb higher than today's in this race two years ago (good ground); worth a glance in the market.

quotes.race: Brian Giles Memorial "National Hunt" Novices' Hurdle (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: I rode Authorised Speed to finish fifth in the Champion Bumper and I said then I thought he was a proper horse. He finds everything so easy and doesn't get stressed. He's a proper soft-ground horse and hopefully he can come back here for the Tolworth - that would be the target at the moment - Josh Moore, assistant trainer.

quotes.race: Don't Miss A Beat With Free RacingTV Open National Hunt Flat Race (Category 1 Elimination) (GBB)
quotes.quote: We've taken our time with Authorised Speed and the hopes were high, but then you see Mr Nicholls here and he's just got one runner. I'll leave plans to Gary, who'll place him, but the thing was to win a bumper - Pat Gallagher, owner.

stable_tour.quote: He jumped foot-perfect until the second-last and was going to win when he took a silly fall on his chase debut at Ascot last season. Plumpton was probably the wrong place to run him after that and things happened too quickly for him around there. He'll run predominantly over two and a half miles and upwards this season on stiff tracks. I think he could progress over fences and he schooled very well last week. I remember finishing fifth on him in the Champion Bumper a few years ago and was cantering going down the hill, but he's only just filling into himself and he's certainly got an engine. Long term, something like the Turners at the festival might be his type of race now it's a handicap. He could start back at Ascot on Saturday but only if the ground is soft enough. 29-10-24

I really do like this horse who is still a big baby. He started the season with a good second in a Listed Ascot bumper and put that experience to good use when winning with his head in his chest at Newbury last month. I am not sure what he beat but Paul Nicholls and Alan King trained the placed runners. We have some big ambitions here as there is a Listed bumper at Newbury coming up which he goes for next, and if he comes through that well then I would certainly consider the Cheltenham Bumper. 02-02-22

runners.comment: Out of form for new stable this year but the refitted cheekpieces might aid his cause
runners.spotlight: Won big-field Listed handicap in first-time cheekpieces at Listowel (2m, good to yielding) for Willie Mullins in September; badly out of form for new stable this year (four runs) but may fare better now that the cheekpieces are reinstated.

quotes.race: Listowel Races Supporters Club Lartigue Hurdle In Memory Of John Molyneaux (Listed Handicap)
quotes.quote: The cheekpieces helped to sharpen up Last Kingdom's jumping and helped him to travel through the race. I felt we were a little bit at sea without them at Galway. I thought they might just help to bring out a bit of improvement, and they did. He jumped much better and travelled sweeter. I committed him plenty early, but I was confident of him staying on that ground, and he did. He saw it out nicely - Paul Townend, jockey.

quotes.race: Farmhouse Foods Novice Handicap Hurdle
quotes.quote: Mark [Walsh, jockey] said Last Kingdom has grown up a little bit since the last day. He said he jumped well and missed the last but still would have managed to win and he travelled away smoothly. He's happy on that ground and he might make into something like a Lartigue horse, he's only four - David Casey, trainer's assistant.

stable_tour.quote: Cheekpieces brought about improvement when he won the Lartigue at Listowel. That was a big step back in the right direction. 17-11-25

runners.comment: Did well in the autumn but progress has stalled since; given wind op last month
runners.spotlight: Started off for new stable in excellent form in the autumn, winning at Kelso (2m6f, good) before big-field second at Cheltenham (2m5f, soft), but his progress has stalled a bit since; needs combination of last month's wind op and first-time tongue-tie to have positive effect.

runners.owner: P J Vogt And Bryan Drew

quotes.race: Virgin Bet A Good Bet Hogmaneigh Handicap Hurdle
quotes.quote: We stepped Fasol up today as I won on him at Wincanton the last time and he got every bit of two miles. He can be a bit of a monkey and sometimes it depends on how he gets out of bed, but he was lovely today. He travelled and jumped really well, so I'm very happy. I love it here, I'm definitely coming back - Olive Nicholls, jockey.

quotes.race: Download The BetMGM App Novices' Hurdle (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: It was about time Fasol got his head in front and it was a last-minute decision to enter him as I thought if the ground was too quick to run the filly then I needed something in it was a good race. Fredie Keighley was due to ride him, but I thought let's see if a girl gets on with him as he gets on well with the girls at home - Paul Nicholls, trainer.

quotes.race: DragonBet - Oncourse And Online Maiden Hurdle (Novices' Championship Hurdle Series Qualifier) (GBB)
quotes.quote: Fasol choked at Windsor last time so we had his wind done and he liked the better ground here. He'll have plenty of options during the spring - Paul Nicholls, trainer, talking to Racing TV.

stable_tour.quote: Somewhat frustrating and I admit he's becoming quite expensive to follow. Breathing problems came to the fore last season, so he had surgery in January and showed the benefit on his return when finally getting off the mark in a Taunton maiden hurdle. He did well for a summer break and clearly needed the run when only fifth at Chepstow last month. Harry Cobden came back and said we need to go right-handed and possibly go up in trip, but we stuck to two miles at Ascot on Saturday where I agree he looked like he needed further, so that's what we'll do next time. He's a novice until December 1 so we'll look for a soft little race somewhere. Not the easiest of rides as he doesn't do a lot in front. 04-11-25

runners.breeder: A D G Oldrey &  G C Hartigan
runners.owner: Andrew And Sarah Wates And Gt Racing

prev_owners.owner: A D G Oldrey & G C Hartigan

runners.comment: Cosily won small-field Ascot maiden in March; could easily have more to offer in handicaps
runners.spotlight: Fairly useful Flat racer; runner-up on first three hurdle starts (all 2m) before cruising clear in four-runner Ascot maiden (2m3f, good) last month; could easily have more improvement to come in handicap hurdles; interesting.

quotes.race: Ascot Racecourse Supports Horse Rangers Hampton Maiden Hurdle (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: The plan is to go to Sandown for the novices' championship final. A lovely, stiff two miles should suit Gnomon really well. That's been the plan from about five minutes before we bought him, and he's the right sort to have a crack at it - Toby Lawes, trainer.

quotes.race: CopyBet Handicap (GBBPlus Race)
quotes.quote: We went a good gallop and got racing early and we were able to skip out off the rail. Gnomon is only just starting to relax over this trip and he's coming up through the gears. The ground was probably too heavy from him last time at Ffos Las. He could end up being a nice horse next year - Rossa Ryan, jockey.

stable_tour.quote: I was very happy with his hurdling debut at Hereford last week - his first run for us since leaving Ralph Beckett, for whom he won twice this year. I wasn't too worried about getting beaten, as it was a slightly tactical race and we just lost out to a bit of experience really. The horse who beat us, Vol Royale, won nicely, and we were 16 lengths clear of the third. He'll be a nice horse, he'll improve on that first run and will definitely stay further in time. He wouldn't want the deep winter ground but I think he'll develop into a really nice handicap hurdler. 17-12-25
