runners.comment: Ran well at Aintree a fortnight ago but his last win came in 2022; others preferred
runners.spotlight: Kept on for sixth of 21 in first-time visor at Aintree (2m, good to soft) a fortnight ago and will be suited by this move back up in trip, but his last win came in 2022 and he's patently not the force of old.

stable_tour.quote: He's run well in many big handicap hurdles, finishing second in a Martin Pipe and third in a Greatwood. He was pulled up in his only chase last season, but he does look like a chaser and we might have another look at that. Otherwise he'll be back into those big handicap hurdles and hopefully it's just a matter of time before he can hit the target in one of them. 22-10-24

runners.comment: 2m winner here in December; still in good form; considered on first attempt at 2m4f
runners.spotlight: Won against his own age-group here (2m, soft; also suited by good) in December and has finished close up on all three outings since (1m7f-2m); must be considered on this first attempt at 2m4f.

stable_tour.quote: He won his second start over hurdles and then we ran him in the Grade 1 Top Novices' Hurdle at Aintree. I wouldn't normally do that, but he ran respectably. We had a couple of hiccups last season but he's going well and we think a bit of him. We'll probably stay over hurdles but he'll jump a fence in time. 30-10-25

runners.comment: Made good progress towards end of 2025 (three wins); returns from a short break
runners.spotlight: Made good progress towards end of 2025, with latest of three wins gained at Kempton (2m5f, good) on Boxing Day; not discredited when fourth at Ascot (2m3f, soft) in January and has good claims if tuned up after a break.

stable_tour.quote: He's been a real fun horse, winning twice over hurdles for us this autumn. He just took his time to develop mentally but he's certainly got the hang of things now. It was  probably a bit quick to run him back the other day at Wincanton, especially around a track that's just far too sharp for him. I think he's still got plenty of improvement in him. At some point we will go up in trip as well - I think he will get plenty further. So I'll pick a couple of races for him post-Christmas and see what comes up - but he's definitely got more to come. 17-12-25

runners.breeder: E A R L Haras Du Camp Benard
runners.comment: Won off reduced mark last month and ran well in defeat ten days later
runners.spotlight: Exploited reduced mark when winning quite comfortably at Ludlow last month and was one of two to pull clear of the others when second at Ascot (also 2m5f, good) ten days later; no surprise if he features.

quotes.race: Events At Ascot Juvenile Handicap Hurdle (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: I bought Royal Way for the Triumph Hurdle but we knew after one run he wasn't a Triumph horse. We then said we'll go for the Boodles and he missed out by one, but what a consolation this is - Keith Loads, owner.

quotes.race: Vobe Electrics Juvenile Hurdle (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Royal Way is the most expensive horse I've bought, I got him privately with a dream for the Triumph Hurdle. That dream was stopped after his first run and then we bumped into one last time but he's settling better and Niall said there's a lot left in the tank. I could take a Fred Winter with him. Gary (Moore, trainer) said we could look at the top tables on the Flat too so there's plenty to look forward to - Keith Loads, owner.

stable_tour.quote: A bit disappointing last winter but hopefully a wind op will have helped him. Once we've schooled him on grass and see how he goes, we might go novice chasing, but there's no huge rush to go over fences. I honestly think he'd have won the Fred Winter two years ago but he was balloted out by one. He could be well handicapped from having had a poor winter. 28-10-25

runners.comment: Ran quite well at Chepstow last month and Sean Bowen takes over today; a possible
runners.spotlight: Gained all six hurdle wins at around 2m but ran quite well when fourth at Chepstow (2m3f, soft) last month; current mark is workable (even from 1lb out of the weights) and Sean Bowen takes over today; could have a say.

quotes.race: Radnor Hills Mares' Handicap Hurdle (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Tour Ovalie just wins races. It's always tactical with her, she has to be delivered late and it's difficult to go up in class, but horses like her are hard to find - Evan Williams, trainer.

quotes.race: Racing TV Club Day Mares' Novices' Hurdle (Herring Queen Series Qualifier) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Tour Ovalie is just a joy. She's progressive and enjoys racing. I think we're all guilty of not running them enough. She can only be a novice for one season, and we ran her because if you took the first two in the betting out, it was a shallow race. I think she's run to her mark. A lot of them haven't had the chance to run in handicaps, and handicappers going back into novice hurdles are just a bit hardier. I think they've probably underperformed somewhat. She's a good, tough, genuine mare, and I have a lot of time for her. I do love a trier - Evan Williams, trainer.

quotes.race: Play Coral 'Racing-Super-Series' For Free Mares' Handicap Hurdle
quotes.quote: Now we know how Isabel rides Tour Ovalie, it makes it easier to watch as an owner as she leaves her late, and you've got to leave her very late, but she runs beautifully - Andrew Strong, owner.

quotes.race: EK Mowers & Machinery Mares' Handicap Hurdle (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Tour Ovalie has been going the right way lately and that was very pleasing. She's improved with time. She used to be a bit hot but she has learned to race the right way. We've always had plenty of belief in her and she's a smashing mare for the owners as she's so consistent. Isabel gets on well with her and we'll quietly step up in grade - Evan Williams, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: She made the frame in two bumpers in the spring and is a smashing type. She'll want some give in the ground but I'm not sure whether she'll go straight over hurdles or have another bumper run. 02-11-23

A genuine mare with a habit of winning, just the kind of habit you want. She's basically a 2m hurdler and she's won six out of 20 in that discipline. I try to keep her in mares' races. She's on a mark of 118, which is just below her highest mark. I'm hoping she takes her consistency to Ludlow on Thursday. 14-01-26

racecards.verdict: The last race of the season can go to GNOMON, who cruised clear at Ascot last month ahead of a next-time-out winner.
racecards.betting_forecast: 7/2 Gnomon, 5/1 Across Earth, 6/1 Favour And Fortune,  Surrey Lord, 13/2 Listentoyourheart, 10/1 Royal Way, 11/1 Trustintimes, 12/1 Fasol,  No Ordinary Joe, 16/1 Tour Ovalie, 20/1 Lucky Manifest, 25/1 Aurigny Mill, 28/1 Last Kingdom, 33/1 Authorised Speed, 50/1 Dargiannini

racecards.race_name: Celebrate With Sponsorship At Southwell Racecourse "Confined" Apprentice Handicap

runners.breeder: Miss S Sands & Mrs Lynette Andersen
runners.comment: Runner-up five times over 6f since September; fourth in better 5f race than this in March
runners.spotlight: Seemingly aided by cheekpieces when runner-up five consecutive times (once here) over 6f in September-January, and last month's 5f fourth at Chelmsford came in a slightly better race than this; worth persisting with over this trip.

prev_owners.owner: The Brian The Snail Racing Club

runners.comment: Placed at Newcastle recently but inconsistent nowadays; younger rivals appeal more
runners.spotlight: Veteran with 14 wins on his CV; kept on for third when dropped back to 5f at Newcastle 12 days ago but is inconsistent nowadays and younger rivals appeal more.

quotes.race: Extra Winnings With BetUK Acca Club Handicap
quotes.quote: Brian The Snail is an old boy who knows the game. Sometimes he breaks out a bit slow - like he's done today - but he thrives being hung onto and it's paid off - Ryan Kavanagh, jockey, speaking to Sky Sports Racing.

quotes.race: Unibet 3 Uniboosts A Day Handicap
quotes.quote: We got a good tow and Brian The Snail battled all the way to the line. On his day he is very good and proved that tonight - Jack Garrity, jockey

quotes.race: Heed Your Hunch At Betway Handicap
quotes.quote: Brian The Snail is a horse with a lot of ability, but he only ever does it every now and again. His work at home is better than what he shows in the afternoon, but when he puts his best foot forward he's a nice horse - Tony Hamilton, jockey.

quotes.race: Owlerton Greyhound Stadium Sheffield Handicap
quotes.quote: Brian The Snail had a wind operation during the winter but his first run back was inconclusive as he didn't handle the track at Epsom. He might get into the Wokingham now - Robin O'Ryan, assistant trainer.

quotes.race: British Stallion Studs EBF Westow Stakes (Listed Race)
quotes.quote: That was too bad to be true, Brian The Snail never ran a race - Richard Fahey, trainer.

quotes.race: Racing UK Anywhere Available Now Handicap
quotes.quote: I was delighted with that. Brian The Snail is quite chunky so we wanted to get a run into him. I've made no secret, we do like him and there is a race at Ascot on May 3 for three-year-olds for him. We have the Commonwealth Cup in mind - Richard Fahey, trainer.

quotes.race: catterickbridge.co.uk Novice Stakes
quotes.quote: Brian The Snail is a good horse. I was a bit worried about the trip -  5f on a sharp track like this - but he's done it well. He'll be a sprinter - Tony Hamilton, jockey.

quotes.race: Book Your 17th October totepool Package Median Auction Maiden Stakes
quotes.quote: Brian The Snail is a grand, laid back horse and it took Tony (Hamilton) a while to pull him up there. He had done everything very easily at home and he had a really good blow so he will come on plenty for that. He is a horse we like a lot and it will be a surprise if he doesn't go on to better things - Robin O'Ryan, assistant trainer.

runners.comment: Consistent 7yo who was placed under James Glennon at Chelmsford in February
runners.spotlight: Consistent 7yo who kept on from the rear for third under James Glennon at Chelmsford (5f) in February, after a layoff; has never run here before but has form on Tapeta at Wolverhampton; can make his presence felt.

runners.comment: Didn't fire here recently but came second twice over C&D last month; must be considered
runners.spotlight: Won twice over C&D last year and came second twice over C&D last month; needs to rebound from a disappointing run ten days ago but he's largely consistent and features prominently in calculations.

runners.comment: 0-12 overall but has made the frame on last three of his four stable starts; considered
runners.spotlight: 0-12 overall but has made the frame on the last three of his four starts for Tony Carroll, most recently when fourth at Lingfield (5f) last month; also suited by Tapeta and continues to edge down the weights; considered.

stable_tour.quote: He's been rock-solid and deserves to win a race as he keeps bumping into one. We never thought he was going to be a two-year-old as he's a monster of a horse, but after every week of work he kept coming back for more. We're going to give him one more run at Catterick on Friday and then we'll probably have him gelded. His wind just catches him out in the last 50 yards of a race and he probably wants that doing as well some time. He was bought for only 1,000gns but I think he could be all right. He'll be a lovely horse for next year. 30-05-24

runners.comment: In the frame on three of his last five 6f starts; needs a good pace to aim at over 5f
runners.spotlight: Raced exclusively over 6f since returning from a break in December, making the frame on three of his last five appearances (twice here); visored for first time since 2022 (has sometimes worn other headgear since); probably reliant on a good pace to aim at over this trip.

runners.comment: Well beaten over 6f here last month and remains without a win since summer 2024
runners.spotlight: Well down the field over 6f here on latest outing six weeks ago and remains without a win since summer 2024; very difficult to enthuse over.

racecards.verdict: Preference is for IRISH DANCER, who didn't fire here recently but came second twice over C&D in March and collected four wins in 2025.
racecards.betting_forecast: 7/4 Clover Time, 7/2 Irish Dancer, 4/1 Sonic Si, 8/1 Brian The Snail,  Cabeza De Llave,  Man On A Mission, 50/1 Coast

racecards.race_name: Summer Social Events At Southwell Racecourse Handicap

runners.comment: Nine-race maiden who was beaten 24l at Doncaster four weeks ago.
runners.spotlight: Nine-race maiden who was beaten 24l at Doncaster (1m2f, good to soft) four weeks ago in first-time cheekpieces (replaced by first-time visor here); steps back up in trip and sliding down the weights but difficult to make a case for.

runners.comment: Has only beaten three rivals in four runs for current trainer.
runners.spotlight: Ex-French; has only beaten three rivals in four runs for current trainer; cheekpieces worn when last of ten at Wolverhampton (9.5f, AW) last month are persevered with; needs to show significant improvement for the return to this longer trip.

runners.comment: Has shown bits of form, latest when fourth at Lingfield last October; new headgear.
runners.spotlight: Showed bits of form when trained by the Kublers, latest when fourth of 16 at Lingfield (1m4f, AW) last October in first-time blinkers; sold for 8,000gns subsequently and switches to first-time cheekpieces on stable debut; one to watch out for in the betting.

runners.comment: Won here (1m4f) off 4lb lower last October; soundly beaten twice since.
runners.spotlight: Won here (1m4f) off 4lb lower last October; reported to have bled from the nose when beaten 34l over C&D last month, but soundly beaten at Catterick (1m4f, good) since; holds claims if he can return to form.

runners.comment: The step up in distance did the trick when he scored at Newcastle last month.
runners.spotlight: The step up in distance did the trick when he scored at Newcastle (2m, AW) last month; always in rear when last of eight at Chelmsford (13.5f, AW) since; holds claims if leaving latest effort behind.

runners.comment: Poor form in three runs this year for new yard following a 400-day absence.
runners.spotlight: Runner-up four times for Karl Burke but poor form in three runs for new yard following a 400-day absence; has plenty to prove.

runners.comment: Well held on last two Flat starts and also on hurdles debut last month.
runners.spotlight: Placed in a couple of low-grade handicaps at around 1m4f but well held on last two Flat starts and also on hurdles debut last month; more required.

runners.comment: Showed signs that another win may not be far away when second of ten over C&D last month.
runners.spotlight: Sole success came when trained by Andrew Balding in 2023; plenty of water under the bridge since but showed signs that another win may not be far away when second of ten over C&D last month, running on after her path was blocked; place claims at least.

runners.comment: Placed for the first time when second at Newcastle in February, but well beaten since.
runners.spotlight: Placed for the first time when second of nine at Newcastle (12.5f, AW; 100-1) in February in first-time cheekpieces (retained since); beat only one home when beaten 26l here (1m4f) 20 days ago; has possibilities if able to show his best form.

prev_owners.owner: Paul H Redmond & T G Fitzgerald & Mrs A M O'Brien & B Fowler

runners.comment: 14-race maiden but didn't fare too badly when third over C&D last month.
runners.spotlight: 14-race maiden but didn't fare too badly when third of eight over C&D last month; has place claims if able to reproduce that effort.

prev_owners.owner: Darren Croot And Mrs Zoe Croot

runners.comment: Huge prices and well beaten in five runs to date (6f-1m2f).
runners.spotlight: Huge prices and well beaten in five runs to date (6f-1m2f); takes a significant step up in trip on her handicap debut in first-time blinkers; one to keep an eye on.

racecards.verdict: This looks best left to RING FENCED who hasn't won since 2023 but was a decent second here last time. Angelardo is the main danger.
racecards.betting_forecast: 7/2 Ring Fenced, 5/1 Rose Warrior,  Angelardo, 6/1 Hickton,  Apache Eagle, 8/1 Argentum, 12/1 Abila, 16/1 Sovereign Applause, 20/1 Easter Sundae,  Trouble In Chicago, 25/1 Nala The Lioness

racecards.race_name: Book The Bistro In Sherwood Restaurant Novice Stakes (GBB/GBBPlus Race)

runners.comment: Well-held on first Flat start here (1m3f; 66-1) in November.
runners.spotlight: Landed a bumper at Worcester on his racecourse debut last September; well-held on first Flat start here (1m3f; 66-1) in November; has his work cut out in this company.

runners.comment: Second to a subsequent Group winner on his debut in a Newbury maiden last April.
runners.spotlight: Encouraging second to a subsequent Group winner on his debut in a Newbury maiden (1m3f, good) last April; off since and has been gelded; must be taken seriously.

runners.comment: Third in a Huntingdon bumper for Michael Keady three weeks ago; tough task on Flat debut.
runners.spotlight: Finished third in a Huntingdon bumper three weeks ago when trained by Michael Keady; this looks a tough assignment on his Flat debut.

runners.comment: Won seven-runner maiden at Haydock last July on debut.
runners.spotlight: 240,000euros yearling; by Sea The Moon out of a close relation to 1m2f Group 1 winner Sultanina; second favourite for seven-runner maiden at Haydock (7f, good) last July, which he nearly blew when making an awkward start and first off the bridle but he came from the back and stuck his neck out well for a narrow win; absent since but should be open to major improvement on AW debut.

quotes.race: MB Health EBF Maiden Stakes (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: I think Birgham Dub is a talented racehorse. He was green from the stalls and I was quite a long way back off a slow pace. I just popped him out with about three and a half [furlongs] to give him a good sighter of where he needed to go and he picked up very well. Jane [Chapple-Hyam, trainer] said he's got a beautiful temperament and he's very straightforward and he proved that. There should be some improvement to come - Hector Crouch, jockey, speaking to Racing TV.

runners.comment: Made a winning debut for top yard at Wolverhampton three weeks ago.
runners.spotlight: Made a winning debut for top yard at Wolverhampton (1m4f) three weeks ago and normal progress should see him bang there at the finish.

runners.comment: Slowly away on his debut when fourth of five at Yarmouth two weeks ago.
runners.spotlight: Slowly away on his debut when fourth of five at Yarmouth (1m2f, good) two weeks ago; will be sharper with that behind him and should win races in time.

runners.comment: Minor appeal on paper and makes his Flat debut in a warm novice.
runners.spotlight: Second foal; by Flag of Honour; dam tailed off in bumper, half-sister to winners Grand Canyon (1m1f/1m2f Flat and 2m hurdle) and Alquimia (7f/1m), out of 7f winning half-sister to US 6f 2yo Grade 2 winner Discreet Cat; likely to need more time.

runners.comment: Showed promise in a couple of maidens (around 1m) last October.
runners.spotlight: Showed promise in a couple of maidens (around 1m) last October; steps up in trip on AW debut but may be a longer-term project; Birgham Dub looks the trainer's main hope.

racecards.verdict: It looks best to side with CHASING TIME, who scored at Wolverhampton on his debut three weeks ago. The main danger is Kenneth.
racecards.betting_forecast: 5/4 Kenneth, 2/1 Chasing Time, 3/1 Birgham Dub, 20/1 Florentine Law,  Temple, 50/1 Ramli,  Peat And Diesel, 100/1 Dartmouth Jet

prev_owners.owner: GB Civil, N Sennett & I Furtado
Gb Civil Engineering & The Giggle Factor

runners.comment: Nine wins at this course (7f-1m4f), including three this year, and he remains in top form.
runners.spotlight: Nine wins at this course (7f-1m4f), including three this year; remains in top form, having finished runner-up here on his last two starts; must be strongly considered on his favoured track.

stable_tour.quote: He didn't show much last year but hit the lids in style this year with back-to-back wins at Southwell in the spring, each time over 1m4f. He was denied his hat-trick back at our local track by a nose. He was disappointing last time but had had had a much-needed break so was always going to be better for the run. There is more to come from him as he is still relatively lightly raced. 29-08-22

runners.owner: SBK Racing & B & J Parr Racing Ltd
runners.comment: 33-1 winner here (6f) in January but below that form at Lingfield (7f) since.
runners.spotlight: Has nine wins (6f-7.5f); 33-1 winner here (6f) in January in reapplied visor (retained since) but below that form at Lingfield (7f) subsequently; returns from a short break and is 2lb above his last winning mark; needs a career-best.

quotes.race: Tyre Scope Handicap
quotes.quote: I probably didn't get to stack them up as much as I'd have liked but Bell Shot likes it here and he was tough - Rossa Ryan, jockey.

runners.comment: Made winning debut in December 2024 and ran well in defeat on several occasions last year.
runners.spotlight: Made a winning debut in December 2024 and ran well in defeat on several occasions last year; signed off with a poor effort when ninth of 11 at Newbury (7f, good to soft) last September but handicapper has given him a chance if he can hit the boards running.

runners.comment: Seven of his 12 wins have been here (five over this trip); never won off a mark this high.
runners.spotlight: Seven of his 12 wins have been here (five over this trip); has never won off a mark this high however and most likely needs to drop a few pounds.

quotes.race: Yorkshire Equine Practice Handicap
quotes.quote: That was a great ride.The instructions were to drop Eligible in and fill him with confidence, he loves passing horses - David Easterby, joint-trainer.

runners.comment: Won four on turf last year, but he was runner-up on his sole AW start at Newcastle.
runners.spotlight: All four of his wins were on turf last year, but he was runner-up on his sole AW start at Newcastle; his progressive profile gives him a squeak but he may be better for his first outing since October.

prev_owners.owner: M Webber, M T Ward & Schiff Family
M Webber, M T Ward & Schiff Family

runners.comment: Returned to winning form at Wolverhampton last month with two wins.
runners.spotlight: Returned to winning form at Wolverhampton (8.5f) last month and followed up back there (7f) seven days later; back up in grade in search of a three-timer and although this looks tougher he cannot de discounted.

quotes.race: Virgin Bet Daily Extra Places Handicap (London Mile Series Qualifier)
quotes.quote: Farasi Lane's homework had been brilliant and he was second here last month, which could be considered a career-best and that's amazing for a 6yo to still be improving. That's probably a career-best again and hopefully it shows what we can do with these older horses. There's a 0-90 on Guineas day I've been thinking about, although he might not get in it now - Jamie Insole, joint-trainer.

runners.comment: Won maiden here last August and performed with credit on two of his last three starts.
runners.spotlight: Won maiden here (6f) last August on stable debut and performed with credit on two of his last three starts; returns from a break and still unexposed; holds claims.

runners.comment: Had been running well in AW handicaps until finishing last here recently.
runners.spotlight: Had been running well in AW handicaps since winning at Newcastle (1m) last October, until disappointing when last of six here (1m) 20 days ago; needs to get back on track.

quotes.race: Northern Commercials Your Local Iveco Dealership EBF Fillies' Restricted Novice (GBB)(IRE Incentive)
quotes.quote: Selection was a very good buy, she only cost 8,000gns but she doesn't know that! She's a tough filly and she'll probably get further in time - Craig Lidster, trainer.

runners.breeder: Lynch Bages, Camas Park & Summerhill B/S
runners.comment: Won at Kempton last September and a good third at Lingfield the following month.
runners.spotlight: Showed improved form in first-time blinkers when getting off the mark at Kempton (1m, AW) last September and was then a good third at Lingfield the following month; headgear left off on this return to action and he has been gelded; not out of this.

racecards.verdict: One that is in top form at present is DOWN TO THE KID (nap), who can bag his tenth course win. Farasi Lane rates the main danger.
racecards.betting_forecast: 5/2 Down To The Kid, 9/4 Farasi Lane, 7/1 Believe The Storm, 8/1 Winston's Warrior, 10/1 Rock Iguana, 12/1 Kisskodi,  Selection, 16/1 Bell Shot, 20/1 Eligible

racecards.race_name: Conference & Events At Southwell Racecourse Restricted Maiden Fillies' Stakes (Bands B, C & D) (GBB)

runners.comment: Off for well over a year; low-grade handicaps are probably next on the agenda
runners.spotlight: Not without hope in two Newcastle starts at big prices but has been off for well over a year since; low-grade handicaps are probably next on the agenda for a yard also responsible for The Wind And Sun.

prev_owners.owner: Hot To Trot Racing 2 & Henry Candy

runners.comment: Big prices/well beaten in four runs as a 3yo; hard to fancy returning from a long break
runners.spotlight: Big prices and well beaten in four runs as a 3yo (5f-1m), often not looking straightforward in the process; yard among the winners but she's hard to fancy returning from a long absence.

stable_tour.quote: She's a lovely filly with a decent pedigree. Although she was too keen on her debut, she's eligible for Band C and D restricted races and I hope she should be competitive in those. Henry likes her and he hasn't really hit top form yet. 02-08-24

runners.comment: Came away with two subsequent winners on her Chelmsford 6f debut last December; player
runners.spotlight: 40,000gns breeze-up 2yo who came right away with two subsequent winners on her Chelmsford 6f debut last December; signs of greenness that night and she's shortlisted in a first-time tongue-tie.

runners.breeder: A J Davenhill & Mrs A L Davenhill
runners.comment: 100-1 for her turf debut 12 days ago and ran accordingly; likely best watched for now
runners.spotlight: Related to winners, including the yard's useful Excellent Times, but she started 100-1 for her turf debut 12 days ago and ran accordingly; likely best watched for now.

runners.comment: 100-1, little immediate promise when beaten a long way (behind Dreamadera) at Leicester
runners.spotlight: Finished lame when last of seven in one run for Michael Appleby last summer; 100-1, offered little immediate promise when beaten a long way (behind Dreamadera) at Leicester for her new yard recently.

runners.owner: D Macauliffe, A Don & J Joyce
runners.comment: Shaped well enough at a big price on debut last spring; market useful after 11 months off
runners.spotlight: Half-sister to two fair sprint winners (first time out, and second time out, as 2yos); finished some way off the two market principals but shaped well enough at a big price on her Redcar debut last spring; market useful after 11 months off.

runners.comment: Half-sister to five winners; interesting to see how she goes in the market
runners.spotlight: 25,000gns yearling who's a half-sister to five winners, including Queues Likely (2-2 on Tapeta) and course winner Singoura; interesting to see how she goes in the market against stablemate Riviera Queen.

runners.comment: Didn't look to see out 7.4f on comeback; has the edge over most in terms of experience
runners.spotlight: Better with each of her three runs last summer and started among the favourites on her handicap debut/comeback from nine months off recently; didn't look to see out a stiff 7.4f that day and has the edge over most in terms of experience.

runners.comment: Three 7f runs last autumn; needs more back from six months off on first crack at sprinting
runners.spotlight: Three 7f runs last autumn, her C&D second looking a notch above her two soft-ground efforts either side; needs more back from six months off on her first crack at sprinting.

runners.comment: Every chance she'll want more of a stamina test and the market will guide on debut
runners.spotlight: Third foal of a mare who won in France at up to 9.5f; every chance she'll want more of a stamina test and the market will guide on debut.

runners.comment: Slowly away when last of 11 on debut; will want to be sharper out from stall 12
runners.spotlight: 14-1 for a similar maiden at Newcastle five weeks ago, when slowly away and last of 11 runners; will want to be sharper out from stall 12 and needs a big step forward.

stable_tour.quote: She's taken a little bit more time than we'd hoped she might, but we like her. She's a nice, physical type of filly but she just kept growing a little bit, so we gave her more time. 23-07-25

runners.breeder: New England Stud & Mount Coote Stud
runners.comment: Yard 6-31 with 3yos on the AW this year and she's arguably the most interesting newcomer
runners.spotlight: 4,600gns foal, 9,000gns yearling who's a half-sister to winners over various trips, notably Valiant (1m2f) and Culturati (6f-7f); yard 6-31 with 3yos on the AW this year and she's arguably the most interesting newcomer.

runners.comment: Didn't look to see out 7f here when last seen; retains potential for a yard in good form
runners.spotlight: Came away with a subsequent winner, despite needing the experience, on her 6f Newcastle debut last September; didn't look to see out 7f from a wide stall when a beaten favourite on her next start here and retains potential for a yard in good form.

racecards.verdict: Zarinca is second choice behind LUNA CELESTE, whose debut Chelmsford second last winter has been well advertised since.
racecards.betting_forecast: 5/2 Luna Celeste,  Sandy Craic, 5/1 Positive Thoughts, 6/1 Zarinca, 8/1 Rivera Queen, 10/1 Rumble Ruby, 12/1 Whazzimo, 25/1 Rianka, 50/1 The Wind And Sun, 66/1 Highland Bear,  Zambezi Diamond, 100/1 Dreamadera,  Moonlight Angel

runners.comment: Hit traffic latest; this is less competitive for a yard in fine form, so he's shortlisted
runners.spotlight: Stamina on the dam's side and he looked sure to be suited by the step up in trip over C&D last time having stayed on nicely on his 7f comeback here; hit traffic that evening and this is less competitive for a yard in fine form, so he has to be considered.

runners.comment: Met traffic over 9.5f latest; can't be ruled out under experienced claimer Ashley Lewis
runners.spotlight: First run at beyond sprint trips when winning an ordinary, small-field Wolverhampton handicap (8.6f) in January; met traffic upped to 9.5f latest (first-time cheekpieces; switches to a visor here) and can't be ruled out under experienced 5lb claimer Ashley Lewis.

runners.comment: Appreciated the step up in trip when winning over C&D 16 days ago; this tougher upped 4lb
runners.spotlight: Dam won twice over 1m for the Crisford yard and this filly appreciated the step up in trip when winning over C&D 16 days ago; that was only a 0-55 and she's 4lb higher in first-time headgear, but there could be better to come.

racecards.verdict: This can go to DELINQUENT, who's coming down in class for a yard in fine form. Kalokalo will be a big danger if allowed to dictate.
racecards.betting_forecast: 5/4 Delinquent, 7/2 What Fools Believe, 5/1 My Champion, 6/1 Safe Harbor, 7/1 Kalokalo

runners.comment: Back to last autumn's debut level over C&D latest; may have more to offer now handicapping
runners.spotlight: 200,000gns yearling who was bought unraced for 5,000gns in October 2024; back to last autumn's debut levels when best of the rest behind an easy, long odds-on winner over C&D on comeback a month ago and may have more to offer now handicapping.

stable_tour.quote: He's a very big gelding who's well bred, being by Sea The Stars out of a Dark Angel mare. He's been placed in a couple of novice races, which is pretty unusual for us, and he'll keep improving as he's still quite immature. He's my pick as a dark horse. 15-04-26

runners.comment: Record over C&D reads 22115112; ultra consistent and looks set to get involved once again
runners.spotlight: Record over C&D currently reads 22115112; didn't look to have any excuses in a race run to suit here three weeks ago and possible he's reached his ceiling mark now, but he's ultra consistent and looks set to get involved once again.

runners.comment: Handicapper seems to have erred on side of caution; Megan Smith takes just a second ride
runners.spotlight: 150,000gns yearling who went for just 5,000gns as a 3yo; fair debut last winter but well held in two runs since (1m2f-1m4f) and the handicapper seems to have erred on the side of caution; Megan Smith takes just a second ride under rules.

runners.owner: A Baker D Slack M Wilson & Partners
runners.comment: Five-time 7f winner here who's currently 0-17 over C&D; others have more pressing claims
runners.spotlight: Five-time 7f winner here (well suited by a good test over that trip) who's currently 0-17 over C&D; patchy since a course win off 1lb lower in February and others have more pressing claims.

runners.comment: Stamina the concern for his new trainer, who's been among winners with her jumpers lately
runners.spotlight: Two wins for Heather Main came over 6f and hasn't always convinced when tried over 7f, although turned in a solid effort from the front over that trip last time; stamina the concern for his new trainer, who's been among winners with her jumpers lately.

runners.comment: Usually misses the break/can hang left; good pace would help for last year's winning yard
runners.spotlight: Four-time course winner, all in the winter months, latterly off this mark in January; usually misses the break and again hung left when behind Marry The Night over C&D last time; a stronger pace would help for last year's winning yard.

quotes.race: pricedup.bet Boosts Handicap (A Jockey Club Grassroots Mile Series Qualifier)
quotes.quote: The break has done Soames Forsyte good, he's come back fresh and well. I wasn't totally expecting it but he has a lot of natural ability and he's very well bred. Sometimes he saves a little bit for himself and I'm delighted. I think it's a track that brings the best out of him as he's now two from two here - Michael Herrington, trainer.

runners.comment: Regressive maiden who can pull hard; will need to settle better round here
runners.spotlight: Regressive maiden who can pull hard (worn a hood once) and has finished tamely in four runs over tonight's trip; entitled to have come on for his recent Kempton comeback but will need to settle better round here.

runners.breeder: S C E A Ecurie Haras Du Cadran Et Al
runners.comment: Patchy for his current yard (been struggling for winners) but the return here could help
runners.spotlight: 7f course winner for Marco Botti last summer off 2lb higher; patchy since for his current yard, who've been struggling for winners, but the return here could help (third over C&D on his only other visit last month).

runners.comment: Ran well to a point at Doncaster before not seeing out 1m2f on his first run in 18 months
runners.spotlight: Ex-Irish gelding who makes his AW debut (half-brother to a Polytrack winner) having been beaten a long way on his first run in 18 months for new connections four weeks ago; ran well to a point at Doncaster before not seeing out 1m2f though.

quotes.race: Lakes Of Killarney Handicap
quotes.quote: Riding a winner for my brother (Tim - owner) is brilliant, he puts a lot of thought and energy into Avatar Jet. Upped to 1m suited him, he travelled better today and the gaps came. I was probably there sooner than I'd have liked - Gary Carroll, jockey, speaking to Racing TV

runners.comment: Four moderate efforts for William Haggas at shortish prices last year; can do better
runners.spotlight: Turned in four moderate efforts for William Haggas at shortish prices last year; perhaps the switch to the trainer of her Group 1-winning sister Saffron Beach and the fitting of a first-time hood will do the job.

runners.comment: Two wins for Roger Teal came in the spring but it's hard to find many other positives
runners.spotlight: Pulled hard and didn't see it out on his hurdling debut last month; two wins for Roger Teal came in the spring but it's hard to find many other positives as he makes his Tapeta debut in a first-time tongue-tie.

racecards.verdict: Maybe the switch to Jane Chapple-Hyam will do the trick with 1.65m euros yearling GOLDIE TRICKETT. Marry The Night is second best.
racecards.betting_forecast: 7/2 Marry The Night, 5/1 Superfortress, 6/1 Iconic Times,  Goldie Trickett, 8/1 Plutarch, 10/1 Soames Forsyte,  Give Me The Night,  Age Of Baroque, 12/1 Avatar Jet, 16/1 King Of York, 25/1 Johnjay

racecards.race_name: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Fillies Maiden

runners.comment: Improved for switch to turf last time when sixth of 13 at the Curragh; others preferred
runners.spotlight: Improved over poor 6f Dundalk debut when a 8.25l sixth for first turf run at the Curragh (7f, soft to heavy); others preferred.

runners.comment: Never better than midfield on Curragh debut at 33-1; others appeal more
runners.spotlight: Never better than midfield on debut at the Curragh (7f, soft to heavy) when 33-1; others appeal more.

runners.comment: Beaten similar distances in two Dundalk runs; hard to fancy
runners.spotlight: Beaten 16l over 7f at Dundalk and 15l over 10.5f there last time; hard to fancy.

runners.owner: Exors of the Late J Connaughton

runners.comment: 2.25l to find with Signora on the basis of their meeting at Cork last time; place claims
runners.spotlight: Eyecatcher when making late gains on debut at Naas over 6f in October; another solid run when a 3.5l third on heavy at the Curragh (6f, heavy) eight days later; 2.25l behind Signora when third at Cork on seasonal return; place claims.

runners.owner: P R Dowling & Ms G Brennan
runners.comment: Not likely to make an immediate impact on paper
runners.spotlight: Second foal; dam unplaced 6f-1m (RPR 42), half-sister to winners Dark Regard (6f inc 2yo), Pride Of Nepal (1m1f-1m4f) and Michonne (French 1m3f/2m), out of German 6f Listed winner; unlikely to make immediate impact.

runners.comment: Just 2.75l behind Ridersinthesky on debut last season; didn't build on that subsequently
runners.spotlight: Finished just 2.75l behind Ridersinthesky when fifth at the Curragh on debut last season (7f, good to yielding); didn't kick on from there in two subsequent starts, including when 13.5l behind at Dundalk when last seen in February.

runners.comment: Took ninth on second start at Leopardstown when 125-1; improvement required
runners.spotlight: Last of 16 on debut at Cork but showed good improvement to finish ninth of 15 in a strong maiden at Leopardstown (1m, good to yeilding) 13 days ago; vast improvement required all the same.

runners.comment: Weakened into a 12.5l eighth at Leopardstown; others appeal more
runners.spotlight: Weakened into a 12.5l eighth at Leopardstown on debut (1m, yielding to soft); others appeal more.

runners.comment: No Nay Never filly cost 125,000euros as a yearling; sister to The Irish Rover (RPR 109)
runners.spotlight: No Nay Never filly; 125,000euros yearling; eighth foal; sister to winners The Irish Rover (Group-placed 6f 2yo; RPR 109) and Just For One Day (6f; 70), closely related to 7f-8.6f winner West Palm Beach (inc 2yo/AW/US; 92), half-sister to two winners; dam placed 6f-1m (81); check market.

runners.breeder: His Highness The Aga Khan's Studs S C
runners.owner: Exors Of The Late H H Aga Khan
runners.comment: Well beaten behind impressive winner on seasonal return; could feature with improvement
runners.spotlight: Looked in need of further when 9l behind on Gowran debut (7f, good to yielding) last September; appreciated extra trip when 5l fifth of 16 over 1m at Cork (yielding); well beaten behind impressive winner back at Gowran on seasonal return (1m, soft); could be in the mix with improvement but drop to this trip may not be the answer.

runners.comment: Third in opening three runs inc' in a Gr. 3; sixth on final run last season; player
runners.spotlight: Third at the Curragh on debut (7f, good to yielding) and again at Cork (7f, good); again made the frame in a Curragh Group 3 in August (1m, good); below her best on final start at Cork when sixth; player.

runners.owner: Michael Tabor & Derrick Smith & Mrs John Magnier

stable_tour.quote: We were very happy with her at Naas. It was her first run against some more experienced fillies, but she acquitted herself very well and Wayne [Lordan] liked her. She's done well since and goes to the Albany.  13-06-25

runners.comment: Vast improvement over debut when third at Naas at 125-1 but others preferred
runners.spotlight: Vastly improved over her moderate debut when outrunning 125-1 odds to take third at Naas (6f, yielding); others preferred.

racecards.verdict: Although expensive to follow, SIGNORA may finally be able to make the breakthrough, having finished runner-up twice this season
racecards.betting_forecast: 5/2 Signora, 100/30 Ridersinthesky, 9/2 Rayzera, 11/2 Expert Dancer, 12/1 Green Interlude, 14/1 White Lily, 20/1 Billy Jean, 22/1 Carmel Valley, 25/1 Divine Legend,  Moon Aura, 33/1 Lamberella, 80/1 Curious Jane,  Glasarmi, 150/1 Ballerina Dancer

racecards.race_name: Irish Stallion Farms EBF (C & G) Maiden

runners.comment: Failed to beat a rival when 80-1 for Gowran debut, may need more time
runners.spotlight: Failed to beat a rival home on debut at Gowran when an 80-1 shot; needs more time.

runners.comment: Well beaten on testing ground on debut, bred to do better, could improve, can't discount
runners.spotlight: One of three for yard; sent off at 12-1 on debut at the Curragh (7f, sft-hvy) last October and was beaten 14.5l; bred to do better and could improve for a sounder surface so can't discount.

runners.comment: 11-2 but no show on debut at Gowran, yard has better chance with The Publican's Son
runners.spotlight: One of three for yard; 11-2 but never landed a blow on debut at Gowran (9.5f, soft); the drop back in trip here should suit but yard has stronger chance with The Publican's Son.

runners.comment: Dark Angel gelding, half-brother to Listed winner, worth a market check on debut
runners.spotlight: Dark Angel gelding; 65,000gns 2yo; closely related to Italian 7f/7.5f 2yo winner Bridge Dress Me, half-brother to winners The Wizard Of Eye (6f-1m inc 2yo/AW Listed; RPR 112) and Arran (5f 2yo; 87); dam maiden (56); a bit of appeal on paper and worth a market check on debut.

runners.comment: 100-1 and never figured on debut at Dundalk, seems safe to put a line through
runners.spotlight: 100-1 and no impact on debut at Dundalk in December; seems safe to put a line through.

runners.breeder: Ross Moorhead & Lope De Vega Syndicate

runners.comment: Galileo Gold gelding, dam related to US Grade 2 winner, best watched on debut
runners.spotlight: Galileo Gold gelding; unraced dam closely related to US 1m Grade 2 winner Ryehill Dreamer, out of 1m winning half-sister to French 2,000 Guineas winner No Pass No Sale; yard not known for Flat maiden winners; watch.

runners.comment: Havana Grey gelding, dam placed at 7f, market best guide on debut
runners.spotlight: Havana Grey gelding; E36,000 2yo; dam placed 7f 2yo (RPR 65), half-sister to French 1m7f Listed winner Only A Pleasure, out of US 1m 2yo Grade 1 winning half-sister to French 1,000 Guineas winner Valentine Waltz; market best guide on debut.

runners.comment: 22-1 and never better than midfield on debut, drops in trip, best watched
runners.spotlight: 22-1 and never better than midfield on debut over 1m2f at Leopardstown 10 days ago; best watched dropped back in trip.

runners.comment: Clearly highly thought of as yet to run outside of Group company; bred to get a mile
runners.spotlight: Belied 40-1 odds with strong-finishing second in Curragh Group 3 (6f, good to yielding) where he was the sole newcomer in the field; inexperience costly when in rear in the Middle Park; slowly away when respectable fifth in Leopardstown Group 3 on return 12 days ago; bred to get the mile and could be a class apart.

stable_tour.quote: He ran very well when fifth at Leopardstown when it was hard to make up any ground. He'll probably go to Cork this month and I think he can make it into Group company this season over 7f to a mile. 22-04-26

runners.comment: Third in both starts, hood worn for promising debut returns, looks the main danger
runners.spotlight: Close third on debut at Leopardstown (7f, yld-sft) in a hood last October; beaten 5.5l at the Curragh on seasonal return last month (7f, sft-hvy) minus the hood; the hood returns now and he looks the main threat to The Publican's Son.

racecards.verdict: THE PUBLICAN'S SON sets a pretty high standard here and he's the one to beat if taking his chance with Zenford the main danger
racecards.betting_forecast: 5/6 The Publican's Son, 3/1 Zenford, 15/2 God Of Power, 14/1 Big Cypress,  Dark Leader, 16/1 Casamorati,  Oro Blanco,  Sancerre Rock, 33/1 Shivoo, 66/1 Little Roy, 100/1 Absoluteassignment,  Garryowen Green

runners.comment: Pulled up over hurdles when last seen in Nov' 2024, best watched
runners.spotlight: Profitable gelding was pulled up in a Punchestown maiden hurdle in November 2024 when 200-1 and not seen since; best watched on Flat debut.

runners.comment: Well-bred, promise both starts for Owen Burrows, bought for 60,000gns, check market
runners.spotlight: Shadwell cast off showed definite promise in two AW starts at 1m-1m2f for Owen Burrows last autumn; bought for 60,000gns and dam from a talented family (half-sister to Baaeed and Hukum); worth a market check on turf debut.

runners.comment: Rated 73, hung left on debut for this yard on AW in Feb', cheekpieces on, more needed
runners.spotlight: Rated 73; placed in one of two starts on AW for Ian Williams; hung left when beaten 5.25l on debut for this yard at Dundalk in February; cheekpieces now go on for turf debut; needs more.

runners.comment: No show in two turf maidens last year, new yard now, lacks a run, best watched
runners.spotlight: Showed little at big prices in two turf maidens for John Burke last year; lacks a run and is likely best watched on stable debut.

runners.comment: No impact in two maidens last year, may do better when sent handicapping
runners.spotlight: Soundly beaten in maidens at Naas (1m, yielding) and Dundalk (7f) last year; may do better when sent handicapping.

runners.comment: Runner up behind smart sort on debut, ran on well over 7f latest, big chance up in trip
runners.spotlight: 6l runner up on debut at Dundalk (7f) in January behind a now 100 rated rival; ran on well for a 0.5l second behind a Ballydoyle colt on seasonal return over 7f at the Curragh (RPR 91, 5l clear of third); could go one place better upped in trip if acts on the ground.

runners.comment: Kept on well over 9.5f on Gowran debut, drop in trip not sure to suit but place shout
runners.spotlight: Pleasing debut when a never nearer fourth of 17 on debut at Gowran (9.5, soft); not sure this step back in trip will suit but should be doing his best work at the finish; place shout.

runners.comment: E38,000 New Bay filly, dam 1m2f/1m4f winner, may need further than this in time
runners.spotlight: New Bay filly was a E38,000 yearling; half-sister to 1m4f winner Cycladic (RPR 99); dam 1m2f/1m4f winner (101), half-sister to 1m2f Listed winner Unnefer and Australian 1m2f Group 3 winner Mount Popa; may need further than this in time.

runners.comment: Huge odds and ran accordingly in two 1m maidens last year, seems safe to rule out
runners.spotlight: Massive odds and ran accordingly in two 1m maidens last year; seems safe to rule out.

runners.comment: Promise on debut but hasn't built on it, beaten 5l at Dundalk latest, needs more
runners.spotlight: Promising debut at Gowran last July (1m, good); disappointed next two starts and was beaten 4l on return from a break when fourth at Dundalk last month; needs more back on turf.

runners.comment: Soundly beaten in 1m4f/1m maidens at Dundalk, would be a surprise winner
runners.spotlight: Soundly beaten in 1m4f and 1m maidens at Dundalk in first two starts; would be a surprise winner.

runners.comment: Off since sole run in June 2023, new yard now, best watched
runners.spotlight: Sole start in June 2023 for Johnny Murtagh wasn't devoid of promise but off the track since; best watched on first run for new yard.

runners.comment: 0-13, rated 77, good handicap run at Leopardstown latest, cheekpieces on, big player
runners.spotlight: 0-13 and rated 77; ground versatile and smart juvenile form included a 4l third on debut at the Curragh behind Lake Victoria and Red Letter; good run from wide draw in 7f Leopardstown handicap latest, staying on well; cheekpieces added to tongue tie; big player.

runners.comment: Modest effort on debut at Naas in March 2025, off since, watch unless market speaks
runners.spotlight: Modest effort when midfield on debut at Naas in March 2025 (1m, sft-hvy); not seen since and likely best watched unless the market suggests otherwise.

runners.comment: Knocking on the door in maidens at 7f-1m2f last season, obvious chance if fit on return
runners.spotlight: Rated 76; knocking on the door in maidens last season at 7f-1m2f on good and yielding ground; obvious chance in this company if ready to rock for her seasonal return.

runners.comment: Tailed off on debut at Gowran 16 days ago, may need more time; reserve
runners.spotlight: First reserve; tailed off when 28-1 on debut at Gowran 16 days ago; may need more time.

runners.owner: Mrs Suzanne McAuley & Ms C A Jennings
runners.comment: Hurdles winner, 0-7 on turf on the Flat, needs to leave last run well behind; reserve
runners.spotlight: Second reserve; dual-purpose; hurdles winner is 0-7 on turf on the Flat but has run well in defeat at times; well below best on seasonal return at the Curragh last month though and needs to leave that well behind.

quotes.race: 50,000 Euro BetVictor Graduation Bonus Series 3-Y-O Hurdle
quotes.quote: Coul Dreamer jumped beautifully there and was in a lovely rhythm. I thought he did that well. I said to Ricky to let him enjoy himself today and, if he makes ground at a hurdle, don't pull him back. He winged everything. We'll maybe aim at the graded race in Fairyhouse, we think a lot of him - Willie McCreery, trainer.

racecards.verdict: SPACEBOUND (nap) has the strongest form on offer and while the ground is a query, this trip looks sure to suit
racecards.betting_forecast: 5/2 Spacebound, 9/2 Sron Na Caise, 5/1 Senna's Girl, 13/2 Treasure Rose, 7/1 Mystic Bella, 8/1 Tyraxes, 9/1 El Rehaiby, 10/1 Je Suis Celebre, 14/1 Torcalot, 22/1 Enchanted Lady, 28/1 Queen Lioness, 66/1 Lauderdale King, 80/1 Ballysax Stew, 125/1 Phidias Ovation, 150/1 Friars Gate, 200/1 Poet's Willow

runners.owner: W Keeling & M C Grassick & Mrs M J Grassick

prev_owners.owner: Mrs M J Grassick/T Oliver Hudson/M C Grassick/W Keeling
Patrick Pearse & W Keeling & M C Grassick & Mrs M J Grassick
Patrick Pearse & M C Grassick & Mrs M J Grassick

runners.comment: Seven-time winner wasn't disgraced on seasonal return; could improve
runners.spotlight: Seven-time winner wasn't disgraced on seasonal return at the Curragh six days ago (7f, soft) when 3.5l behind the winner; could improve for that first run back; not discounted.

quotes.race: O'Reilly Consulting Group Supporting The IRFU Charitable Trust Apprentice Handicap
quotes.quote: Loingseoir was 5lb higher than when winning this race last year. He loves that ground and coming home from off a strong pace. The handicapper hasn't been kind to him all year. He ran well at Galway but then got 3lb and it took a long time for him to get down to where he's competitive. He's a grand horse to have in the yard. I'm sure there'll be another race for him back here, he likes the Curragh - Michael Grassick, trainer

quotes.race: Fermoy Handicap
quotes.quote: He jumped a little slowly but I let him get into his rhythm. He quickened up well in the straight and won well at the line. He was good and tough. He stuck his head out and he galloped right to the line. He loved the ground - Mikey Sheehy, rider of Loingseoir

runners.comment: Three wins on AW over winter; 0-10 on this surface and 9lb lower on it; not ruled out
runners.spotlight: Flying on the AW over the winter, winning over 1m in October and twice in January; winless from ten on turf, although ran okay at times; rated 9lb lower on this surface; not ruled out.

runners.comment: Led before fading into fourth of 8 on h'cap debut ten days ago; likely capable of more
runners.spotlight: Best effort from five maidens came at Galway in July when a 6l fifth of 14 (7f, yielding); led before fading into fourth of 8 on handicap debut at Leopardstown ten days ago (1m1f, yielding to soft); likely capable of better; cheekpieces applied now.

prev_owners.owner: Mrs Magette Meagher & Thomas P Meagher

runners.comment: Successful twice last autumn; capable of more than she has shown in two outings this term
runners.spotlight: AW maiden winner was successful on turf twice last autumn at Cork (1m, yielding) and Roscommon (7.5f, soft); ran some solid runs in defeat afterwards; capable of more than what she has shown in two runs this season.

quotes.race: Irish Stallion Farms EBF (Fillies) Maiden
quotes.quote: La Tulipe Noire jumped okay, there wasn't much pace on and I was able to dictate. The blinkers helped her. She was tough and always doing enough, Declan McDonogh, rider.

runners.comment: Gowran winner last time but form doesn't look great; mark still okay if improving
runners.spotlight: Had been on a losing run of over 2.5 years before a short head victory at Gowran last time provided her fourth career turf win (1m, soft); runner-up hasn't done much for the form in the meantime; still on an attractive mark compared to her previous wins if continuing on an upward curve.

quotes.race: Societies Welcome At Gowran Park Handicap
quotes.quote: We're delighted to get Lady Arwen's head back in front, coming back into the grass it's a great way to start. We gave her a couple of runs in Dundalk and I don't think she's in love with it. She's always been happier on the grass with a bit of cut in the ground. It's fantastic for her to win again and I think after a couple of runs she'll get a little bit further as well - Charlie O'Dwyer, trainer's son.

quotes.race: Golf At Gowran Park Handicap
quotes.quote: Lady Arwen was unlucky not to win in Sligo and I knew the trip in Sligo was a little short for her, but I knew she'd come up the hill well. Once we got a mark of 70 I said I'd take advantage of it. I always thought she'd win a maiden, but it's a great result. I think she's a filly who could develop into a nice Lincoln filly for next year, she'll stay a mile - James Barrett, trainer.

runners.comment: Off the mark at Dundalk in Nov' 2024; finished last in both starts last season
runners.spotlight: Off the mark when winning a 1m handicap at Dundalk in November 2024; ran just twice last season, finishing last on both occasions; makes stable debut now in a first-time hood.

quotes.race: Irishinjuredjockeys.com Handicap
quotes.quote: Mags is a big, raw filly and we need to let her mature a bit more. I'm glad we can close off the year for her and job done with a winner. It is nice to see a horse that is going forward at the line - Kieran Cotter, trainer

runners.comment: Added second AW win last month off 3lb lower at Dundalk; could go well
runners.spotlight: Added a second AW win at Dundalk last month (1m) off 3lb lower; ran some decent races in defeat on turf in 2024; hurdling wasn't her bag; could go well.

runners.comment: Just fair form in h'caps but mark is dropping; fifth of 13 when last seen on turf
runners.spotlight: Just fair form in handicaps to date but her mark is beginning to drop and she is lightly raced; finished a 5.5l fifth of 13 at Down Royal when last seen on turf (7f, yielding); got upset in stalls and weakened quickly into tenth at Dundalk in November (10.5f).

runners.comment: Hasn't built on minor promise shown on debut; last of 12 on return earlier this month
runners.spotlight: Promise on Curragh debut when beaten 5.5l (7f, good) but hasn't been able to build on that initial effort; finished last of 12 on return at Leopardstown 10 days ago (7f, yielding to soft); others more appealing.

runners.comment: Won three on the bounce last term after addition of headgear and blinkers go back on now
runners.spotlight: In the form of his life last June, notching three wins on the trot at 1m/1m1f following addition of visor/blinkers; final leg of the trio came over this C&D off 54 (good); well beaten in two starts this season but interestingly the blinkers go back on now.

quotes.race: Greenmount Suite @ Limerick Handicap
quotes.quote: That is brilliant as I didn't know if Deuteronomy could do the three-in-a-row. Sometimes little horses like that just get their confidence and he has had his palate operated on, so it all helps. Nicola (Burns) knows the horse best so I left instructions up to her. A big thanks to Tony McLoughlin, his owner, who is a tremendous help and I wouldn't be here without him - Robbie Burns, trainer

quotes.race: KCLR 96FM Apprentice Handicap (Div I)
quotes.quote: Deuteronomy was a little unlucky at Leopardstown as he got his gap and then it closed again. I thought if there was a little horse who deserved a win, it was him. I thought a mile on the drying ground would be on the sharp side but Shane Foley told me one day to put some headgear on him to help him concentrate so thanks to him as the visor helped - Robbie Burns, trainer.

runners.comment: Some decent efforts in defeat at Dundalk; makes turf debut and trip should suit
runners.spotlight: Some decent efforts in defeat in Dundalk maidens over 7f-1m; respectable handicap debut (7f) in February when fourth of 13; makes turf debut now and this trip should suit.

runners.comment: Three-time winner was below par last year; attractive mark if returning to form
runners.spotlight: Three-time winner was below par in six runs last year; now 17lb below last winning mark but must return to form.

quotes.race: Tote, Never Beaten By SP Rated Race
quotes.quote: Linger For Longer can buck out in front but Dylan was happy to let the other two go on. Six or seven is her trip and easier ground. I had notions of taking her out because of the ground - Austin Leahy, trainer.

runners.comment: Consistent in defeat on turf last season; good attitude to finish fifth on seasonal return
runners.spotlight: Consistent form in defeat in seven turf runs as a juvenile over 6f-7.5f; way below her best on AW debut at Dundalk in October; demonstrated a good attitude to take a 7.5l fifth on seasonal return at Bellewstown (1m, soft); dropped 1lb and could improve.

runners.breeder: E A R L Ecurie De Chanlecy & Guy Pariente Holding Sprl
runners.comment: Moderate maiden form; may do better now entering handicaps
runners.spotlight: Moderate maiden form; may do better now entering handicaps.

racecards.verdict: A tricky race but it's interesting that blinkers go back on \bDEUTERONOMY after he won three on the bounce in headgear last term
racecards.betting_forecast: 9/2 Lady Arwen, 7/1 Bella Colombia, 15/2 Burford Beauty,  Electric Night, 9/1 Glamazon, 10/1 Medieval Night,  Deuteronomy, 11/1 Loingseoir,  La Tulipe Noire, 12/1 Teffian Warrior,  Nicky Larson, 14/1 Moyassr, 16/1 Linger For Longer, 33/1 Mags,  Cannonball Queen

runners.comment: Won twice in Britain; badly hampered when tailed off on stable debut; form on good ground
runners.spotlight: Won twice for James Ferguson last year, including once on turf at Nottingham (8.5f, good) off 9lb lower and filled the runner-up spot the next twice; picked up for 10,000gns in October but was tailed off on stable debut at Bellewstown when badly hampered; all form has come on good or better.

runners.comment: M'den winner didn't look like gaining a h'cap win in two runs after; mark on high side
runners.spotlight: Killarney maiden winner (1m, yielding to soft) in July last year; didn't look like gaining a handicap win in two subsequent runs; may need some help from the handicapper.

runners.comment: Won off 66 last summer; creditable return to turf last time when fourth; in the mix
runners.spotlight: Enjoyed a good spell on turf last summer, winning at Leopardstown in June off 66 (1m, good); moderate Dundalk run in March but creditable return to turf at Leopardstown when fourth of 17 (1m, good to yielding); in the mix.

runners.comment: M'den has run okay for former yards; moderate stable debut at Gowran last time
runners.spotlight: Maiden has run well in defeat several times for former yards up to 1m; moderate stable debut at Gowran (1m, soft) when 12l behind the winner; others preferred.

runners.comment: Couldn't repeat form of m'den debut when just denied; could go well on seasonal return
runners.spotlight: Just denied in a Galway maiden on debut last August over extended 1m trip (good to yielding); hasn't reproduced that form since, including in two handicap starts on heavy ground; could go well on seasonal return with the ground drying.

runners.comment: Back-to-back wins in 2024; two recent Curragh runs don't suggest he will add to his tally
runners.spotlight: Won two on the bounce for Owen Burrows in Britain in 2024; two Curragh runs this term don't suggest he's on the verge of adding to his tally.

runners.comment: Claims if repeating his penultimate Killarney m'den run when runner-up
runners.spotlight: Best maiden run came at Killarney on penultimate run last season when a 5.5l runner-up (1m, soft to heavy); way below that at Gowran next time (7f, heavy); claims if repeating his Killarney effort off this mark.

runners.comment: Decent form for Ollie Sangster but poor on final British start and similar on Irish debut
runners.spotlight: Best run for Ollie Sangster was when runner-up in a 1m3f Southwell novice contest in March last year; poor on final British start and got off to a bad start on stable debut at Gowran earlier this month when well beaten; visor goes on.

runners.comment: Recorded tenth win under rules' on AW last month; C&D winner last year off 5lb higher
runners.spotlight: Back to form when recording a tenth win under rules' at Dundalk last month (7f); 6f perhaps a bit sharp back at Dundalk last time and was hampered turning in; she was a C&D winner last June off 5lb higher, so a few things in her favour back on turf.

quotes.race: Ballyduane Stud Fillies Handicap
quotes.quote: Amemri was part of the syndicate but she just wasn't selling for enough so I bought her as a present for my wife. She's been remarkable. We thought she might win a couple but that's five in a row now and six since we bought her, while she won three for the syndicate - David Marnane, trainer.

quotes.race: Rose Hotel Handicap
quotes.quote: Amemri is a good and tough mare. I was happy all the way and I probably got there soon enough turning in, but it worked out grand - Luke McAteer, rider.

runners.comment: Three-time turf winner made a positive return to turf last time; could feature
runners.spotlight: Three-time turf winner who appreciates an ease in the ground; 3lb above his last success in September at Roscommon (7.5f, soft); positive return to turf at Bellewstown (1m, soft) two weeks ago when fourth of 14 following a poor effort at Dundalk prior; no surprise to see him feature.

runners.comment: Has shown modest form in m'dens; may improve now handicapping
runners.spotlight: Towards the rear and well beaten in opening three maidens; gelded since last seen at Galway in October; has shown nothing to date to recommend him but may improve now handicapping.

runners.comment: Filled third spot in final two starts last year; well beaten on seasonal return
runners.spotlight: Filled the third spot in final two starts last year at Killarney (1m3f, soft) and Musselburgh (1m5f, soft); prominent before weakening into a 19.5l tenth of 13 on seasonal return; could improve.

runners.comment: Signed off with a win for former yard on AW last time; check market for stable debut
runners.spotlight: 1-26 after signing off with a win for former yard at Dundalk in January (10.5f); some good placed efforts on turf last season; check market for stable debut.

runners.comment: Received a bump when 11l behind on h'cap debut; down 3lb and could improve
runners.spotlight: Not a threat in three maidens; beaten 11l on handicap debut at Naas when last seen in September (1m, yielding to soft) but did receive a bump at a cruicial stage; down 3lb and could yet improve.

runners.comment: Beat previous few rivals in opening m'dens; sixth of ten at Gowran last time
runners.spotlight: Beat precious few rivals in opening three AW maidens nor on turf debut at Navan last month; sixth of ten at Gowran last time was an improvement (1m, soft); handicap debutant.

runners.comment: Runner-up in final two AW starts last year upped to 7f; not out of it if bringing best
runners.spotlight: Finished runner-up at Dundalk on final two starts last year when upped to 7f; 2lb wrong here but not out of it if bringing his AW form.

racecards.verdict: A speculative choice is SMITHFIELD who couldn't repeat his tight defeat on maiden debut last term but may go best on seasonal return
racecards.betting_forecast: 11/2 Mythical Rock, 6/1 Faoladh, 7/1 Amemri,  Selective Power, 8/1 Monvoe, 9/1 Sayidah New Bay, 10/1 Smithfield, 11/1 Bay Of Dreams, 14/1 Green Kite,  Bear Right, 16/1 Minaun View,  Fits Perfect,  Only One Scobie, 25/1 Red Hugh O'Donnell, 40/1 Green Icon,  Lady Odette

runners.comment: Last year's Irish Lincoln winner, beaten 21l in both starts this season, revival required
runners.spotlight: Last year's Irish Lincolnshire winner has lost way since a Galway premier handicap third last August; beaten 21l in both starts this season and remains 5lb above last winning mark; revival needed.

quotes.race: Nua Healthcare Irish Lincolnshire (Premier Handicap)
quotes.quote: Orandi was always missing the break, but Shane [Foley] rode him twice last year and was confident he would get him out sharp, which he did. Wayne Hassett was due to ride him but there were crossed wires, which was unfortunate for him and fortunate for Shane. I thought claiming 5lb [Hassett's claim] would be a big help, but it worked out well anyway. He's in the race [William Hill Lincoln], but I doubt he'll run. He was ready to peak here. There's always hope, but I'd be well below 50-50 about running at Doncaster - Tony Martin, trainer.

quotes.race: Alan Smurfit Memorial Beresford Stakes (Group 2)
quotes.quote: Crypto Force is a very exciting horse for next year. Colin thinks he will be better on fast ground, he will have no trouble getting 1m2f but on quicker ground he will have just that bit more pace. Ideally it would be just nice to put him away and train him with next year in mind - Michael O'Callaghan, trainer.

quotes.race: Ryans Cleaning Waste And Recycling Irish EBF (C & G) Maiden
quotes.quote: Crypto Force did it very well and he will have learned a lot today, he was quite green when he got there. Colin thinks he's very smart. The plan was to go to the Chesham if he was good enough to win one of these - Michael O'Callaghan, trainer.

prev_owners.owner: Beaumelles Racing, Blu Racing Et Al

runners.comment: French AW winner, potentially well treated on debut for new yard, check market
runners.spotlight: French AW winner; 0-4 on turf but wasn't beaten far behind a 97 rated rival when fourth in a 1m listed heat at Longchamp (soft) last June (RPR 97); could be well treated and market can reveal expectations on debut for new yard.

runners.comment: Tailed off on debut for this yard in the Irish Lincoln, can only be watched after that
runners.spotlight: Five-time winner for Joe Murphy; tailed off on debut for this stable in the Irish Lincolnshire last month; acts on most ground but can only be watched after that latest effort.

runners.comment: Course winner, 7lb penalty for 7f Gowran win three days ago, up in trip, chance if stays
runners.spotlight: Course winner (7f, good) bounced back to form with a 7f win at Gowran (soft) three days ago; carries a 7lb penalty for that and steps up in trip now; chance if she stays (not beaten far sole previous start at 1m).

quotes.race: CBE Concannon Group Handicap
quotes.quote: That was very impressive and maybe the cut in the ground today helped, but also the extra furlong. Rion Rubette had been running over a shorter trip and she was unlucky to meet a good horse the last day. On her Curragh run, I thought she might get through and win but I thought she might only win by half a length or a length - Michael Butler, trainer.

runners.comment: Galway maiden winner, good effort on h'cap debut latest, 1lb lower now, chance
runners.spotlight: Consistent form last season included a Galway maiden win (7f, yielding); sound effort on handicap debut and seasonal return at Naas (7f, soft) last month; sharper for that and place shout at least stepped back up to 1m off 1lb lower.

quotes.race: Caulfield Industrial Irish EBF Maiden
quotes.quote: We've always thought a lot of Collecting Coin and he was shrewdly bought by Patrick [Cooper] from the John Dance dispersal sale last February. He misbehaved at the Curragh and Cork earlier in the year so we gelded him since and he behaved impeccably today. He did what he was supposed to do and is a lovely horse going forward. We'll plot our way through the season as he is ground-versatile - Kate Harrington, trainer's assistant.

stable_tour.quote: He made an excellent start to his racing career at Cork on Saturday. We were very happy with that and he'll come on a ton for it. We'll take him to Leopardstown in about three weeks' time and we think he'll progress through the ranks as the season goes on. 23-04-25

runners.comment: Cork maiden winner on final start for former yard, stable/h'cap debut now, check market
runners.spotlight: Placed over C&D (good) on debut for Gavin Cromwell; won a 1m Cork maiden (soft) on third and final start for that stable last September; opening mark looks fair; market best guide on stable/handicap debut after a break.

quotes.race: William Hill Gold Weekend Starts 8am Friday Maiden
quotes.quote: Hellorhighwater is a fine, big, good-looking, scopey horse and I thought a mile round here with ease in the ground would suit him lovely. We flowed along nicely and he travelled and the best furlong was probably my last furlong. He'd enjoy going an extra two furlongs, he should keep improving and there's a good day in him - Gary Carroll

runners.comment: Promise on stable debut in Irish Lincoln, trip too far latest, down 3lb, could go well
runners.spotlight: French winner on good to soft (1m); shaped promisingly enough on debut for this yard in the Irish Lincolnshire (1m, heavy); 1m2f may have stretched latest; dropped another 3lb, moves back in trip and drying ground in his favour; could go well.

runners.breeder: M Delacher Sanchez & F A McNulty
runners.comment: No win since 2024, out of form last year, hood goes on, stable form a positive
runners.spotlight: Has come up dry since back-to-back wins at the Curragh in 2024; no impact in three runs last season; hood now reached for; sliding mark and stable form the main positives but likely best watched on seasonal reappearance.

quotes.race: Finlay Volvo Handicap
quotes.quote: Follow Me is a fair horse, everything went wrong that could go wrong and he still weaved his way through. Three down I was like 'oh no', it was like watching a horror movie. Billy was so cool on him, he got his spots and got out - Ross O'Sullivan, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: He'll be entered in the Sovereign Path at the Irish Champions Festival next weekend and, hopefully, the ground will be okay for him. We put his below-par effort at Royal Ascot down to the quick ground. He's in great shape and we're dying to get a run into him. 11-09-24

runners.breeder: Robert Ryan, Brendan Quinn & Joan Quinn

quotes.race: QuinnBet Spring Fillies Handicap (Premier Handicap)
quotes.quote: Lady Lilac is improving and with another year under her belt she will be a nice filly - Joseph Murphy, trainer.

runners.comment: All Flat wins over an extended 1m1f, has run well over C&D but may be on tough mark
runners.spotlight: Dual-purpose; 3-22 on turf on the Flat; all three Flat wins have come over an extended 1m1f on good ground; has run well over C&D before and fit from the AW but remains 4lb above last win and beaten off lower AW mark on latest.

quotes.race: Peter Queally Memorial Maiden Hurdle
quotes.quote: Expound has plenty of ability and it's good the way he can mix it between both [codes]. When he won his [Flat] maiden he made the running and Denis [Hogan, trainer] said to keep it simple, he likes to make the running and let the horses try and catch him. He was very good from the front, jumped really well and travelled and when they came to him he picked up and done it nicely in the end - Daniel King, jockey, speaking to RTV.

runners.comment: Sole win in April 2023 but has run well in defeat, strip fitter for latest, place chance
runners.spotlight: Sole success came in a Bellewstown maiden in April 2023; has run well in defeat at times and should strip fitter for her comeback run at Gowran 17-days ago; place chance if steps forward from that.

runners.comment: Two h'cap wins last season, solid fifth at the Curragh latest, may need softer ground
runners.spotlight: Won two handicaps last season; below best on seasonal return in Irish Lincolnshire but much better on latest back at the Curragh (1m, sft-hvy) when a 4l fifth of 21; dropped 1lb for that but may need softer ground than this.

quotes.race: Golf At Gowran Park Handicap
quotes.quote: Highbury See See had a nice run in the Curragh the last day. I think he likes a bit of ease in the ground. Hopefully we have a horse for Galway or something like that. We'll keep tipping away with him and see where we end up. It wasn't the plan to be back so far. He had a good draw and we were going to try and make it but he was slow away and things just went wrong. It worked out in the end anyway - Andrew Slattery, trainer.

runners.comment: Up 21lb for three wins last season, beaten 7.25l when third latest, just 1lb lower now
runners.spotlight: Went up a cumulative 21lb for three handicap wins last season; beaten 7.25l when third of 16 at Gowran on latest and dropped 1lb; has placed C&D form but may need a bit more help from the handicapper.

runners.comment: On long losing run, below best both starts this season, others arrive in better form
runners.spotlight: No win since October 2023; promise on first two starts for this yard last October but two runs this season have not been good (very slowly away latest); others arrive in better form.

quotes.race: KONE Handicap
quotes.quote: San Aer loves that ground. He's a very honest little horse and has won here before. He might go to the Curragh on Sunday - Tom Mullins, trainer

runners.owner: Mark Feighery & Kevin Blake & Paul McKeon
runners.comment: French AW winner, back to form on AW latest, return to 1m a plus, chance off same mark
runners.spotlight: French AW winner; promise on debut for this yard at Leopardstown but blood in both nostrils when a beaten favourite for her next run at Navan; back on track after a break at Dundalk (7f) last month when a 1l third; chance off the same mark if backs that up.

runners.breeder: B Kennedy & Mrs Ann Marie Kennedy
runners.comment: Versatile sort, 10.5f AW win in December, this trip looks too sharp; reserve
runners.spotlight: First reserve; versatile sort has won eight races on the Flat and over hurdles; scored at Dundalk (10.5f) in December off 3lb higher but ordinary effort back on turf at Leopardstown latest; this trip looks too sharp.

quotes.race: Edmondstown Maiden Hurdle
quotes.quote: Walhaan got a no-nonsense ride, Eoin was very good on him. We felt he had improved since Navan and had this race pinpointed. The flat track and nice ground suited him well. He's really starting to get the hang of hurdling now - Ciaran Murphy, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: He won twice in France for Jean-Claude Rouget but has been winless since and has only just joined us after a season with Ian Williams, for whom he finished second twice at Ascot. They were good runs and fingers crossed we can do something with him this year off his mark of 90. From what he has shown me at home he could win off his mark. He may start off this week at Newcastle on Friday and I think as the season progresses he can win a race or two. 28-04-21

runners.comment: Won at Gowran last Oct, beaten 9l back there latest, others better treated; reserve
runners.spotlight: Second reserve; off the mark at Gowran (9.5f, heavy) last September off 10lb lower; not a bad effort back there on latest but was beaten 9l and just 2lb lower now; others look better treated.

quotes.race: Support The Irish Injured Jockeys Fund Apprentice Handicap
quotes.quote: Great Mover tries very hard, this filly. Megan [Telford-Kelly] gave her a great ride the last day in Naas but just didn't get to the Hartys' horse [Areana]. I told her today to jump out and conserve as much as possible. I thought she gave her a lovely ride and she seemed to love the ground. She did it nicely in the end. We'll try and get her out again before the end of the year. She gets through that ground and tries - Willie McCreery, trainer.

runners.comment: 11-time winner, well below best first two runs of this season, needs to revive; reserve
runners.spotlight: A winner of 11 races on turf, the latest at Roscommon (7.5f, soft) last September off this mark; well below best on first two runs of this season and needs to leave those tame efforts behind.

quotes.race: Listowel Arms Hotel Handicap
quotes.quote: Earls is as game as a pebble. When I got him out and rolling in the straight, he really put the head down and hit the line really good. He showed he stayed the mile today too. Hopefully he's not finished, he's only winning by short margins so the handicapper can't kill him - Garry Carroll, jockey.

quotes.race: Mehmas Handicap
quotes.quote: Earls has been in the paddock since he came home, I didn't know what to expect. When I saw he had an entry I thought he was one we could claim and then run again quickly. We'll give him a bit of a break now and get to know him a bit more - Garvan Donnelly, trainer

quotes.race: Tattersalls Ireland Handicap
quotes.quote: He normally likes to make the running but there was loads of pace so he couldn't. He pulled up a bit in front but it was a funny race and he was out on his own. There was a fair wind as well. He's in again on Thursday at Navan so we'll see how he is in the morning. I think he'll handle Dundalk as well - trainer Eddie Lynam.

racecards.verdict: COLLECTING COIN is narrowly preferred after his pleasing comeback run at Naas with the step back up to 1m a plus
racecards.betting_forecast: 11/2 Lady Lilac, 6/1 Hellorhighwater, 13/2 Rion Rubette, 7/1 Collecting Coin, 15/2 Um Wadi, 9/1 Spanish Temptress, 10/1 Expound,  Highbury See See, 11/1 Motu Proprio, 14/1 Fast Tara, 16/1 Crypto Force, 18/1 Orandi, 20/1 Dark Summit, 22/1 Follow Me, 25/1 Grey Leader,  San Aer

racecards.race_name: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Fillies Maiden

runners.comment: Well held in two m'dens to date; a lot of improvement required
