runners.spotlight: 150,000gns yearling has been well held in her two maiden runs to date; a lot of improvement required.

runners.comment: Half-sister to three winners inc' Charlus (RPR 96); trainer also runs Near Perfection
runners.spotlight: Eighth foal; half-sister to winners Charlus (Listed-placed 9.5f/1m2f inc 2yo/AW, RPR 96; 2m hurdle), Kosciuszko (1m-1m2f inc 2yo/Spain; 94) and Aquileo (Australian 1m-11.5f); dam French Group-placed 10.5f winner (102); trainer also runs newcomer Near Perfection.

runners.comment: Well clear of third when runner-up on seasonal return; big player with best form
runners.spotlight: Improved plenty over Cork debut last September (1m, yielding) when taking the third spot at Gowran; good return to action at the Curragh when a 2.75l second (1m2f, soft to heavy) and 18l clear of third; tongue tie goes on and she's a big player with the best form on offer.

runners.owner: Michael Tabor & Derrick Smith & Mrs John Magnier
runners.comment: Half-sister to five winners inc' Anthony Van Dyck; market can split trainers' two
runners.spotlight: Half-sister to five winners inc Anthony Van Dyck (7f-1m4f inc 2yo/Derby; RPR 121), Bounding (NZ/Australian 4.4f-7f inc 2yo/Group 1; 112) and Twinkle (7f 2yo; 88); dam Australian 5.5f 2yo Group 3 winner, sister to 5f Group 2 winner Kuroshio; market can split trainer's two newcomers.

runners.comment: 500,000gns yearling; half-sister to Fast Attack (RPR 104); Chablis Rock also runs for yard
runners.spotlight: 500,000gns Y; sixth foal; half-sister to 7f 2yo winner Fast Attack (inc AW/Group 3; RPR 104); dam 5f/6f winner (inc triple Listed; 109), closely related to 5f 2yo winner Xanthe, out of 5f 2yo Group 2 winner; Chablis Rock looks the pick of the stable's pair.

runners.comment: No sign of winning potential in opening two maidens
runners.spotlight: No sign of winning potential in opening two maidens.

runners.comment: Beaten 17l on AW debut earlier this month; tongue tie needs to spark a big improvement
runners.spotlight: Beaten 17l on debut at Dundalk earlier this month; tongue tie needs to spark a big improvement.

racecards.verdict: Well clear of third when runner-up on seasonal return at the Curragh, CHABLIS ROCK can put her race-fitness to use and get a first win
racecards.betting_forecast: 5/4 Chablis Rock, 4/1 Near Perfection, 11/2 Pleased, 17/2 Aravalli, 9/1 Benaki, 16/1 Nathema, 18/1 Zitkala Sa, 20/1 Sofi's Gift

runners.comment: Dual 1m course winner, sound 1m2f effort at Navan latest, has won at 1m4f, go well
runners.spotlight: Dual-course winner at 1m is capable off this mark and he shaped promisingly at Navan (1m2f, heavy) last month (3l behind Calmint); should go well stepped back up in trip (has won over 1m4f on AW).

quotes.race: William Hill Lengthen Your Odds Handicap
quotes.quote: Church Mountain has taken a while to come around to our way of thinking but we got him started at Leopardstown a couple of weeks ago and ran a lovely race. It gave us confidence to drop him in because he's won his other races for Denis Hogan making it. He looked like he won snug enough at the line so hopefully he'll be able to go to Galway and be competitive - Michael O'Callaghan, trainer, talking to Racing TV.

quotes.race: Limerick Racecourse Handicap
quotes.quote: You'd call stall 18 a bad draw usually, but not with Church Mountain because he doesn't like traffic around him. If he's drawn low and misses the break, it can be hard for him to get going, but Dan is super value for his 7lb claim off those weights. This horse has won twice at Galway and hopefully will go back there. Even though he's a big horse, he seems to like good ground - Denis Hogan, trainer

quotes.race: James P. Cunningham Electrical Handicap
quotes.quote: Church Mountain picked up well and did everything for me today. I'd say he's going to make a lovely dual purpose horse, he won't be a horse until next year - Joey Sheridan, jockey.

quotes.race: Kenny Galway Volvo Handicap
quotes.quote: Church Mountain is one we always liked, but he's a massive horse and still not the finished article. He was green in front but he needed to be there because he is a 1m2f horse. Making the running was the making of him - Denis Hogan, trainer.

quotes.race: Floodlit Fridays At Dundalk Handicap
quotes.quote: Deed Pole has plenty of size and scope so could make a nice summer jumper - Cian Hughes, trainer, speaking on Racing TV.

runners.comment: Staying on third at Dundalk (10.5f) after break, moves up in trip, chance with a repeat
runners.spotlight: Returned from a 136-day break with a staying on third at Dundalk (10.5f); not discounted off the same mark upped in trip if repeating that on return to turf.

runners.comment: Maiden, best effort off 4lb higher at Cork (1m4f) last year, lacks a run but can't dismiss
runners.spotlight: Maiden shaped okay at times last season without really threatening to win; her best run came over this trip at Cork when a 2.75l fourth and she's 4lb lower now; lacks a run but can't dismiss.

runners.comment: Best effort yet on latest at Gowran, step up in trip a plus, player off 1lb higher
runners.spotlight: Best effort yet when a 1.25l second of 14 at Gowran (9.5f, soft) on seasonal return; shaped like this longer trip would suit and is a player off just 1lb higher.

runners.owner: Jacqueline Moloney/J C Fleming/Crampscastle Bloodstock Ltd
runners.comment: Modest form in all four starts so far, major improvement required
runners.spotlight: Modest form so far in three maidens and again on handicap debut on seasonal reappearance at Gowran 16 days ago; major improvement required off just 1lb lower.

runners.comment: Not a bad run over timber when last seen at Cork in Nov', entitled to need this
runners.spotlight: Dual-purpose veteran has won eight races including four on turf on the Flat; not a bad run on final start for Ian O'Connor in a Cork handicap hurdle in November; off since and entitled to need this on first run for Charles Coakley.

quotes.race: Two-Mile Borris Handicap Hurdle
quotes.quote: Ellaat has had too tough runs here in a fortnight so we'll see how he comes out of it, but we'll try and get another run into him before the ground goes - Noel Kelly, trainer.

quotes.race: Leugh Handicap Hurdle
quotes.quote: Ellaat is a game, wee buck. I thought the ground was going to be too soft for him but he got away with it - Noel Kelly, trainer.

quotes.race: Bay Leaf Handicap
quotes.quote: Ellatt normally wings the gates but he walked out of the stalls today and I had stopped watching to be honest. He's a big weak horse and Killian thinks the track didn't suit him. He's improving all the time and we'll probably take our time with him - Denis Hogan, trainer.

runners.comment: No win since May 2024, poor form on AW recently, hard to make a case for
runners.spotlight: No win since May 2024; hasn't looked like ending the drought on the AW on recent starts; hard to fancy.

runners.comment: 0-9 on turf, went close off 6lb higher at Tramore last Aug, drying ground a plus

runners.comment: A cut above these rivals on his Norfolk Stakes defeat of the subsequent Middle Park winner
runners.spotlight: Brother to Bluebeard (Prix Morny and Middle Park); only fourth of seven when 4-6 for his Curragh debut (5f, good) last April; made handsome amends with wins in a C&D maiden (soft), a four-runner Naas conditions event (5f good) and the Norfolk Stakes, at the main expense of Middle Park winner Wise Approach; top-class sprinting prospect, reportedly in good shape.

quotes.race: Norfolk Stakes (Group 2)
quotes.quote: Charles Darwin is a very fast, big, powerful, strong horse. He's big, mature, physical and a very good mind as well so he's very exciting. We were obviously hoping that he would get a lead but he's very quick; we would be happy to get a lead, he never sees the front at home in his work, he's always very happy to sit but he's very strong and very quick. Ryan obviously does his own thing always, the gates open and he decides so he was very happy; he said he powered through the line so couldn't be happier really. Albert Einstein was always something that we've never seen before. This horse is very fast, he's a sprinter; I don't know how far he is going to get, he's very quick. The horse on Tuesday [Gstaad] looked like he'd get seven and that means he could get a mile - Aidan O'Brien, trainer.Very professional horse, super attitude. Charles Darwin jumped very quick, showed good speed, I was just trying to control him the best I could. They came to me about the two and a half and I asked him to go and he picked up well. Very good horse. He's got a good brain, he's obviously a very mature, very strong two-year-old; another No Nay Never like the filly yesterday [True Love]. He's doing everything right, doing everything really lovely, couldn't be happier with him really. He'll get six [furlongs] - Ryan Moore, jockey.

quotes.race: Coolmore Stud The Antarctic Race
quotes.quote: We're very happy with Charles Darwin. He just needed a nice sharp bit before Ascot and it was nice to do it on lovely ground. Ryan was very happy with him, he's still babyish but I suppose he's being doing everything very easily. Obviously when he goes to Ascot, he won't have much time for learning but he was very happy. Hopefully that will have done the job and we'll look after him between now and then. I think the Norfolk is the likely plan but that could change, it depends on what the lads want to do. Albert Einstein might run next weekend and we always thought he could be a Coventry horse and this was a Norfolk horse - Aidan O'Brien, trainer.

quotes.race: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Maiden
quotes.quote: Charles Darwin is a lovely, big, powerful and strong horse and we always thought was an Ascot horse. He was very green at the Curragh and the race was a bit messy, and he did everything right today. He travelled and quickened very well. He's not short of speed, so it will be the Coventry or Norfolk for him at Royal Ascot - Aidan O'Brien, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: He won three times in the first half of last year, including the Norfolk Stakes, but missed the rest of the season. He'll go down the three-year-old sprinting route on the way back to Royal Ascot for the Commonwealth Cup and he could be a very good sprinter. He's just a pure sprinter; big, powerful and strong, a big block of a horse. We're very happy with him. 31-03-26

quotes.race: Queen's Vase (Group 2)
quotes.quote: I knew Carmers would stay and I knew turning in Billy [Lee] looked comfortable and I was happy to see the horse come outside him and just not have him at the front and that he was able to get a breather into him round the bottom. He looked comfortable when the bell rang and I was thinking we had a chance. I think staying is his game and he's a pretty good horse. He's done everything we've asked of him and he will have an entry in the St Leger at Doncaster and we'll see, he's done what we've asked him to do today; he's run three times and won three times and hopefully he'll continue doing it - Paddy Twomey, trainer.Race went to plan all the way, jumped well, had a great position, when Harry came around I just let Carmers go on and was able to just hack away but got him rolling early from five out just to get him going forward; he takes a while to build up a head of steam and I know he'd stay well. I wanted to stretch them so I was always going to try and make it a stamina test and you can see him there pricking his ears going to the line, just doing enough. Staying was always going to be a forte of his. He's so laid back at home, he wouldn't pass out the dog at home, he's just that type of character, he saves plenty. I knew when I got stuck into him he'd keep finding away - Billy Lee, jockey.

quotes.race: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Yeats Stakes (Listed Race)
quotes.quote: He's a horse who des just what he has to do, hence the headgear. I thought Carmers would be in the first three at Ballinrobe but he surprised me how well he won at the line. He came home, licked the pot, rode out this week and didn't care so we decided to come here and see what happens. We knew he'd stay but we didn't want to make it, he's a horse who probably doesn't want to be in front too long. To be fair he kept on well, he's keeping plenty to himself. The Queen's Vase is probably the race for him - Paddy Twomey, trainer, speaking to Racing TV

stable_tour.quote: He's unbeaten and has done nothing wrong. I liked what I saw from him at Navan last time and the Queen's Vase has always been the plan for him. I think the race will really suit him. 13-06-25

runners.owner: Michael Tabor & Derrick Smith & Mrs John Magnier
runners.comment: Goodwood Cup winner, confirmed progression with St Leger triumph, Gold Cup candidate
runners.spotlight: Won four of his five races at three, the exception when a close-up fifth behind Carmers in the 1m6f Queen's Vase; improved with cheekpieces, winning a five-runner 1m5f Group 3 at Newmarket by almost 9l and mastering older stablemate Illinois in the Goodwood Cup (2m, good); dug deep to hold off Rahieb on soft ground in the St Leger (Carmers fifth); top-class stayer.

quotes.race: Betfred St Leger Stakes (Group 1) (No Geldings)
quotes.quote: I'm delighted, Scandinavia is hardy and Tom gave him a great ride. He stays very well obviously, but we were a little bit worried when the ground went on the slow side. The better the ground, the better you'll see him. He has a beautiful temperament and he stays, but he'll probably have no problem coming back to a mile and a half as he has loads of gears. Every week he's getting better. He's in the Melbourne Cup and he has to get scanned to see whether he's eligible to go or not, but there's every chance the lads might want to go down there with him - Aidan O'Brien, trainer.

quotes.race: Al Shaqab Goodwood Cup Stakes (Group 1)
quotes.quote: We're delighted. This was Illinois's race, all was planned out, but when Ryan [Moore] said at Newmarket that Scandinavia felt very classy, it was the right thing to do to let them come and run the two of them together and see. Scandinavia looks a very classy stayer, he travelled very well through the race and Wayne [Lordan] gave him a beautiful ride. He was always a very smart horse. The lads actually backed him for the Derby very early in his career, he was considered a very good horse. He won his maiden over a mile and a quarter and Wayne was delighted with him at Ascot next time - he got trapped six wide but he still didn't lie down the whole way and came back at the line to try and win. He's a great stayer with a great mind, he's uncomplicated, and like we saw today he handled the ease in the ground well. You couldn't be more delighted with him really. You would imagine he looks a ready-made Leger horse. Lambourn didn't go to the King George, he is looking at the Voltigeur, and after that an Arc or the British or Irish Leger after that. Scandinavia doesn't have to run again before the Leger if he's going there, so all the options are there - Aidan O'Brien, trainer.Scandinavia has improved all year. He was stepping up to two miles today against the older horses. It's a tough task but I thought he stepped forward quite well. He was hanging onto a little bit even when he got there so I think there's plenty of improvement to come. Today was going to find out how smart he is and he's obviously a very smart stayer - Wayne Lordan, jockey.

quotes.race: Bahrain Trophy Stakes (Group 3)
quotes.quote: I think the St Leger in England, or Ireland, would be targets and then hopefully Scandinavia can develop into a cup horse for next year. We can plot our way to those nice staying races for the rest of the year. We'll see how the horses perform over the festivals at Goodwood and York. He seems to have improved again since Ascot. Hopefully now we can have some fun with him over these longer distances - Paul Smith, co-owner.Scandinavia has been improving with every race and ran well at Ascot. He got into a lovely rhythm today and stayed on really well. I never rode him in a race before although I have rode him at home, so I wouldn't know about the [first-time] cheekpieces. He was impressive today - Ryan Moore, jockey.

stable_tour.quote: He won two Group 1 races last season, the Goodwood Cup followed by the St Leger. He'll be going down the staying route again. He's a big, long-striding horse and we're very happy with everything he's doing. He'll more than likely go for the Vintage Crop and the Saval Beg. 31-03-26

runners.breeder: Al Shira'Aa Farms S A R L
runners.comment: Beat Dallas Star in a 1m6f Curragh event last August, tailed off in the Irish St Leger
runners.spotlight: Stepped outside of handicap company (fourth in Chester Cup and in Ascot Stakes) to win a four-runner St Leger Trial at the Curragh last August, readily brushing aside front-running Dallas Star in the final furlong; faced a very stiff task but ran no sort of race when tailed off in the Irish St Leger.

quotes.race: Comer Group International Irish St. Leger Trial Stakes (Group 3)
quotes.quote: A steady pace, Leinster was a bit in my hands all the way and I would have loved to go a stride quicker. I needed to get him to relax today because he was doing too much the last couple of runs. Coming back in trip and up in grade I thought there would be more of an even gallop on but we did go slow again. I was comfortable at the 2f so I just let him flow, he's a good horse - Dylan Browne McMonagle, jockey, speaking to Racing TV.

quotes.race: Tote.ie Handicap
quotes.quote: Leinster had a real nice run at Roscommon and had a setback so it was unfortunate he missed the rest of the season. Hopefully he can be a progressive stayer. He looked at Roscommon as if the trip was a bit short for him so we were looking forward to stepping him up and I don't think stamina will be any issue to him going forward. The form of the Roscommon race was strong and he handles soft ground well - Joseph O'Brien, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: He's training nicely at the moment and could start off at Navan. He ran well in the Chester Cup last year and is entered again but probably has plenty of weight. He seems to be well suited by the Curragh so could run in a Listed race there on Guineas weekend. We'll see how his first run goes and then decide. 22-04-26

runners.breeder: E Dieuaide & Domaine Billard Et Fils

quotes.race: P.W. McGrath Memorial Ballysax Stakes (Group 3)
quotes.quote: Dallas Star will be entered in all the big races now I suppose and we'll see where we go. I'll have to chat to Kia [Joorabchian, owner] and Robson [Aguiar] and see where they want to go. He came to us over the winter and is a lovely horse - Adrian Murray, trainer.

quotes.race: British EBF Future Stayers' Novice Stakes (Sire And Dam Restricted Race) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Dallas Star is s a lovely horse and has always been a big, raw type. His first run was good at Haydock and then we pitched him in deep in the Chesham, and he ran well, but I stress he's big and raw and has taken time. Rossa says he'll be nicer again next year when he'll want further. I remember saying to someone at Haydock he could be an Ebor horse one day and I haven't changed my mind - he'll be a nice, staying type. This ground isn't essential, but he enjoys it - Dominic Ffrench Davis, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: We've always thought he's a stayer, so we're going to have a crack at the Queen Alexandra. He's never run beyond two miles but I think he should get the trip. 13-06-25

He's been running really well. He came to us with a big reputation from Robson Aguiar, who pretrains all the Amo horses, and he thought a lot of him. He has proved to be a nice horse and I remember saying after his first run that he might be an Ebor horse one day and I still think he will be. I think he'll be a lovely staying type of horse, it's just a case of keeping him on the right side of the handicapper and bringing him along nice and slowly. He's had a bit of a break but you can expect to see him out before the end of the year and we'd like to find him a race he could win rather than pitching him in too deep. 21-09-23

runners.comment: Good form last season on home soil and in France, well below his best on reappearance
runners.spotlight: Consistent last season apart from a poor run in the Hampton Court Stakes at Royal Ascot. went close in a 1m2f Group 3 at the Curragh in May; Listed winner at Gowran (1m4f, good) in July before runner-up in Group 2 and Group 3 (both over 1m7f on very soft ground) in France; failed to show his best form when fourth behind Layfayette on reappearance at the Curragh.

quotes.race: Qatar Prix Chaudenay (Group 2) (3yo) (Grande Course) (Turf)
quotes.quote: Emit ran a smashing race, too. It was great to see him run so well - Kevin Blake, trainer's representative.

quotes.race: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Marble City Stakes (Listed Race)
quotes.quote: He was game and tough. Emit was unlucky in the Curragh in that group race where he came out the worst of it and Ascot didn't really go to plan. We decided to come here up in distance and he seemed to really enjoy it. He fought really well. Dylan (Browne McMonagle) said he'd even go a 1m6f. I suppose he's into group races now - Joseph O'Brien, trainer

quotes.race: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Maiden
quotes.quote: Emit is a grand horse. He didn't get the message to go past but when he did he was snug at the line. He's a lovely staying colt - Declan McDonogh, rider.

stable_tour.quote: He finished off last year well and he'll probably go down the staying route. It was a nice run when he was fourth on his comeback and I expect him to step forward nicely from that. We're looking at going to Navan or Chester next. 22-04-26

runners.comment: Retains considerable ability and enthusiasm judged on Curragh win on first 1m6f attempt
runners.spotlight: Winner of ten races; last of six stakes race wins was in 2023 Royal Whip over 1m2f at the Curragh; however, he proved that he retains considerable ability and enthusiasm when winning a conditions event over this trip at the Curragh on seasonal debut;  (Dallas Star third, Emit fourth), that was his first 1m6f attempt, on his 47th outing.

quotes.race: Fitzdares Royal Whip Stakes (Group 3)
quotes.quote: I'm delighted for Layfayette and I'm delighted to see Helvic Dream come back to a bit of form as well. I was disappointed the last day at Naas but he had a bit of time off after getting some treatment on his back and he got stuffy and blew up. Colin looked to be travelling well and I thought he was going to pick them up once he went for him. He loves this place and the long straight. He probably will go for the Leopardstown Paddy Power Stakes over 1m4f if there is an ease in the ground - Noel Meade, trainer.

quotes.race: Tally Ho Stud Irish EBF Martin Molony Stakes (Listed Race)
quotes.quote: Layfayette is an enthusiastic horse and he likes to win. It got a bit tight and there was a loose one but he won very easy - Seamie Heffernan, rider

quotes.race: Coolmore Sottsass Irish EBF Mooresbridge Stakes (Group 2)
quotes.quote: Layfayette nearly got there too soon. He's beaten the same horses again but has beaten them better and I thought he travelled better today - Noel Meade, trainer

quotes.race: Hollywoodbets Alleged Stakes (Group 3)
quotes.quote: The two of them did a little piece of work the other morning, Colin [Keane] rode the other fella and Oisin [Orr] rode Layfayette. He worked so well I said I couldn't not run him. This fella goes on any ground, maybe not heavy but he goes on most ground. He's just getting better and Oisin thinks he'll be better over a bit further - Noel Meade, trainer.

quotes.race: Lenebane Stakes (Listed Race)
quotes.quote: Layfayette didn't let down on quick ground last year but he handled it. They went hard up front and I was able to ride a nice waiting race on him. There might be something for him on Champions Weekend - Chris Hayes, rider.

quotes.race: Paddy Power Irish Lincolnshire (Premier Handicap)
quotes.quote: I put cheekpieces on him and Chris (Hayes) said they made some difference to him. He's quite a nice horse and hopefully he'll be able to build on that. The first day he ran here last year the ground was very quick and it took him a long time to get over it as he was sore after the run. He's not a hurdler, he's not that shape, and he has quite a flicky action. He'll get further - Noel Meade, trainer

quotes.race: Good Luck To Our 20 Lockdown Heroes Handicap
quotes.quote: I didn't think he was going to win at any stage. I don't know whether that was the ground or whether he's gone lazy, but I suppose when he races like that it helps him to see out the trip. He'd been coming home every time and that's the first time we pushed him out to that trip. I'd say he will run on Irish Champions Weekend if he gets in - Noel Meade, trainer

quotes.race: Foran Equine Irish EBF Auction Maiden (Plus 10 Race)
quotes.quote: He got into a lot of trouble the last day at the Curragh and we fancied him today. He jumped very quick at the Curragh and Colin made a decision to take him back, but when he took him back he could never get out after that. He did come home really well - Noel Meade, trainer

stable_tour.quote: The race can obviously be a bit of a lottery but we're hoping to take our chance. He ran well at the Curragh on Guineas weekend when fourth after probably being a bit unfortunate in running. The handicapper put him up 2lb for that and hopefully he'll have a chance of getting in at the weights. 08-06-21

runners.comment: Durable sort, suited by testing conditions, drying ground against him
runners.spotlight: Useful dual-purpose sort, 3-34 on Flat (and second on ten occasions); his only two stakes race wins from 28 attempts have been in the 1m2f Naas event in which he was third of eight last month; suited by testing conditions, drying ground against him.

quotes.race: TOTE Irish EBF Devoy Stakes (Listed Race)
quotes.quote: Sunchart has never run a bad race at this track so it's a pity there's not more races like this here and he loves an ease in the ground. It's great to have a servant like him. It took him a long time to win a race and he's now won two Listed races one year after the other. We might go travelling this year, somewhere like Germany where he'll get soft ground over a mile and a quarter or mile and a half. We're going to have to as he's an eight-year-old now. He could go back over hurdles and the ground suits him over hurdles as it's watered - Andy Slattery, trainer.

quotes.race: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Devoy Stakes (Listed Race)
quotes.quote: Sunchart deserved that more than any of us. Pat has kept persevering with him. He is a hard horse to place but he likes this track and likes soft ground. It was a good opportunity, he had the highest rating - Andy Slattery, trainer.

quotes.race: Athassel House Stud Irish EBF Maiden (Plus 10 Race)
quotes.quote: Ben said he improved from Listowel and he'll improve again as he was green enough. He was green enough in the parade ring today as well and I think we'll give him another run in the Eyrefield Stakes. He has a fancy entry in the Epsom Derby next year and we think a good bit of him. He'll be a better three-year-old and I just think he'll need another run. The Eyrefield will give him a bit more education and I think he'll need it - Andy Slattery, trainer

racecards.verdict: Goodwood Cup winner SCANDINAVIA confirmed his high-class staying credentials in the St Leger and can uphold form with \bCarmers\P

runners.owner: Mrs John Magnier & Michael Tabor & Derrick Smith

runners.spotlight: Wootton Bassett filly out of a Listed winner by Galileo; stepped up from unplaced debut at Leopardstown to win a 1m maiden at Cork last September; stable's two other runners are more appealing.

quotes.race: Irish EBF Fillies Maiden (Smullen Series)
quotes.quote: I always thought I had it covered, just had to get Bloom organised as she's a big filly and very laidback but she knuckled down well. I think her last furlong was her best and she hit the line strong. - Jack Cleary, jockey, speaking to Racing TV

stable_tour.quote: She won a mile maiden at Cork on her second run last year and she'd be one for an Oaks trial. 31-03-26

runners.comment: Won 1m maiden at Dundalk, not guaranteed to stay as far as this on pedigree
runners.spotlight: Invincible Spirit filly created a good impression when beating an 86-rated previous winner in a 1m maiden at Dundalk in December on her only juvenile start; interesting, although not guaranteed to stay as far as this on pedigree.

runners.owner: Mrs M V Magnier & Mrs Paul Shanahan & S E Sangster

prev_owners.owner: Mrs M V Magnier & Mrs Paul Shanahan & S E Sangster

runners.comment: Stayed this trip well when a winning favourite on soft-to-heavy at the Curragh
runners.spotlight: Showed promise when 7l second to an experienced Ballydoyle-trained filly over 1m at Leopardstown on sole start at two; stayed this trip well when a winning favourite on soft-to-heavy at the Curragh on reappearance.

runners.comment: Beat a stablemate at Dundalk, gets this trip, needs to improve, drying ground should help
runners.spotlight: Half-sister by Camelot to 2025 Lingfield Derby Trial winner Puppet Master; won a 7f barrier trial at Leopardstown last August, second to the promising Yellowstone Lake n a 7f maiden at Dundalk in September; batted well to beat a stablemate over a bit further than this at Dundalk; needs to improve, drying ground should help.

runners.owner: Michael Tabor & Derrick Smith & Mrs John Magnier

quotes.race: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Fillies Maiden
quotes.quote: Ice Dancer is a fine, big filly. She might go to the Silken Glider next. Whatever she does at two will be a bonus - Chris Armstrong, trainer's representative.

stable_tour.quote: She has a good pedigree and is exciting. She ran very well in a hot maiden on her reappearance where she was just nabbed by a high-class filly. We're going to step her back into stakes company next, although we have to decide where. 22-04-26

racecards.verdict: Ryan Moore's presence on Ice Dancer is significant, but she appears held by THUNDERING ON, based on a Curragh clash last October
racecards.betting_forecast: 3/1 Ice Dancer, 7/2 Minerva, 4/1 Emmeleia,  Thundering On, 11/2 Chasing Paradise, 13/2 Bloom, 14/1 Camino Vino

racecards.race_name: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Median Auction Maiden (Smullen Series)

runners.comment: Finished with only one behind him in a 16-runner 7f Naas maiden last autumn, 100-1 then
runners.spotlight: Finished with only one behind him in a 16-runner 7f Naas maiden last autumn; 100-1 shot then; has been gelded.

runners.comment: Newcomer is a half-brother to winners in France, Colin Keane rides his 83-rated stablemate
runners.spotlight: Newcomer is a half-brother to winners in France, Colin Keane rides his 83-rated stablemate.

runners.comment: Made an encouraging seasonal debut over 1m at this venue but has a bit to find Huff'N'Puff

runners.owner: David Spratt & Sean Jones & Mrs Lynne Lyons
runners.comment: Third in a Listed race on debut, failed to build on that in two subsequent outings
runners.spotlight: Made a very encouraging debut when third behind the Aidan O'Brien-trained Daytona in 1m Listed event at Naas last July; but below that level in a Leopardstown maiden later that month on softer ground; faded late into fourth in a 1m1f maiden at Tipperary in August; has been gelded.

runners.comment: Noteworthy as a half-brother to the trainer's Chesham Stakes/Meld Stakes winner Snellen
runners.spotlight: Third foal; half-brother to the talented winner Snellen (Chesham Stakes and Group 3 Meld Stakes for this stable); dam 1m2f turf/1m4f AW winner, half-sister to 1m 2yo Group 3 winner Night Lagoon (dam of King George winner Novellist).

runners.comment: Inns Of Court half-brother to winners, including multiple scorers Booyea and I Am Not Here
runners.spotlight: Seventh foal; half-brother by Inns Of Court to winners, including multiple scorers Booyea and I Am Not Here; dam Listed-placed 7f winner.

runners.breeder: Mme Badovin De La Motte Saint- Pierre
runners.comment: Half-brother by Golden Horde to four winners, dam maiden, likely to need experience
runners.spotlight: E38,000 yearling; eighth foal; half-brother to four winners; dam French maiden, out of half-sister to French 2m4f Group 1 winner Karkour.

runners.comment: Chased home possible Irish Derby candidate Shaihaan at the Curragh, sets the standard
runners.spotlight: Gleneagles colt cost 280,000gns as a yearling; unraced at two; chased home possible Irish Derby candidate Shaihaan at the Curragh four weeks ago on debut; form was boosted by his third-placed stablemate Asakir when beating a Joseph O'Brien-trained favourite at Leopardstown.

runners.comment: Fair run on only outing at two but will need to have improved considerably to win this
runners.spotlight: Respectable run at Leopardstown in October on only outing at two; will need to have improved considerably to win this.

runners.owner: Gary Devlin & Kevin Osborne & Richard J Fitzsimons
runners.comment: Respectable debut at a big price in a Gowran race dominated by market leaders, can improve
runners.spotlight: Alkumait half-sister to four winners including Holiday Magic (ten wins, all on AW), Coolnagree (two 7f wins, Group 3-placed); respectable debut when third at a big price in a 1m Gowran maiden dominated by market leaders; can improve.

runners.owner: Mrs H Shanahan & Mrs Jane Shanahan
runners.comment: Fourth foal, half-sister to 6f AW 2yo winner Lady Amanda, dam won twice for Mark Johnston
runners.spotlight: Fourth foal; half-sister to 6f AW 2yo winner Lady Amanda; dam won twice for Mark Johnston.

runners.comment: Showed some ability at Galway last October but not enough to make her a leading fancy
runners.spotlight: Dam has produced seven winners, including Rocques (Group 3) and Mea Domina (Listed); showed some ability at Galway last October, but not enough to make her a leading fancy.

runners.comment: Half-sister to two minor winners, dam a heavily raced AW Listed winner, hooded for debut
runners.spotlight: Fourth foal; half-sister by U S Navy Flag to two minor winners; dam, by Fantastic Light, was a heavily raced AW Listed winner; hooded for debut.

racecards.verdict: The form of the Curragh maiden in which LATIN AMERICA (nap) finished second is persuasive enough to give him the vote over Genchev

runners.comment: Fine run at Gowran on return; creeping up the weights but looks capable of a good run
runners.spotlight: Won a Clonmel handicap over just short of 1m2f last autumn; fine runs in defeat over 1m at Killarney and 1m1.5f at Gowran (return) since; creeping up the weights but looks capable of a good run.

quotes.race: Suir Blueway Handicap
quotes.quote: I knew Justenzia would keep pulling it out. She'd probably make a nice hurdler, too - Joey Sheridan, rider, speaking to Racing TV.

runners.comment: Best run came when in a 1m maiden at this track last September; trip is a query on return
runners.spotlight: Best run came when beaten only 2.25l in a 1m maiden at this track last September; was below that level on testing ground next time; this trip is a query on return.

runners.owner: Eleanora Kennedy & Mrs J S Bolger
runners.comment: Not a bad run over 1m4f in a Curragh handicap on return; can improve from that; considered
runners.spotlight: Decent efforts last year in three maidens up to 1m4f and not a bad run over that trip in a Curragh handicap on return; can improve from that and one to consider.

runners.comment: Solid runs in AW maidens from 1m-1m4f; hood added for handicap debut and can run well
runners.spotlight: Tailed-off in two bumpers but better runs in two AW maidens (1m-1m4f) either side of a poor run on heavy ground; hood added for handicap debut and can run well.

runners.comment: Best turf effort when second in a Leopardstown handicap over this trip last year; a player
runners.spotlight: Three AW wins up to 1m4f and some decent efforts in defeat over the winter season; best turf effort when second in a Leopardstown handicap over this trip last year; a player if repeating that.

quotes.race: Floodlit Fridays At Dundalk Handicap
quotes.quote: Pepper Noir enjoyed going the trip, she travelled better and actually picked up well. I think we will be sticking to this trip and hopefully there is more to come - Gary Carroll, rider.

runners.breeder: H H The Aga Khan's Studs Sc
runners.comment: Hurdle winner is a maiden on the Flat but some fine runs; needs a return to form
runners.spotlight: Hurdle winner is a maiden on the Flat but has posted some fine runs; however, has been poor in both codes last two starts so needs a return to form.

runners.comment: Won a 7f Laytown maiden last year but stays this trip; looks vulnerable off this mark
runners.spotlight: Won a 7f Laytown maiden last year but stays this trip too; poor at Dundalk last winter and brought down halfway at Bellewstown on return; looks vulnerable off this mark.

runners.comment: Bumper winner went close on the Flat over 2m at Tramore last year; this trip looks short
runners.spotlight: Bumper winner went closest on the Flat in his four starts over 2m at Tramore last year; this trip looks on the short side on return.

runners.breeder: S C P Ecurie Du Sud & S A S Ecurie Gribmont
runners.comment: Best run when 2nd in a Naas handicap over this trip last year; has to return to that form
runners.spotlight: Best run when second in a Naas handicap over this trip last year; has been poor on softer ground the last twice but can do better today if returning to best form.

runners.comment: Won Curragh h'cap over 1m last year and some decent runs since; new trip on return
runners.spotlight: Won a Curragh handicap over 1m last year and some decent runs since between 7f and that trip; up in trip on return and has to prove she stays.

quotes.race: Robbie Dolan Melbourne Cup Winner Handicap
quotes.quote: She's been a frustrating sort as Tofino has been too keen and missing the break. She travelled really well and, when you let her down, all she does is gallop. The stiff track here suited her. She's always promised a bit more than she has showed, so after getting her head in front hopefully she can improve - Gary Carroll, jockey.

runners.owner: Mrs S Bury & Ralph Kelly & Odhran O'Neill & Thomas Cox
runners.comment: Maiden after 22 runs but placed several times; should be thereabouts
runners.spotlight: Maiden after 22 runs but has been placed several times up to 1m4f; not a bad effort at Leopardstown over 1m on return and should be thereabouts.

runners.comment: Maiden was beaten a long way over 7f last time but can do better over this trip
runners.spotlight: Maiden was beaten a long way over 7f last time at Leopardstown and while he doesn't hold that much appeal can do better over this trip.

runners.comment: Smart hurdler has run well on the Flat in defeat but is returning off a long absence
runners.spotlight: Smart hurdler has run well on the Flat in defeat but is returning off a long absence and can only be watched.

quotes.race: ITM Stallion Trail Hurdle
quotes.quote: I would say he is more of a Fred Winter type than one for the Triumph Hurdle and I certainly wouldn't fancy taking on Henry's horse [Alpine Tower] again after what happened at Leopardstown. He will be entered in the Grade 1 at Leopardstown next month, but there is also a rated novice hurdle at Naas in February that we might look at - Gavin Cromwell, trainer of Wolf Prince

quotes.race: Alternative Christmas Party Day 11th January 3-Y-O Maiden Hurdle
quotes.quote: He was entitled to do that. We might look at Leopardstown for him next - Gavin Cromwell, trainer

stable_tour.quote: He'll be entered in the Grade B handicap hurdle at Fairyhouse next week but I don't think he's that well handicapped. We might try to find some conditions hurdles for him. 19-11-21

runners.comment: Won a 1m3f Down Royal h'cap last autumn but was poor on AW after (had excuse); needs best
runners.spotlight: Won a 1m3f Down Royal handicap last autumn but was poor on AW after (found to have mucus in his lungs); needs best on return but can't be ruled out.

runners.comment: Some good runs in defeat including on return at Bellewstown; needs more; visor on
runners.spotlight: Has posted some good runs in defeat since tackling handicaps including on return at Bellewstown over nearly 1m4f; needs more and is unproven in this ground but a player if adapting; visor replaces cheekpieces.

runners.comment: Not bad runs last two maidens last year up to 1m; has to be ready after long absence
runners.spotlight: Not bad runs last two maiden starts of 2025 over 7f and 1m, the latter at this track; has to be ready after a long absence; the market can help.

runners.comment: Won three h'caps at Galway in 2024 but no win last year; fit from hurdling; run well
runners.spotlight: Won three handicaps at Galway in 2024; no win last year but some solid efforts up to 1m4f; is fit from hurdling over the winter and can run well.

runners.comment: Won a 1m4f h'cap at Galway last year; well beaten on Curragh return so needs much more
runners.spotlight: Won a 1m4f handicap at Galway last year on soft ground but has form on good too; was well beaten on her Curragh return so needs much more.

runners.comment: Dual-purpose maiden seems best watched back in this sphere after a layoff
runners.spotlight: Dual-purpose maiden was pulled-up over hurdles when last seen; seems best watched back in this sphere after a layoff; new yard.

runners.comment: Poor in two runs on softer ground recently and not easy to fancy on that form
runners.spotlight: Maiden has been poor in two runs on softer ground recently and is not easy to fancy on that form.

runners.comment: Won Gowran and Naas h'caps last year over similar trips to this; vulnerable off this mark
runners.spotlight: Won Gowran and Naas handicaps last year over similar trips to this; not as good last two runs last term and looks vulnerable off this mark.

quotes.race: Sonix Entertainment Handicap
quotes.quote: Casheldale Lass is a bit hot. The last day, we had a hood on to try and settle her as she was keen the first day but she nearly settled too much, I think. We stuck the cheekpieces on today. She always showed a good bit working. Paul O'Brien has done a lot of jumping with her recently and it seems to have settled her. We were scratching our heads after the last day so we just changed tactics all together and said we'd go forward here. I was a little worried about the ground. I thought she was a nice filly and did good work as a two-year-old. We actually fancied her first time out even though the family take time. She'll be a dual-purpose filly. She's a real game filly and she finally showed today what we thought of her at home - Andrew Kinirons, trainer.

runners.breeder: A C Coombs & Mr J William Rowley
runners.comment: Won well over C&D last October but not as good off higher marks after; needs more
runners.spotlight: Won well over C&D last October but wasn't as good off higher marks after and needs more on return down 2lb; eyecatching jockey booking, though.

quotes.race: AOS Security Handicap
quotes.quote: Forlio has done some amount of work but I did think he would need the run. Colin said he didn't really love the ground as it was sticky for him so normal soft would be better for him - Paul Flynn, trainer.

runners.comment: Not much racing in last two years; dropping in the weights but best watched
runners.spotlight: Hasn't had much racing in the last two years; is dropping in the weights but still best watched.

runners.comment: Won a Punchestown h'cap last year; solid Leop'town return; considered; reserve
runners.spotlight: First reserve; won a Punchestown handicap last year over 1m1f; some decent hurdle runs over the winter and a solid Leopardstown return over 1m; considered.

runners.comment: Some fine runs in defeat incl' on return at Curragh (1m); one to consider; reserve
runners.spotlight: Second reserve; maiden has posted some fine runs in defeat including on return at Curragh (1m); stays 1m4f so can do better over this trip; one to consider.

runners.comment: Not bad maiden runs in UK; poor on heavy ground debut for this yard; do better; reserve
runners.spotlight: Third reserve; not bad maiden runs in UK; poor on heavy ground debut for this yard behind a stablemate; can do better now handicapping.

quotes.race: Aidan Moffitt Memorial Handicap Hurdle

quotes.race: European Breeders Fund EBF Peter Willett Future Stayers' Maiden Stakes (Sire/Dam Restricted) (GBB)
quotes.quote: High Honour is a nice staying horse who was green last time but has come on from that - William Buick, rider.

runners.comment: Ran poorly over 1m2f on heavy ground on her only handicap start, premature to write off
runners.spotlight: Half-sister to the talented Thunder Kiss; third in two of her four starts in maidens; ran poorly over 1m2f on heavy ground at Leopardstown on her only handicap start; premature to write off.

runners.comment: Ended last term with a 1m6f Curragh victory over Quiz Test, 9lb higher, same apprentice
runners.spotlight: Two wins last season, both gained at the main expense of members of this field; edged out God The Highness at Sligo; ended the campaign with a 1m6f Curragh victory over Quiz Test; 9lb higher now, same apprentice claiming 7lb.

runners.breeder: His Highness The Aga Khan's Studs S C
runners.comment: Versatile mare has won on turf/AW and over hurdles, ground should be coming right for her
runners.spotlight: Versatile mare has won on turf/AW and over hurdles; ground should be coming right for her; lacks the advantage of a recent outing.

quotes.race: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Mares Maiden Hurdle
quotes.quote: Early in the race, it didn't look as though Daboya would be involved. Danny [Mullins] said she made a few mistakes and didn't really travel, but then she switched on and showed some of her class from the Flat. We had planned to give her a break but Danny is anxious to keep going. Now that she has won really well, you'd have the mares' novice hurdle at Cheltenham in the back of your mind. She is a nice prospect - Richard Donohoe, trainer.After a few slow jumps early, a bit of class brought Daboya into it, all in all a very good performance. She's a one for those nice mares' handicaps over the winter - Danny Mullins, jockey, speaking to Racing TV

quotes.race: Book Online At dundalkstadium.com Maiden
quotes.quote: DABOYA floated on the surface. This was her last run for us. She's in the sales and has a nice pedigree, so this was important - Chris Hayes, rider

runners.comment: Only Flat win came in 2023, fit from hurdling but hard to fancy on recent evidence
runners.spotlight: Only Flat win came in 2023; fit from hurdling but hard to fancy on recent evidence.

quotes.race: Adare Manor Opportunity Maiden Hurdle
quotes.quote: Granville Street was a bit novicey as he was entitled to be but he jumped well and I like this horse. He has more in him - Eoin Walsh, jockey.

runners.comment: Five wins in Britain, has not shown a great deal in seven AW starts for this stable
runners.spotlight: Five wins for the Johnston yard, but has not shown a great deal in seven AW starts for this stable; down the field at Lingfield early this month.

runners.spotlight: Out of form since a Limerick win last June; towards the rear on both turf starts this term.

quotes.race: Racing Again On 12th July Handicap
quotes.quote: They went a bit too slow for God Of Thunder early and I was always bringing him back but I got a lovely run down the outside coming into the home straight and he did it well. He won a maiden hurdle impressively here and hopefully he can progress on the Flat now - Dylan O'Connor, jockey.

runners.comment: Winning form on Flat and over hurdles last August, should be better for last month's run
runners.spotlight: Won over 1m4f at Roscommon (good) last August and added a Wexford maiden hurdle (good) ten days later; should be better for last month's run when fifth over 1m6f here, 1 3/4l behind the reopposing Earthsong.

runners.comment: Ran poorly on seasonal debut, stable appears to have a better chance with Celtic Druid
runners.spotlight: Hurdles winner on good ground; 0-10 on Flat; ran poorly on seasonal debut at Bellewstown; stable appears to have a better chance with Celtic Druid.

runners.comment: Struggled over hurdles during the winter, not without a chance on last year's Flat form
runners.spotlight: Twice successful in Germany, suited by 1m4f; struggled over hurdles during the winter; not without a chance on last year's best Flat form, namely a third placing over this trip at Down Royal.

runners.breeder: Al Shira'Aa Farms S A R L
runners.comment: Should be better for her seasonal debut here last month, closely matched with Kool One
runners.spotlight: Best effort came on handicap debut over1m6f at this venue on yielding ground last August, staying on from the back for a 2l third of 11; should be better for her seasonal debut here last month; has a slight edge with Kool One.

runners.comment: Disappointed over hurdles for Gordon Elliott after a 2m Flat win at Tramore,  stable debut
runners.spotlight: Three Flat wins, twice in Britain and over 2m at Tramore last April for Gordon Elliott; disappointing over hurdles on last two starts in 2025; makes stable debut.

runners.comment: Second at Clonmel last September has been the only bright spot since a 2024 Chester win
runners.spotlight: Second at Clonmel last September has been the only bright spot since a 2024 Chester win; some merit in his recent Clonmel run.

quotes.race: Donaghmore Handicap
quotes.quote: He has ability and he stays well. He was a bit unlucky in the Ulster Cesarewitch but he has won plenty and is a great sort. He jumps nicely and we will probably go down that road next. Shane Crawley - trainer.

quotes.race: smartvetmeds.com EBF Novice Stakes
quotes.quote: Rich Belief is bred to get the trip and the two runs at sprint distances has helped him gain experience and sharpen him up. The extra furlong has suited him today, he's done it quite nicely, real workmanlike. The pace wasn't very strong, he jumped really well today, he was in the right position turning in and stayed on really strong all the way to the line. He was lugging to his left late on and I had to give him a couple of flicks to straighten him out, but once I did that he went about his business. He's bred to get a bit further and progress with age. He's quite a nice little horse - Robert Winston, jockey.

runners.comment: Placed form in France and at Dundalk, towards the back over 1m2f here last month
runners.spotlight: Dam is an unraced half-sister to Irish Derby winner Westover; placed in two of his three Flat starts in France at three; ran creditably in a Dundalk handicap on only start last year; towards the back over 1m2f here last month.

prev_owners.owner: Tobias Jones, James Finch & Samuel Sutton

runners.comment: Continues to drop in the handicap, recent Gowran run provides limited encouragement
runners.spotlight: Dual-purpose winner has been well beaten last six Flat starts; continues to drop in the handicap; recent Gowran run provides limited encouragement.

runners.comment: Picked up an injury on seasonal debut, also had an excuse at Bellewstown, not ruled out
runners.spotlight: Signed off last season with a promising run behind this year's Irish Lincoln winner Ribee at Gowran (7f, heavy); picked up an injury on seasonal debut; also had an excuse at Bellewstown, hampered under half a mile out; not ruled out.

runners.comment: Decent form without winning last autumn, each-way chance if reappearing in same shape
runners.spotlight: Sole win came at Cork in 2023; decent form in defeat last autumn, including a close third over 1m4f at Galway and second to Trubshaw in a 19-runner contest at the Curragh, with Plunkett Street, Earthsong and Bruant behind; each-way chance if reappearing in similar shape.

runners.comment: Failed to run to market expectations at Gowran on seasonal debut, capable of better
runners.spotlight: Won a 1m4f Cork handicap on return last year and some good runs off higher marks after; won over hurdles in November but disqualified after a positive sample; failed to run to market expectations at Gowran on seasonal debut, capable of better.

runners.comment: Progressive in winning twice at Dundalk, definite chance here with Sadhbh Tormey's claim
runners.spotlight: Progressive in winning back-to-back 1m4f handicaps at Dundalk; appeared to have plenty left in the tank last time; those two runs, if not his pedigree, suggest the extra two furlongs will be within his range; holds a leading chance here with Sadhbh Tormey's claim in play again.

runners.comment: Chance here with fitness advanced by a hurdles run, third of 23 over 1m6f here last autumn
runners.spotlight: Chance here with fitness advanced by a hurdles run at Fairyhouse; went close against Trubshaw in a small-field Sligo event last August; probably a better effort third of 23 over 1m6f here in October.

runners.comment: First reserve, went very close in a similar race here on penultimate Flat start last year
runners.spotlight: First reserve; went very close in a similar race here on his penultimate Flat start last year; went on to win over hurdles before a below-par Bellewstown run; durable sort.

quotes.race: Cusack Hotel Group Family Raceday July 13th Handicap
quotes.quote: Arcland's first run for us over hurdles in Downpatrick was very encouraging. He was off a very low mark there today and it was nice to win with him - Gavin Cromwell, trainer.

quotes.race: Happy Retirement Eamonn Lloyd Apprentice Handicap (Div I)
quotes.quote: He'll go jumping after that and should make a nice hurdle horse as he jumps well - trainer Harry Rogers.

runners.comment: Second reserve, four-time turf winner whose recent Dundalk form has been poor
runners.spotlight: Second reserve; a four-time turf winner whose recent Dundalk form has been poor.

quotes.race: Aspall Suffolk Draught Cyder Handicap
quotes.quote: The only question mark was the ground as Edge Of Darkness won on heavy last time. He's not had much racing and is just finding his feet really - Charlie Johnston, trainer.

runners.comment: Third reserve, both wins in Britain came on AW, drying ground should help for Irish debut
runners.spotlight: Third reserve; both wins in Britain came on AW; drying ground should help for Irish debut.

quotes.race: Free Race Replays On attheraces.com Fillies' Handicap (GBBPPlus Race)
quotes.quote: Timeless Charm is a big filly. She just gallops. When I let her down in the straight she put her head down and tried really hard. She's obviously got a bit of ability and she's got the heart for it too - Oisin Orr, jockey, speaking to Sky Sports Racing.

stable_tour.quote: She was disappointing at Doncaster. I think she wants better ground. She's worked nicely through the spring and I certainly haven't lost hope in her. I can give her another chance. 04-04-24

racecards.verdict: With race-fitness on his side and drying conditions a plus factor, CELTIC DRUID can maintain the progress evident at Dundalk.
